in writing. − international air transport relations between member states and third countries are usually governed by bilateral air service agreements. the eu court of justice ruled in 2002 that nationality clauses in bilateral agreements are contrary to eu law. they allow a third country to refuse, withdraw or suspend the authorisation or privileges of an air carrier which bears the mark of an eu member state but which is not majority owned by that member state or its nationals and is not subject to effective control by that member state or its nationals. this is considered to be discrimination against eu carriers which are established in the territory of a member state but are owned and controlled by nationals of other member states. the commission has therefore negotiated an agreement replacing certain provisions in the existing 19 bilateral air services agreements concluded between eu member states and indonesia. it was signed on 29 june 2011 and both parties to it have agreed to comply with this agreement from the date of its signature until its entry into force. the council must obtain the consent of the european parliament before it can conclude it. i think it is appropriate for the committee on transport and tourism to vote in favour of the conclusion of the agreement.
in writing. − if you have the memorandum of cooperation (moc) aims to formalise and strengthen relations and cooperation between the eu and the international civil aviation organisation (icao). it was signed on 28 april in montreal and on 4 may 2011 in brussels and has been provisionally applied since then. icao was established in 1944 by the chicago convention as a specialised agency of the united nations. its current 190 member states cooperate in the fields of aviation safety, security, air traffic management and environmental protection. the overall objective of the moc is to guarantee greater harmonisation of standards and closer coordination of relevant activities. so far, only aviation safety provisions have been developed. the parties agree to cooperate closely and coordinate their activities in the field of security. the approach is based on a mutual commitment to achieve the highest possible level of aviation safety worldwide and the global harmonisation of safety standards and recommended practices (sarp). the identification of unsafe areas and air carriers is a common core interest and a significant part of the joint activities. i believe that parliament should be involved in strengthening the eu's position within icao and it is therefore appropriate that the committee on transport and tourism give its consent to the conclusion of a memorandum of cooperation between the european union and the international civil aviation organisation, thus providing a framework for enhanced cooperation.

in writing. −directive 2002/96/ec on waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee) was adopted on 27 january 2003 and entered into force on 13 february 2003. member states were required to transpose the requirements of the directive by 13 august 2004. since the adoption of the directive, the causes of the problems and the reasons for collecting and recycling weee have not changed. experience with the implementation of the weee directive in the early years has shown technical, legal and administrative problems resulting in unintentionally costly efforts by market players and administrations, continued environmental damage, low levels of innovation in waste collection and treatment, unequal conditions or even distortions of competition and unnecessary administrative burden. the commission is committed to creating a better regulatory environment that is at the same time simple, understandable, effective and legally enforceable. the specific objectives of the review of the weee directive were therefore to: reduce administrative costs while maintaining a level of environmental protection; implement the directive through enhanced compliance and reduced system abuse; limit the environmental impacts of the collection, treatment and recovery of weee to the level where the greatest net benefits to society are achieved. if the necessary measures were not taken, the problems and irregularities in the matter would continue. for that reason, the directive was amended accordingly.

in writing. − biocidal products are designed to kill, repel and destroy harmful organisms. many of them can be harmful to humans or animals. each country therefore monitors their use very closely, making sure that they are used only when absolutely necessary and that they do not endanger people. a regulation on biocidal products, which harmonises the rules on the market for such products, is necessary for two reasons. in particular, it gives citizens of the european union the assurance that each manufacturer must meet the same strict conditions for his product to appear on the market. manufacturers must therefore maintain the same standards in protecting human health and the environment. however, this uniform approach is also beneficial for producers. it reduces their costs for certifying their products and allows them to supply their products to any eu country without having to go through the difficult authorisation procedures many times over. this creates scope for innovation in biocidal products and improves their availability. the competitive environment is improving and this has a positive effect on prices. in addition, the centralised authorisation system also contributes, inter alia, to better consumer protection.

in writing. − space activities and applications are crucial to the growth and development of our society. they often have a direct impact on the daily lives of citizens. in this context, space policy constitutes an instrument for the union's internal and external policies. space is a space for knowledge, for new products and for new forms of industrial cooperation. it is therefore a driver of innovation, contributing to competitiveness, growth and job creation. the sector directly contributes to the europe 2020 strategy objectives of ensuring smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. space policy thus constitutes an integral part of the industrial policy flagship initiative. the european parliament has always advocated an ambitious european space policy, setting itself objectives such as promoting technological and scientific progress, innovation and competitiveness, or seeking to enable european citizens to benefit from space applications, and thus to give europe a greater say on the international space scene.

in writing. − food waste has become such a global problem that it is present at all stages of the agri-food chain. it occurs in agriculture, manufacturing, distribution companies, or consumer households. food is wasted in both developed and developing countries. food waste forms a parallel chain with the production chain and leads to a number of negative externalities. the issue of food waste is at odds with the fundamental issue of food security, which is seriously threatened by a range of factors, including limited natural resources in relation to the growing world population and insufficient access to food for the poorest population groups. the fight against food waste must become a priority in the european political agenda. the commission, the council and the member states should endeavour to adopt strategies and concrete measures aimed at reducing food waste throughout the supply chain, while at the same time making efforts to raise awareness of the problem among the general public with a view to seeking a remedy. it is necessary that citizens are informed not only about the causes and consequences of waste but also about the ways to reduce it. in this context, the call for 2013 to be declared the european year against food waste appears to be an important tool to raise awareness and to raise awareness of this important issue.
in writing. − food waste is now so widespread that it must be considered a global problem. we can say that from the producer to the consumer, the entire food chain is present. it is estimated that more than half of all wholesome and edible food is thrown away. the issue of food waste is at odds with the fundamental problem of food supply, as the world's population grows, and with it the limited access to food for the poorest. not to mention the high environmental costs of producing food that is not consumed. the causes of waste, however, are not always the same. while in industrialized countries the focus is on marketing and consumption, primarily because of the abundance of food produced, in developing countries the lack of advanced agricultural techniques and safe storage facilities is the cause. these data clearly show that the amount of food produced today should be reused for food purposes rather than simply thrown away like other waste. the fight against food waste must be a priority on the european political agenda. we need to develop a concrete strategy to halve food waste across the entire food supply chain by 2025. i believe it is extremely important to educate citizens not only about the causes and consequences of waste but also about ways to reduce it. i voted in favour of the report.

energy poverty is a serious problem in developing countries. worldwide, nearly 1.3 billion people are regularly deprived of electricity for their daily activities. i think that this problem has not been given enough priority in development. access to modern energy services is a prerequisite for eradicating poverty. but few developing countries have made progress in improving access to energy. households typically spend a large proportion of their income on poor-quality lighting and heating materials. this is because those without access to fuels and electricity do not benefit from aid. we already have a number of technologies to bring clean and efficient energy to poor communities. in addition to fossil fuels, technologies that use local energy sources can also provide a solution. we need to promote the creation of a global financial fund to support investments to reduce poverty. we must do everything we can, both politically and financially, to achieve universal access to energy by 2030.
access to modern energy services is a prerequisite for poverty reduction and sustainable development. without access to energy, entire communities are forced to live in poverty and in undignified conditions. over the past period, there has been a significant effort to promote private investment in energy access. but apart from countries with transforming economies, very few developing countries can demonstrate progress in increasing energy access for the poor. financial assistance for access to energy for this population has been limited so far and therefore there is a need to increase private sector involvement. as for the future, the european union energy facility is the only fund in the world specifically designed to support investment to tackle energy poverty. however, there are currently no commitments for the european union energy facility for the future. i therefore believe that, in particular by increasing political will and financial commitments, the union can play a decisive key role in achieving universal access to energy by 2030.

in writing. − the growing political and economic importance of brazil, russia, india, china and south africa (the brics group) is increasing the foreign policy importance of these countries. in terms of the global economy, the economies of the seven fast-developing countries (brazil, russia, india, china, indonesia, mexico and turkey) are also expected to be larger than the economies of the g7 (usa, japan, canada, uk, germany, france and italy) combined by 2050. in terms of gross domestic product, china is projected to become the world's largest economy before 2020 and india could become the world's fastest growing economy before 2050. i believe that it is appropriate to try to go beyond mutual trust, recognition and cooperation and to make efforts to create a common platform for foreign policy issues, based on the premise that a new system of global governance will be established that is sufficiently accessible to the brics and other emerging powers and based on common values. the current trade agreements between the eu and the brics countries are not only mutually beneficial from an economic point of view, but also politically beneficial for both parties. it is important to build relations with the brics on bilateral dialogues aimed at promoting further democratisation and strengthening relations with the eu.
in writing. − sanctions or restrictive measures are perceived as coercive measures without the use of force, such as arms embargoes, trade sanctions, economic and financial sanctions, asset freezes, flight bans, entry restrictions, diplomatic sanctions, boycotts of sporting and cultural events and the suspension of cooperation with a third country. however, the application of sanctions and restrictive measures is only effective if it is part of a coherent comprehensive human rights strategy of the eu and the member states. however, the union often applies its sanctions policy unevenly and treats third countries with similar human rights and democracy deficiencies differently, and such behaviour has prompted criticism of the use of the so-called double standard. i therefore believe that it is necessary to establish clear criteria as to when restrictive measures are to be applied, to set out the objectives to be achieved by those restrictive measures, to determine the form of the sanctions to be applied, the guidelines for their periodic evaluation and the review procedure to be followed in consultation with the european parliament. it is desirable to draw up the criteria in a way that enhances the consistency and credibility of eu sanctions, while allowing the union sufficient flexibility at the operational level and thus the effective use of this instrument in its external activities.
in writing. − if you have articles 49 and 54 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union guarantee the right of establishment for all companies. cross-border corporate migration is one of the key elements in completing the internal market. however, it is necessary to take into account the heterogeneity of legislation regarding the relocation and the rules for the relocation of the registered or actual seat of an existing company under national law from one member state to another within the single market, and the associated employment risk, as well as the administrative difficulties, costs incurred, social consequences and lack of legal certainty. business mobility still faces a high administrative burden as well as social and tax costs. the transfer of the registered office should preserve the continuity of the legal personality of the company concerned in order to guarantee its proper functioning. the relocation should not affect the rights of the parties involved and the relocation process should be governed by strict rules on transparency and on informing the parties involved before the relocation takes place. i also believe that it is important to ensure the uniformity of employee participation procedures in the different legislative provisions that are part of the company law directives when a company's registered office is relocated.

in writing. − in the european area of justice, citizens must be able not only to enjoy their rights, but also to enforce them effectively. eu legislation is intended to enable parties in crossborder situations to either enforce their rights effectively or to reach out-of-court settlement of disputes through mediation. the benefits of adr cannot be denied, but equal access to justice should be preserved for all eu citizens. consumers harmed by infringements often face significant barriers to access, effectiveness and affordability in seeking redress, sometimes due to the high costs of litigation, the potential psychological consequences, complex and time-consuming procedures and a lack of information on available means of redress. in some member states, the overall effectiveness of existing consumer redress and enforcement tools developed at eu level is not considered to be satisfactory or these mechanisms are not sufficiently known, which means that they are used to a limited extent. i believe that it is necessary to take account of the legal traditions and legal systems of the various member states and to increase the coordination of good practices between member states. it is necessary to introduce safeguards under the horizontal instrument to prevent unfounded claims and the abuse of collective redress in order to ensure the fairness of judicial proceedings.
in writing. − as with any new legislation at eu level, the interests of the eu citizen, who is in this case primarily the injured party, must be given priority when considering the possibility of collective redress. the justification of a form of redress not fully known to the continental legal culture should be duly substantiated by the commission and other legislators before a proposal is made on the subject. in addition to the uncertainty surrounding the real impact of the new procedural rules, which put the interests of the individual first, it is nevertheless possible to mention the positive aspects that can be achieved by a common procedural rules for a collective remedy. abuses are often committed by companies with large capital and infrastructure, against which individual enforcement may seem hopeless. sometimes the consumer, the customer, is not able to bear all the burdens that are necessary to enforce his rights under the law, and so he does not use them. in such cases, joint action by the injured parties may be justified, in accordance with the rules of the collective redress form and only on the basis of an individual decision on participation. i believe that a future legal instrument in the field of collective redress should also focus on the objective of enabling eu citizens and businesses to enjoy the rights guaranteed to them by the community. this report reflects those views.
in writing. − if you have taking into account the principles governing the selection of authorised nutrition labels for food, the commission proposed a new nutrition label now containing x% less [nutrients] to be included in the annex to regulation (ec) no 1924/2006. such a designation is contrary to the purpose and content of the basic act because it is confusing, ambiguous and misleading to the ordinary consumer. the newly introduced designation 'now contains x % less [nutrients]' infringes the principle of comparative assertions as laid down in article 9 (2) of council regulation (ec) no 1924/2006. it allows the nutritional values to be compared with the previous version of this product, regardless of the fact that the starting level of nutrients could be disproportionately high compared to other products on the market. products which have not been modified but which nevertheless have a lower proportion of certain nutrients than the modified product of another brand will not be eligible for a nutrition declaration. this procedure is bound to mislead the consumer. i consider that the commission's proposal for a regulation is not in line with the purpose and content of the basic instrument and therefore i consider it necessary for the commission to submit an amended proposal.

the creation of an integrated market for electronic payments in euro, without substantial differences between national and cross-border payments, is essential for the proper functioning of the internal market. although this initiative by the commission could have come earlier, we are glad to have it here. the objective of the single euro payments area project is to develop common payment instruments within the european union, which would replace the current national payment instruments. it is sepa that should provide citizens and businesses of the european union with secure, easy-to-use and reliable euro payment services at competitive prices. it is also expected to create room for creating favourable conditions for increased competition in payment services and for the unrestricted development and rapid implementation of payment-related innovation. consequently, savings should increase, mainly due to increased operational efficiency. at the same time, there will be pressure to reduce prices across the board, which should have a significant impact, especially in member states where payments are relatively expensive compared to other countries. the success of sepa is very important from an economic, monetary, but also, of course, from a political point of view. it is fully in line with the europe 2020 strategy aiming at a smarter economy. for this reason, it also appears justified and important to achieve a smooth and rapid transition to sepa. the single payment area is a good example of a common approach within the eu and also benefits our citizens.
the functioning of the european union's internal market without the dismantling of borders in the banking sector would certainly be problematic. therefore, the effort to create a single european transaction execution system by moving from national to international standards is an understandable change that will make it easier for our citizens and businesses to make cross-border payments within the european union. the fact that from 2014 euro area citizens and from november 2016 citizens of other european union countries will be able to execute cross-border payment orders and direct debits in the european union under the same conditions as at national level is, i think, a natural manifestation of integration and the building of a common market, which our citizens and business entities will certainly welcome. i therefore hope that the application of the proposed amendments creating the single european union payments area will no longer encounter administrative or economic obstacles in the banking sector which would further complicate its implementation.

in writing. − the european union's economic prosperity also rests on sustainable creativity and innovation. it is therefore important to make efforts in relation to measures to protect them effectively. intellectual property rights are important business assets that help to ensure that innovators and creators are fairly remunerated for their work and that their investments in research and new ideas are protected. however, despite all efforts, the number of violations of these rights is constantly increasing, posing a threat not only to the union's economy but also to the health and safety of its population. efficient, immediate and coordinated action at european and global level is therefore needed to prevent this phenomenon. one of the main initiatives of the council and the commission back in 2009 was the establishment of a european counterfeiting and piracy centre to respond to the threat. however, i believe it is equally important that the member states also make efforts to increase cooperation between the office and the national intellectual property offices. for the full range of these rights, data and exchange of best practices are needed to obtain a global picture of the situation and to enable the establishment of comprehensive strategies to limit infringements of intellectual property rights. the mandate of the office should be extended to cover the protection of patents, copyright and related rights, as well as geographical indications.
in writing. − the situation in the member states today shows that the priority of governments at national and european level must be to ensure economic growth and the related maintenance of employment. research and innovation have become an area where european countries gain a competitive advantage. inventions and patents are the result of time-consuming and costly research and development and therefore deserve to be properly rewarded and protected in order to truly return on investment and to encourage similar investments in the future. the field of intellectual property is one of the fastest-growing areas, with countless european experts finding their way into it. not only are new jobs created, but europe has become a leading innovation place thanks to new inventions. if we are to maintain this position in the fierce global competition, we must create and protect an environment in which authors, inventors and manufacturers are not afraid to share their creations and knowledge for public use, but produce better products.
in writing. − taking advantage of the opportunities offered by the internal market, businesses are increasingly moving beyond national borders. there is an increasing demand for access to company information in a cross-border context. however, official information on companies from other member states is not always readily available and current voluntary cooperation between registers does not appear to be sufficient. it is therefore the interconnection of central, commercial and companies registers that could and should contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of european enterprises by reducing the administrative burden and increasing legal certainty. at the same time, this would support the overcoming of the crisis, which is one of the priorities of the europe 2020 strategy. cross-border communication between registers should also be improved by taking advantage of innovations in information and communication technologies. however, i am convinced that the shift in cross-border access to business information can only take place if all member states are involved in building the electronic network of registers, which should ensure both expertise and accuracy. i also believe that information should be sent to business users in a standardised format throughout the union.
in writing. − the proposed directive is, in my view, clearly a step in the right direction in the interests of building the internal market in the european union. insufficient interconnection of registers and difficulties in obtaining true information on companies have often caused barriers to cross-border trade. improving the interconnection of registers, involving all member states through standardised sharing of basic information, will, on the contrary, lead to increased legal certainty, trade and, ultimately, economic growth. i am convinced that the interconnection of registers will also contribute to the protection of third parties, to increasing the share of smes in cross-border trade. i therefore see the interconnection of registers as another tool to consolidate the internal market and increase its competitiveness.
in writing. − trade registers are currently maintained exclusively at national and regional level, which creates differences in particular in the reliability and scope of the data recorded, but also in relation to their legal record. the directive aims at a purely technical interconnection of existing national registers and not at harmonisation of their legal implications. such linking is an important measure to promote further integration of the eu economic area and to strengthen legal certainty for citizens and businesses. another positive contribution of this directive will be the opportunity to make use of all available options for keeping electronic registers, resulting in savings of money and time. it should be noted that a number of questions relating in particular to technical details cannot be answered definitively. the networking phase will be necessary to find solutions to the problems that arise. we should leave the decision to the member states, but they must not forget the benefits and savings that such links will bring to them.
in writing. − if you have the negotiations between the european commission and the republic of guinea-bissau have resulted in a new protocol which applies for a period of one year from 16 june 2011, as the previous protocol expired on 15 june 2011. guinea-bissau is a tropical west african state with limited natural resources and an estimated population of 1.6 million. it is one of the least developed and poorest countries in the world. its economy is predominantly agricultural, with a strong dependence on the export of the single crop of cashew nuts. the country is highly dependent on donor support, with the eu being the main donor, providing about one-third of international donor assistance in 2008. potentially advantageous trade in fishery products with the eu is hampered by non-compliance with eu hygiene standards. guinea-bissau has a large number of fish stocks, both coastal and oceanic species. the catch from the small-scale fisheries sector was last estimated at between 30 and 50 000 tonnes per year. the fisheries partnership agreement ensures that eu fleet components have access to fishing opportunities from areas highly dependent on fisheries, promotes their regional presence in west africa, contributes to job creation and additionally supplies the eu market. it is in the interest of both parties to conclude a new protocol and i therefore believe that parliament should give its consent to its conclusion.

in writing. − the eu-morocco joint document on the strengthening of bilateral relations confirms the objectives of the enhanced status granted by the european union in response to morocco's expectations of a strengthened partnership with the eu. these objectives shall focus on better reflecting the strategic priorities of both parties and on the progressive integration of morocco into the internal market. enhanced status shall open the possibility for morocco to participate in the activities of community agencies and community programmes and shall provide it with appropriate financial support. in this context, the eu should ensure in particular that the policies being developed in morocco benefit all regions of the country and in particular the western sahara region, which needs stability and solutions. the kingdom of morocco has become a political and economic partner for us and this protocol represents a significant act of support and encouragement by the eu in relation to the efforts towards sustainable democracy in the region. that is why i believe and hope that morocco will not betray our trust.
in writing. − council directive 2000/75/ec of 20 november 2000 laying down specific provisions for the control and eradication of bluetongue lays down control rules and at the same time measures to combat and eradicate the disease, including rules for the establishment of protection and surveillance zones and the deployment of vaccines. in order to ensure better control of the spread of bluetongue virus and to reduce the burden of that disease on the agricultural sector, it is appropriate to amend the current vaccination rules laid down in directive 2000/75/ec to take account of the latest improvements in vaccine production technology. the amendments provided for in this directive should make the rules on vaccination more flexible and should also take into account the availability of inactivated vaccines which can be successfully deployed outside areas where animal movement restrictions apply. i believe that amendments to the legislation are necessary to take account of technological progress in vaccine development. the proposed amendments would also facilitate the adoption of bluetongue control strategies based on the specific situation in the member states without unnecessary union intervention.
in writing. − if you have the creation of an integrated market for electronic payments in euro without substantial differences between national and cross-border payments is essential for the proper functioning of the internal market. to this end, the single euro payments area (sepa) project aims to develop common union-wide payment instruments to replace the current national payment instruments. it is sepa that should provide union citizens and businesses with secure, easy-to-use and reliable euro payment services at competitive prices. at the same time, there is a presumption that there will be room for creating favourable conditions for increased competition in payment services and for the unrestricted development and rapid implementation of payment-related innovations. it can be expected that there will be an increase in savings as a result, in particular due to the increased operational efficiency. pressures for a general price reduction will be exerted, which should have a significant impact in particular in member states where payments are relatively expensive compared to other countries. the success of sepa is very important from an economic, monetary and political point of view. it is fully in line with the europe 2020 strategy aiming at a smarter economy. it is for this reason that i believe that it is justified and important to make efforts to achieve a smooth and rapid transition to sepa.
in writing. − the proposal to create an internal market for payments without differentiating between internal and external payment systems aims to simplify and reduce fees for payments in european currency throughout the european union. this initiative started as early as 2008, but progress was very slow. on 16 december 2010, the commission therefore published a draft regulation to set deadlines for the prohibition of interchange fees and their transfer to the sepa structure. in addition to simplifying and making payments more accessible to citizens and businesses, the potential benefit to the european economy could be between eur 100 and 300 billion over a six-year period. i think that the transitional periods for replacing the existing national payment systems with a single european system with union-wide schemes, common standards and technical requirements should be as short as possible. in the context of multilateral interchange fees, the commission proposed to keep fees only for r-type transactions, while other transactions should become free of charge. i welcome this proposal because the proposed changes maintain the ambitions set out in the commission proposal while ensuring a high level of consumer protection and safeguarding the national practices in this area.

after several years of the european council blocking the continuation of union food aid to the most deprived, we are finally getting to the point where we can discuss and approve the continuation of this aid in 2012 and 2013. given that this interim programme already takes into account most of the substantial changes proposed by the european parliament, such as the procurement of food in accordance with the rules of competition or the use of food mainly originating in the union, there is no reason to prolong this process by submitting further amendments. it is therefore also necessary to respect the annual ceiling of eur 500 million for the union's assistance and to ensure that food aid is distributed efficiently and meaningfully so that it reaches those who need it most. but we must start working on the mechanisms for continuing this programme beyond 2013 today, commissioner, otherwise we may be left without help in europe after that date.
access to food and adequate nutrition should be fundamental rights for every citizen. the statistics prove otherwise. in 2008, 13 million people in 18 member states benefited from food aid, but by 2010 that figure had risen to 18 million. the economic crisis and the associated decline in employment have brought more poverty for more people who have become dependent on food aid. the programme must therefore remain one of the key options for protecting those who rely on it most in the future. the effectiveness of the programme must be not only in its availability but also in its speed. let us avoid the mistakes we have in the individual member states, for example in my country, slovakia, where redistribution takes a very long time and is accompanied by misunderstandings, which makes the aid provided meaningless. therefore, the chain from production to distribution must be organised as quickly and efficiently as possible.
the milk and milk products sector has recently undergone significant changes, which have been exacerbated by the financial and economic crisis. high input cost prices and the current decline in demand for dairy products have caused a reduction in the incomes of direct producers, but have not been reflected in reduced prices for final consumers. the lack of transparency in the functioning of the consumer chain thus reveals many inconsistencies which may indicate the existence of unfair commercial practices to the detriment of producers but also to the detriment of households at the end of the chain. i therefore believe that the dairy sector should take more account of fundamental market signals, such as in particular supply and demand, in setting prices, and that strengthening competition, clarifying the fundamental rights and obligations of individual actors, improving their awareness and responsibility should also lead to a fairer distribution of the total income within the chain and to an improvement in the adequate standard of living of livestock farmers.
i understand the effort of the highly indebted countries of the union to help themselves by financing their national debt with bonds that would be largely borne by others. however, only national governments are fully responsible for the management of their own economies. i therefore understand the caution of those governments which have no problem so far in borrowing at a reasonable premium on the financial markets, if they do not want to involve their countries in the dubious game of holding their country responsible for the exploitation of others. if the commission and some member states really think that the idea of jointly issuing so-called stabilisation bonds is as beneficial as they claim in the green paper, they could already consider issuing jointly issued bonds for a group of countries which see this as a way out of the crisis. we would all be interested to see what interest there would be in the financial markets in the issue of joint stabilization bonds by a group of southern european countries, for example, portugal, spain and cyprus, and what premium they would trade on the markets. if their surcharge were at the level of germany, i would say that this solution could be beneficial for the european union.
i consider consider considerations of introducing stabilisation bonds to be premature in the context of the unresolved sovereign debt and deficit crisis in many member states of the european union. the issuance of common bonds, which some see as a 'potentially powerful tool to address the limited solvency of some euro area member states', would in my view only divert attention from the acute, unresolved problems of fiscal discipline. the crisis requires the introduction and strict adherence to an appropriate fiscal framework and the simultaneous recovery of economic growth. continuing jointly with public debt would only deepen the current negative situation, although some negative effects would be delayed and masked in the short term, but the core of the problem would remain unchanged. the introduction of co-issued stabilisation bonds would also radically change the structure of the euro area sovereign bond market and introduce new, as yet little-studied risks for member states.
i'm not a financier, i just want to use common sense. let me ask you a question: does anyone else remember the stability bond advocates who caused the mortgage crisis in america? financial institutions created packages for investors with mortgages of varying quality. these collateralised bonds were to share the risk of defaulting on the mortgage. they were created by a political order. the effort to provide every citizen with a home loan, regardless of their financial capabilities. what we now call stability bonds is no different. it's a political effort to make additional loans available to those who can't afford to pay them back. even the strictest rules of financial discipline fail if they are not enforceable. in the case of mortgages, the lender could recover part of the loan by selling the property. for sovereign debt, this option does not exist. i think the risks of eurobonds have not been sufficiently taken into account.
in writing. the green paper on the feasibility of the introduction of stabilisation bonds assesses the feasibility of a joint sovereign bond issue by individual euro area countries and the conditions required. state-owned issuance in the euro area is currently conducted by member states at a decentralised level using different issuance procedures. the introduction of jointly issued stabilisation bonds would mean pooling member states' sovereign issues and merging the related revenue streams and debt service costs. this would significantly change the structure of the euro area sovereign bond market, which accounts for the largest share of the euro area financial market as a whole. as the sovereign debt crisis in the euro area intensified, a broader debate was sparked on the feasibility of a joint issue. a significant number of politicians, market analysts and academics have supported the idea of a common issue and have identified it as a potentially powerful tool to address the limited solvency of several euro area member states. the joint issue of stabilisation bonds would also require a further shift towards a common economic and fiscal policy. the commission should indicate the progress of the consultations on the stability bonds referred to in the green paper or the further steps it intends to take following the public consultations on its green paper. i personally believe that the introduction of the common bonds is one of the key points in the fight against the current crisis. i hope that the council will take a firm stand on this.

in writing. − parliament asked the commission to report on the possibility of introducing european securities, which are an integral part of the agreement between parliament and the council on the package of six legislative proposals on economic governance. the euro area is in a unique situation where euro area member states have a single currency without a common fiscal policy and a single bond market. however, issuing bonds on the basis of joint and several liability would require a process of deeper integration. as the issuer of the world's second largest international currency, the euro area has a shared responsibility for the stability of the international monetary system. it is in its long-term strategic interest to take full advantage of the euro's issuance, which has the potential to become a global reserve currency. the euro area and its member states are responsible for ensuring the long-term stability of a currency used by more than 330 million people, as well as many companies and investors, with implications for the rest of the world. stabilisation bonds would help facilitate the transfer of euro area monetary policy and promote efficiency in the bond market and in the wider euro area financial system. i also believe that the introduction of a sustainable fiscal framework aimed at better economic governance and growth is a necessary condition for the joint issuance of bonds. i also believe that the prospect of stabilisation bonds can strengthen stability in the euro area.
in writing. − the social consequences of the crisis are far-reaching and are currently aggravated by the impact of austerity measures introduced in some countries in response to the sovereign debt crisis, job losses in both the private and public sectors, and cuts in social security benefits and public services. this situation leads to a deepening of poverty across the eu. the labour market situation is particularly critical for young people, regardless of their level of education, partly due to the mismatch between acquired skills and labour market requirements. but, in addition, people approaching retirement age, the long-term unemployed, workers from outside the eu and unskilled workers are also among those hit hardest by the crisis. the crisis has created new categories of people at risk of poverty and, when fiscal consolidation measures are poorly targeted and regressive, social protection systems are negatively affected and the number of people at risk of income poverty, child poverty, severe material deprivation and social exclusion is increasing. for this reason, i believe that the implementation of integrated active inclusion strategies should become a central element of social policy programmes at eu and national level. in view of the worst economic crisis the union has ever experienced, there is an urgent need to put in place national reform programmes.

for the efd group. to begin with, any strengthening of the safety deposit system is good news for our citizens who put their savings into financial institutions. the revision of directive 94/19/ec on deposit-guarantee schemes is also justified today by the fact that there are now several dozen different deposit-guarantee schemes in the union with different obligations for financial institutions and different levels of deposit protection. the same deposit protection rules across the european union for the residual of a depositor's legal right to protection of up to eur 100 000 give the same security to depositors in all countries of the union, thus avoiding unnecessary movements of deposits between countries. however, i find the mechanism of borrowing money between member states' systems problematic, since in certain situations it could also become a mechanism for spilling the crisis from one country to another, and that would certainly not be good.

i'd like to talk about the things that are questionable from my point of view. i would include among these areas the very definition of the so-called reasonable prospect of obtaining a right of permanent residence. this vague definition from the green paper can be dangerous, in particular in that if too much leeway of interpretation is left to member states, the result will be that no third-country national will be able to act as a guarantor for a family member. in some member states, a potential sponsor must have resided in the territory of the state for at least 2 years before applying to take in a family member. the background to these requirements is, in particular, the desire to monitor the behaviour and economic situation of the applicant as a potential guarantor. this is how the politically engineered separation of families in time and space is created. several ngos have pointed out that this is a violation of the right to privacy and family life as provided for in article 8 of the convention. furthermore, it may not be the right to marry and the principle of non-discrimination. for this reason, i am in favour of reducing the length of the procedure and the waiting period. the report on the implementation of the directive and the green paper also highlight problems and shortcomings in the implementation of this directive at national level. they raise concerns regarding the transposition of this directive. they conclude that too much leeway is left to the member states to apply certain of its provisions.

in writing. − no bank, regardless of its financial position, has sufficient liquidity to pay all or a substantial part of its deposits on the spot. the commission notes that the bank's capital needs are not covered by the banking communication. this can have serious repercussions for the whole economy. there are currently around 40 deposit protection schemes in the eu, which protect different groups of depositors and deposits with different levels of cover and impose different financial obligations on banks, limiting the benefits of the internal market for both banks and depositors. in order to facilitate the taking up and pursuit of the business of credit institutions, it is necessary to eliminate differences between the laws of the member states as regards the rules on deposit-guarantee schemes to which those institutions are subject. the directive in question constitutes an essential instrument for the establishment of an internal market in the field of the activities of credit institutions in terms of the freedom of establishment and the freedom to provide financial services, while enhancing the stability of the banking system and the protection of depositors. it should create a level playing field for credit institutions, allow depositors to easily understand the characteristics of deposit protection schemes and facilitate the rapid payout of depositors by sound and trustworthy deposit protection schemes in the interests of financial stability. for this reason, it is necessary to harmonise and simplify the protection of deposits as far as possible.

in writing. − in the light of the implementation plan adopted at the 2002 un world summit on sustainable development in johannesburg, the european community commits itself, inter alia, to maintain or restore fish stocks at levels capable of producing the maximum sustainable yield, with a view to achieving these objectives rapidly in the event of stock depletion and, if possible, by 2015 at the latest. the western stock is the economically most important stock of norway lobster in union waters. biological information on these stocks is not sufficient for an overall assessment of these stocks which would allow for the setting of a fishing mortality target related to the maximum sustainable yield and which could base the total allowable catch on scientific forecasts in this area. preventive scientific advice suggested that the annual catches of western hake should be kept below 150 000 tonnes for several years from 2003, provided that this would make the exploitation of stocks sustainable, even if there is no exceptionally high replenishment of stocks in the future. the areas for which annual total catch limits for blue whiting are established do not correspond to the stock limits for this fish in the atlantic ocean. it is necessary to ensure that the catch rules provide for a precautionary approach to the management of those stocks.
in writing. − fishing is one of the oldest human activities and fish are an important and indispensable part of the human diet. therefore, efforts related to the protection and maintenance of fish stocks are necessary. the role of fisheries as a food provider for human society has been long recognised and widely recognised. the fisheries sector, including wild fish and aquaculture, is an activity that contributes to the production of irreplaceable common goods through the three main components fishing, processing and marketing. the fisheries sector provides high-quality food for europe's population and creates economic and social added value for the european union. it is therefore necessary that the reformed common fisheries policy ensures the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources and the protection and maintenance of fish stocks at healthy levels, in such a way that fishing activities can continue within their traditional areas and communities in the long term. the fisheries sector is one of the most important pillars of food security for the european union and its sustainability and stability must therefore be ensured through the reform of the common fisheries policy so that in the future the sector can supply fishery products of sufficient quality and quantity to meet the demand of more than half a billion european citizens.

in writing. − the association agreement between the european union and morocco entered into force in 2000. in december 2010, the council of the european union signed a document which, after ratification by the european parliament, would allow the second phase of the liberalisation of trade in agricultural and fishery products between the european union and the kingdom of morocco to start. as regards agriculture and fisheries, the new agreement gives mutual preference to the strengthening of large-scale industrial farming at the expense of family and small-scale farming. increasing reduced-rate quotas for a wide range of fruit and vegetables will put european producers in a difficult competitive position and will not even strengthen the balanced development of agriculture in morocco. we must not forget the eu's commitments in the wake of the arab spring to help the countries of the southern mediterranean transition to democracy through trade and economic instruments to ensure greater freedom and greater economic opportunities. in this context, the agreement in question appears to be a positive step towards promoting political stabilisation and mutually sustainable economic development. it is the liberalisation of trade between the eu and morocco that can lead to mutual benefits, increased economic growth, prosperity, job creation and poverty eradication.

in writing. − access to books and other printed material for blind and visually impaired people is severely limited in the european union, as 95% of all books published are never converted into 'accessible formats' such as braille, large print or audio. it is regrettable that there is currently no international legal standard for a targeted exception to copyright rules for the cross-border distribution of formats adapted to persons with reading disabilities worldwide. for this reason, the copyright committee of the world intellectual property organization (wipo) is considering the development of an international treaty aimed at improving access to books for blind and other visually impaired persons. in its report of 13 april 2011 on unlocking the potential of the cultural and creative industries, the european parliament called on the eu to support a binding wipo treaty and calls on the council and the commission to support a binding wipo treaty with regard to copyright in books and printed matter for the blind and visually impaired. it is necessary and important to advocate for this treaty, as the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities itself, in particular articles 21 and 30, and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union lay down principles relating to the prohibition of discrimination against persons with disabilities.

in writing. − the global monitoring for environment and security (gmes) programme is one of the two major eu space initiatives and plays a key role in earth observation, which is a vital tool for combating climate change and environmental degradation, civil protection and security, sustainable development, mobility and crisis management, as well as securing important economic opportunities. gmes is of great political, strategic and technical importance to europe and offers very high value for money in terms of economic, social and technological benefits. the absence of a sound financing plan to ensure long-term and stable financial support would likely lead in the long term to higher costs, to differences in access to the output information and to different benefits for european citizens, to the suspension or even interruption of the programme and the provision of its information, and could ultimately mean that the investments made so far would become redundant and that europe would lose its independence and technological edge in this important space infrastructure. any uncertainties regarding the future of the gmes programme and its funding would significantly hamper the development and marketing of gmes services and applications, which are expected to bring economic growth and prosperity to european citizens.

for the efd group. i have studied with interest the proposal for a regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions and authentic instruments in matters of succession and on the introduction of the european certificate of succession, submitted by the european commission. i understand that the increasing migration of union citizens may cause certain problems for survivors of a deceased person who has settled in another country. however, it seems unfortunate to me to link the determination of jurisdiction and the applicable law in succession proceedings to a kind of habitual residence of the testator or the deceased, which, as a key concept, is not properly defined or clearly defined in the regulation. such a broad and loosely worded concept can be interpreted differently by the courts in different countries and i therefore believe that it is necessary to choose more precise and better formulated definitions for such a sensitive regulation in the future.
i think we should agree with the basic decisions of the commission's proposal. the proposal will of course not affect existing laws in the member states, but will allow for the first time a new crossborder succession regime. this is of course an important step towards strengthening the internal market and i regret that some member states are still holding back progress on this issue. the proposal provides us with legal certainty, is relatively clear and simple and, in the most important issues it addresses, is understandable to the ordinary citizen. it prohibits the division of inheritance. since the starting point would be the place of habitual residence, the competent court could, as a rule, apply its own legislation. the new right to choose the legal order will strengthen the independence of citizens. its limitation to nationality this restriction preserves the function of the law of succession in the area of public policy and the protection of family members. circumvention and abuse of systems would be largely avoided where possible. a regulation cannot, of course, solve all the problems and adjust all the details, but it will significantly improve the current legal situation. citizens will have a clear and secure basis for the transmission of their legacy. they could exercise their rights more effectively in the internal market. legal clarity and certainty are central legal values in the field of succession law. a regulation would strengthen these legal values, bring benefits to the citizen and create significant european added value.
every citizen of the union has the right to enforce his rights in succession and to dispose of his property on his death. these rights are confirmed by the order of succession. in cross-border succession cases, heirs often encounter administrative and enforcement difficulties. the regulation will provide citizens with clear rules and legal instruments that will apply equally in all member states. the introduction of the european certificate of succession will make it possible to prove the status of heir more easily. the document will contain the same information in all official languages and in all the participating member states on the heir and his rights, and will facilitate the work of the authorities and the quick and cost-effective completion of the probate procedure. the issuing of official documents for procedures, such as extracts from the register, in minority languages should also be done in the future in a way that guarantees equal rights for all eu citizens. finally, we say goodbye to our colleague lechner, thank him and wish him all the best in life.

in europe, there are 160 000 cooperatives, employing some 5.4 million workers. the financial crisis has shown that it cannot be solved only unilaterally from the point of view of the shareholders of these companies, but also the responsibility that the company has as a social organisation should be considered. indeed, the undertaking is not only liable to its shareholders, but also to its employees, creditors and society. legislation on cooperatives and employee participation is fundamentally different across the european union. the statutes of the european cooperative are so far the only legal form of the social economy at european level. cooperatives and other social economy enterprises are part of the european social model and the single market and deserve decisive recognition and support, as laid down in the various key european union documents. the revision of the directive should address in particular the specific needs of employees of cooperatives, including the possibility of being both an owner and an employee of the same undertaking. i believe that it would be appropriate for the commission to create an instrument to facilitate the ownership of cooperatives by employees and users. employee participation in enterprises should be a matter of course in all countries of the european union and, likewise, employee participation in cross-border forms of enterprises should be strengthened and not kept at the lowest level.

in writing. − in december 2002, the council authorised the council presidency, with the assistance of the european commission, to open negotiations with norway and iceland on an agreement on mutual legal assistance. now, in line with the new legal framework resulting from the lisbon treaty, the european parliament's consent is required. the agreement itself aims to improve judicial cooperation between eu member states and norway and iceland by applying almost all the provisions contained in the 2000 convention on mutual legal assistance between member states and its protocol adopted in 2001. it includes, inter alia, provisions on the examination of witnesses, experts and accused persons by telephone or videoconference, on controlled deliveries, on secret investigations and joint investigation teams, and on requests for information on and monitoring of bank transactions, bank accounts, in order to combat crime in general and organised crime in particular. norway and iceland extend the rules on mutual legal assistance already in force and mostly applied in the member states. i am convinced that the agreement will help in the fight against crossborder crime and will strengthen cooperation with two countries that already belong to the schengen area, and with one of which, iceland, is currently in eu accession negotiations. i agree with parliament's approval of the agreement.

the growing epidemic of diabetes is a serious problem for civilised society and the increase in its incidence in the union cannot really be ignored. more than 90% of the diseases are type 2 diabetes, where the loss of glucose utilization is caused by poor diet and lack of physical activity. the disease, which until recently was predominantly found in adults, is now spreading rapidly in the child population. as there is no cure for diabetes and the disease is increasingly taking its toll on the lives of patients, our actions must be geared towards effective prevention by changing harmful eating habits and increasing physical activity in the population. for example, by charging a special price for the consumption of products that are harmful to health, as in the case of tobacco or liqueur, we could contribute to a greater orientation of consumers towards healthy, natural food products. the funds raised could then be used to stimulate the community to participate regularly in light fitness sports. there are certainly more opportunities to create positive changes in current habits, but the commission must be able to work creatively with them and then put them into practice effectively.
diabetes is increasingly common in the member states of the european union, affecting the lives of some 32 million citizens, representing almost 10% of the european population. diabetes is also the cause of up to 325 000 deaths within the eu. type 2 diabetes results in a reduction in life expectancy of 5 to 10 years, and type 1 diabetes results in a reduction of life expectancy of up to about 20 years. by 2025, the number of people with diabetes will increase by about 16 percent. the average cost of treatment for each eu citizen with diabetes is between 10% and 18.5% of the total health expenditure in the country. and we also need coordination at european level, although healthcare is certainly a matter of national sovereignty and each country should have its own action plan. we should therefore also support the fight against obesity and promote healthy lifestyles.
