the european union's sensitive and constructive policy in the balkans is also bearing fruit in bosnia and herzegovina. the accession of croatia to the european union and the opening of accession negotiations with serbia are certainly stimulating political conditions in that country. the european union's intervention in this country should, i think, continue to be geared to stabilising local democratic conditions and calming or relieving ethnic tensions. the motivation of the european perspective for the citizens of bosnia and herzegovina, as well as for its political representatives, can be a significant stimulus for the implementation of the necessary reforms of the political system as well as of the public administration institutions. there is no need to have illusions that bosnia and herzegovina's path towards european political culture will be easy. but we must be patient and we should be able to appreciate any positive change that happens in this country.
mr president, most of us would like to see bosnia and herzegovina developing strong and effective institutions at state level. it is obvious that without a functioning state no country can cope with the demands of european integration. but there is a real risk here that we, the eu, can overshoot it. if we push too hard for central institutions our efforts might backfire. it will stoke precisely those centrifugal and nationalist dynamics that we want to prevent, because in the end, for any state to function, it requires democratic legitimacy and that cannot be imposed by outsiders. let me be clear: european integration can indeed transform the politics and economics of candidate countries as it has done in my country, but it cannot construct democratic legitimacy of states and their institutions. only its citizens and its political elites can. of course bosnia and herzegovina can only join the eu as a single state, but it needs to be a single state that its citizens and politicians from the three entities will agree upon amongst themselves.
mr president, i voted in favour of the resolution on bosnia and herzegovina. i hope that it will send a message for reflection to the politicians in the country and it will stimulate them to engage with the reforms which the country urgently needs. i would also like to stress in this connection that it is of upmost importance that the politicians in bosnia and herzegovina find the courage and political will to work together. culture of compromise and constructive dialogue is the key for the future progress of the country. major issues such as constitutional reform, reform of the judiciary and further economic and social reforms would not be possible without common effort. i believe that progress of the country in the future development and integration processes is in the interests of our security and stability of the region but most importantly in the interests of european citizens and the citizens of bosnia and herzegovina.
in writing. − the global financial crisis and economic downturn have seriously damaged economic growth and financial stability and caused a significant deterioration in financial and economic conditions in several member states. despite the measures already taken to offset the negative effects of the crisis, its impact on the real economy, the labour market and citizens is still largely explorable. the aim of the proposal is to provide increased support through the european fisheries fund to member states experiencing (or threatened with experiencing) serious difficulties, in particular in relation to economic growth and financial stability and the worsening of their deficit and debt. the proposal seeks to help member states in their efforts to overcome the financial crisis, and aims to provide the member states concerned with the necessary funds to support projects and to revive the economy. the current situation requires a rapid response to mitigate the negative impact not only on the fisheries sector as such but also on the economy as a whole, and therefore i believe that the proposed regulation should enter into force as soon as possible and apply retroactively to periods during which member states have received financial assistance from the union or from other euro area member states in order to address serious difficulties related to their financial stability.
in writing. − the hormone-containing beef dispute has adversely affected transatlantic trade relations in agricultural products for more than two decades. in 1988, the eu banned the import of beef and meat products treated with certain growth hormones in order to protect consumers and food safety. although the hormone-containing beef dispute concerned a relatively small volume of trade, it led to a reduction in trade and had significant consequences on both sides of the atlantic. close business partners got into a long-running business dispute. the continued application of retaliatory duties on some european products has hampered exports and eu producers have subsequently lost market share. however, through bilateral negotiations between the union, the us and canada, a pragmatic way to avoid the destructive dynamics of trade sanctions has been found over time. the negotiations resulted in the so-called memoranda of understanding, which envisage the gradual lifting of sanctions imposed by the us and canada on eu agricultural products in exchange for autonomous tariff quotas with zero duty for hormone-free high-quality beef. the memoranda of understanding and their application clearly create a win-win situation for the trading partners. i am convinced that the swift and smooth adoption of the proposed regulation will help to restore and strengthen mutual trust and to overcome the existing contradictions in transatlantic trade relations in this sector.
in writing. − if you have the proposed regulation of the european parliament and of the council amends certain regulations relating to the common commercial policy. as regards the procedures for adopting certain measures, 26 regulations in the field of the common commercial policy are to be adapted to the new primary law provisions enshrined in the treaty of lisbon. in particular, this concerns the alignment of those regulations with articles 290 and 291 tfeu and with regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council laying down the rules and general principles concerning mechanisms for control by member states of the commission's exercise of implementing powers, established by article 291 (3) tfeu. article 290 tfeu introduces the legal institute of delegated acts in european law for the first time. consequently, the legislator may delegate to the executive legislative acts which are not essential. the legislator shall retain the right to revoke such delegation at any time and to take the relevant decision itself. the legislator may also veto any decision taken by means of a delegated act. it shall be sufficient if the council or parliament objects to the proposed commission decision. on the other hand, article 291 tfeu governs the adoption of implementing acts. the implementing acts are intended to ensure that european law is transposed in the same way in all member states. most of the relevant regulations thus allow for measures to be adopted precisely to protect commercial policy.
in writing. − the european parliament, noting the commission's updated financial perspective for 2007-13 and the fiscal consolidation efforts undertaken by most member states in the wake of the financial and budgetary crisis, recalls that the budget of the european union is one of the most important instruments for solidarity between member states and between generations and that it provides clear added value in view of its extraordinary impact on the real economy and the daily lives of european citizens. if union policies were to be financed by member states alone, their costs would increase sharply. in this respect, the european budget, when used in a synergistic way, really represents a clear common saving for the good of all. however, i also believe that the austerity measures taken at national level should not lead to an equivalent reduction of funds at eu level, as each euro issued at this level can create savings in the 27 member states. all measures taken so far to combat the crisis should help to return to a growth trajectory. the tailor-made savings measures already taken must be accompanied by targeted investments that will result in sustainable economic development. i am convinced that the eu budget has a crucial role to play in this context as a tool to ensure rapid and well-coordinated action in all areas.
in writing. − the european parliament has decided to set up a special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering with the following powers: to analyse and assess the extent of organised crime, corruption and money laundering and their impact on the union and its member states and to propose appropriate measures to enable the union to prevent and address these threats at international, european and national level; or to analyse and assess the implementation of union legislation on organised crime, corruption and money laundering and relevant policies at present, with a view to ensuring that union law and policy are evidence-based. the european parliament also decided that the powers of the european parliament's standing committees responsible for matters relating to the adoption, monitoring and implementation of union legislation in this field will not be changed and that the special committee may, in close cooperation with the relevant standing committees, make recommendations on measures or initiatives to be taken.
in writing. − the european parliament pointed out that the european judicial area must be built on a common european judicial culture in the ranks of practising lawyers, judges and prosecutors. this culture was not only based on eu law but also created through knowledge and understanding of national judicial systems, a complete reworking of university curricula, exchanges, study visits and joint learning, with the active support of the academy of european law, the european judicial training network and the european law institute. judicial training should be linked to a discussion on the traditional role of the judiciary and its modernisation. i believe that there is also a need to create a common judicial culture among members of the judiciary in order to promote the core values of the judicial professions through discussion and the establishment of a common professional ethic, the principles of the rule of law and the principles for the appointment and selection of judges, thus fostering the mutual trust necessary for the effective creation of a common judicial area. one of the other objectives should be to coordinate the training provided by existing schools in the field of judicial training and to promote dialogue and contacts between professionals. i also think that multilingual training is equally important, as the study has shown that only a relatively small number of judges speak foreign languages at a sufficiently good level to be able to participate actively in judicial training in other member states.
in writing. − if you have the international labour organization (ilo) estimates that more than 215 million children worldwide are working in activities that should be abolished. of these, 152 million are under 15 years of age and 115 million are engaged in hazardous activities. parliament must give its consent to the conclusion of the 2010 international cocoa agreement. however, the parties concerned have expressed serious concerns about the use of child labour in the cultivation and harvesting of cocoa beans. any use of the worst forms of child labour in the cultivation and harvesting of cocoa beans shall be unacceptable. in recent years, programmes and initiatives to tackle the worst forms of child labour on cocoa farms in west africa have made significant progress, but there is still a lot of work to be done, given the scale of the sector. i am deeply convinced that the use of child labour in cocoa plantations is strongly condemned. i consider it important that all stakeholders involved in the cultivation and processing of cocoa beans and their derived products governments, global industry, cocoa producers, labour organisations, ngos and consumers take responsibility for their obligations in combating all forms of forced child labour and trafficking in children, exchange experiences and cooperate in creating a sustainable supply chain for cocoa production without child labour.
in writing. − according to the international labour organisation, two forms of child labour should be distinguished. nothing should prevent children or adolescents from undertaking work which is not harmful to their health and development of their personality, nor does it interfere with their school duties. the problem is not who is working, but under what conditions. forced child labor on cocoa plantations in africa is as bad as modern day adult slavery in the factories that make cell phones and computers. and by buying chocolate without a certificate of origin, we are promoting inhuman treatment in the same way that we are promoting the purchase of electronics with made in china components. we are hurting people who have no choice but to hurt ourselves because in the unfair battle to reduce production costs europe cannot, and i hope will not, win.
in writing. − the international cocoa agreement 2010 will replace the existing agreement of 2001. the objectives of the new agreement are to promote international cooperation within the global cocoa economy, to provide an appropriate framework for discussion of all issues related to cocoa between governments and with the private sector, to contribute to the strengthening of member states' national cocoa economies, and to seek fair prices that lead to fair profits and returns for producers and consumers alike. the overall aim of the agreement is to bring more transparency and sustainability to an industry on which the livelihoods of 50 million people worldwide depend. its provisions will be administered and its implementation monitored by the international cocoa organisation. grown on more than eight million hectares of tropical land in 40 countries, cocoa is a crop that goes through a long supply chain from producers to traders, exporters, processors, chocolate makers and retailers to consumers. as the world's main importer and consumer of cocoa and the home of its largest processors and chocolate manufacturers, the eu bears a large share of the responsibility for making the sector more sustainable. i believe that the 2010 international cocoa agreement will have a positive impact on all actors involved in the cocoa economy. i therefore believe that parliament should give its consent to its conclusion.
in writing. − as the european parliament has a say in the negotiations on the new international cocoa agreement, thanks to the eu's status as the largest importer of cocoa and one of the main partners in the agreement, we must not allow minors to be involved in any way in the agricultural sector, including cocoa farming. it is a health hazardous work for children in a totally inappropriate environment and conditions instead of going to school. forced labour, slavery and human trafficking must not be tolerated under any circumstances. i therefore want to support and congratulate the rapporteur on this excellent initiative to make acceptance of an international agreement on the elimination of child labour in this sector conditional on its approval. it is also necessary to take a broader view of the problem and to look for ways to monitor the situation of child labour worldwide. i therefore call on the commission to take this initiative.
in writing. − diabetes is one of the most common non-communicable diseases, estimated to affect more than 32 million eu citizens, with another 32 million suffering from glucose intolerance, which is highly likely to develop into diabetes with clinical signs. the number of people affected by diabetes in europe is estimated to increase by 16,6% by 2030, mainly due to the obesity epidemic and the ageing of the european population. diabetes is currently incurable. complications associated with this disease can be prevented by promoting a healthy lifestyle and, above all, by early diagnosis, as often up to 50% of all people with diabetes are unaware of their disease. in this context, i believe it is justified for member states to develop, implement and monitor national diabetes programmes aimed at promoting health, reducing risk factors, predicting, preventing, early detecting and treating diabetes, targeting the general public and in particular high-risk groups. in order to meet the objectives related to non-communicable diseases, as well as to address public health, social and economic challenges, it is equally important that the eu and the member states continue to integrate prevention and control of risk factors into all relevant legislative and policy areas.

in writing. − iceland fulfils the copenhagen criteria and accession negotiations were opened with it on 27 july 2010, following approval by the council. it cooperates closely with the eu as a member of the european economic area (eea), under the schengen agreements and the dublin ii regulation, and has already adopted a substantial part of the acquis. it contributes to european cohesion and solidarity through the eea financial mechanism and cooperates with the eu in peacekeeping and crisis management operations. the progress made by iceland in the accession process is welcome, as is the opening of eleven negotiating chapters and the provisional closure of eight of them during the accession negotiations. i believe it is important to create the conditions for the completion of the accession process with iceland and to ensure that its accession is a success. the fact that a large proportion of icelanders support the continuation of accession negotiations is also positive. the government supports the organisation of balanced discussions on the accession process, based on sufficient information, and the involvement of icelandic society in public debates on eu membership. the union can acquire a new member state with a long history and a strong democratic tradition and civic culture.
in writing. − iceland is a country with a long-standing functioning democracy and therefore fulfils all the political criteria for membership of the european union. in addition to a long tradition of representative democracy, the country has a very high level of judicial system and anti-corruption measures and measures that oblige ministers and many officials to use procedures to minimise conflicts of interest. many of these procedures and measures may be at a higher level than in some current member states. despite a functioning market economy, iceland has some trade disagreements with the european union. in particular, it concerns the protection of fisheries in iceland. many observers say that it is on fishing that a country's membership of the eu depends. it's not the whaling that's the problem, which is banned in the eu, but the overall nature of the country that's based on this sector. it is precisely the nature of the country that requires this extension to be properly addressed. i fully support iceland's accession and firmly believe that the obstacles in the area of the common fisheries policy (cfp) will be overcome.

mr president, many have argued that the eu should radically rethink its russian policy; that it cannot be business as usual after months of protests and vladimir putin’s return to the kremlin after the presidential elections. let me say that such a policy shift would be a strategic blunder. the eu should continue to do what it is doing, only do it better. our current approach, a strategic but critical engagement with russia, remains sound and it is working. i agree with mr fleckenstein that what is happening in russia today is a political awakening of the middle class. the ever louder demands for political reform in russia are a direct consequence of its economic prosperity and openness to the world but that prosperity and openness is in a large part due to the density and volume of the eu-russia interactions: investments, trade, tourism and all that. we need more of that, including visa-free travel in the future. i am not saying that we should not be critical of the russian government whenever it disregards human rights or fails to uphold the principles of the rule of law and democracy but in the end constructive engagement will do more to advance our values in russia than tough talk in rigid positions. therefore, i would say that recent events in russia and the presidential elections actually present a case for staying the course in terms of our policy. in that framework i support the resolution.
russia is the european union's most important neighbour, both economically and politically. the presidential elections in this country are an important civic decision on the character of the state, because the democratically elected president of this country concentrates in his hands the decisive political power. the election, which was won by vladimir putin, was met with a number of objections from the opposition, whose leaders received little public support. the doubts about the absolute purity of the electoral process were also confirmed by the independent osce observers. at the same time, they noted that none of vladimir putin's opponents had any real hope of success. therefore, i think it is appropriate to respect the fact that in russia at present there is no significant political force that would represent a real alternative to the current power for us, but especially for the citizens of russia. in a healthy society, there must be an open political dialogue in a free media environment, and this should be our main objective for russia as well, so that even the currently unsuccessful opposition can show its real political potential in the new free environment.

for the efd group. water is of immense importance to our planet and its inhabitants. it's a necessary condition for the functioning of living organisms. we need it in homes, in factories, and in agriculture. the amount of water we have determines where we can live, grow and harvest our food. it makes up about two thirds of the human body, which cannot survive more than 12 days without it. leonardo da vinci, a genius thinker who was generations ahead of his time, spoke of its significance: "water was given the magical power to be the very essence of life on earth". however, the amount of water on earth is not unlimited. our demands for it are increasing with the increasing development of society. and since no new water is created on earth, but the same water is constantly being circulated in an eternal cycle, we must learn to manage it more rationally and protect its purity and quality. legislative pressure to protect water resources more strictly, to ensure that all people have access to the necessary drinking water and to regulate effectively the management of water in production sectors is therefore a legitimate and important measure to reduce the waste of this precious and vital liquid.
access to drinking water is a major problem in many countries of the world. on the other hand, we who have plenty of water at this time often use it irrationally, devalue it, waste it. poor water management in all contexts is certainly a major contributor to climate change. if we can regulate emissions, industrial production, or huge rivers, then we have to find a way to protect water and soil, to capture a raindrop where it falls. dense soil, uncontrolled growth of forest roads are the main cause of natural disasters in valleys every year, when precipitation falls cause significant damage to property and human lives. i am therefore convinced that the commission's future concept will include technical measures to ensure that rainwater, by reclaiming compacted soil, remains where it fell, gradually penetrates the soil, the roots of plants and naturally fills the sources of streams, rivers and wells.

in writing. − the eu, as a strategic partner and direct neighbour of russia, followed with particular interest the electoral process and public debate, as well as the large-scale and protracted protests in russia, concerning the state duma elections last december and the presidential elections to be held in early march. as regards respect for and protection of human rights and respect for commonly agreed principles of democracy, electoral rules and procedures, concerns remain about developments in the russian federation. however, the russian federation is a full member of the council of europe and the organisation for security and cooperation in europe (osce) and is therefore obliged to uphold the principles of democracy and respect for human rights. i believe that it is necessary to be critical of russia, but at the same time it is appropriate to fully support the modernisation programme, which includes a dialogue on economic and political reforms. this is how reforms can be introduced and implemented to address existing shortcomings. criticism of irregularities in the preparation and organisation of these elections is justified, and at the same time efforts must be made to strengthen democratic rules for future elections. it is important that president medvedev ensure the adoption of the necessary reforms of the political system, and at the same time that the new russian president is prepared to continue these reforms.
in writing. − both the european union and kazakhstan could derive considerable benefits from deeper cooperation. the european parliament supports this objective and stresses that economic cooperation must go hand in hand with political cooperation and must be based on the political will to implement and promote common values. negotiations on a new enhanced eu-kazakhstan agreement, which is to replace the partnership and cooperation agreement currently in force, started in june 2011. in february of that year, the kazakh president signed several laws aimed at improving the legal basis for labour relations, workers' rights and social dialogue, and strengthening the independence of the judiciary. sound relations between the union and kazakhstan are essential, as is the strengthening of political and economic cooperation, including in strategic areas such as human rights, the environment, energy, trade and transport, as well as the fight against terrorism, organised crime and drug trafficking. i am convinced that the kazakh authorities, as well as the wider civil society, would have great justification and benefit from taking such measures as would help to restore stability and security and restore the country's international standing.
in writing. − freedom of religion, belief, conscience and thought are among the freedoms which are fundamental and universal values and constitute essential elements of democracy. the european union has repeatedly expressed its commitment to protecting freedom of religion, belief, conscience and thought and has stressed that governments have an obligation to guarantee these freedoms worldwide. i am deeply convinced that all forms of violence in nigeria are reprehensible and, in addition, that the threat of continuing ethnic, religious and political tension, which continues to cause suffering to thousands of people, is particularly worrying. it is imperative that the nigerian government find a way to end the violence as soon as possible and to guarantee the safety and protection of the nigerian population as well as respect for human rights. the president should also make the necessary efforts to promote dialogue between representatives of different religions and beliefs, and in this way also strengthen freedom of thought, conscience and religion. the country's leaders should strive to fight poverty and inequality and promote social, political and economic reforms in order to build a democratic, stable, secure and free state that respects human rights.
in writing. − the sixth world water forum, taking place in marseille from 12 to 17 march 2012, is a unique platform where water experts, policy makers and decision-makers from all regions of the world can meet, discuss and seek solutions for water. the european union must also promote water solutions to ensure further progress at global, national, regional and local levels, and set itself the goal of fighting poverty and climate change. with regard also to the commission's future vision for the protection of europe's water resources and the report on the application of eu water legislation, i believe that it is essential to address the challenges facing europe and the world in the 21st century, in particular developing countries, in order to protect water resources, ensure water quality and ensure its availability worldwide. water management has a direct impact on human health, energy production, agriculture and food security. i also believe that there is a case for concluding and implementing international agreements on the joint management of crossborder surface and groundwater resources, which would bring together the public and administrations to ensure sustainable management of water resources and which would act as a safeguard against local and international conflicts.
on behalf of the ppe group. – madam president, this week, besides this case, i have some other news about trafficking in human beings: one case from sweden and one from china, where more than 24 000 victims were discovered last year. as cnn reported (as was mentioned), bodies of african refugees have been found in the sinai desert with organs missing. according to the testimony of victims and witnesses, corrupt egyptian doctors are directly involved in organ theft, coming to the sinai region with mobile hospital units, buying organs from bedouins and performing operations, mostly removing corneas, liver and kidneys. organs are taken from refugees while they are still alive; the organs are not useful if they are dead. they drug them first, remove their organs then leave them to die and dump them in deep dry wells along with hundreds of bodies. in a recent report the world health organisation called egypt a regional hub for the organ trade. there is no doubt that the driving force of trafficking is demand. where the legislation is missing and law enforcement is weak, trafficking is flourishing. i am convinced that the issue of human trafficking should be put higher on the agenda of bilateral negotiations.
the story of a group of eritreans kidnapped by traffickers from sudan and brought to the village of al-mahdiya near rafah last december is a shocking testimony to the moral devastation of a criminal community that profits from human misery and poverty. the sole witness to the murder, torture and rape 25-year-old eritrean solomon, who escaped from captivity by his captors, is a serious threat to a criminal gang trafficking in human beings and the human organs of his victims, and therefore every effort should be made to protect and secure him. the fact that the criminals whose testimony solomon is threatening have put a $50,000 bounty on his head is evidence not only that they make a good living trafficking people, but also that they are aware of the threat of testimony and the level of punishment they face if caught. commissioner, it is important for all of us - the european union, egypt, israel, but also the whole civilized world - to stop this atrocity in sinai as soon as possible and bring the perpetrators to justice. so we need to be more proactive on this.
for the efd group. the armed military raid on the palestinian educational television station al-quds by israeli defence forces units in late february of this year must be classified as a senseless and unnecessary act of hostility and violence by the israeli state power against the palestinian population. the additional argumentation that was supposed to justify this raid on the television studio and the theft of television equipment in front of the general public turned out to be false. before the raid on the tv studio, the israeli authorities never warned the palestinian authorities that the use of the frequencies to transmit the tv signal would cause them any technical problems. nor was the joint technical committee set up by the oslo accords informed. the european union supports the efforts of the palestinians to build civilian structures and institutions that help stabilise the political environment in the middle east. the european union is committed to the peace process and to the peace process in the gaza strip.
for the efd group. during the arab spring the previous year, bahrain's moderate islamic regime was rocked by a wave of civil unrest that left 35 people dead and hundreds imprisoned. at the request of the international community, the king of bahrain established an independent commission of inquiry which found, inter alia, that five people had been tortured while in detention in the crackdown and that disproportionate force had been used against peaceful demonstrators and political activists. many individuals have been tried and imprisoned in trials that did not comply with international standards and even with bahraini criminal law. in accordance with the recommendations of the committee, a special investigation unit was established to determine responsibility for the deaths of civilians, their torture and unlawful judicial proceedings. however, this effort needs to be continued. in parallel with the ongoing investigation, it is necessary to restore social consensus, improve the protection of human rights and pursue a constructive dialogue. i think it's our duty to remind the king of bahrain of this as well.
i appreciate the excellent work of rapporteur jelko kacin. the result is a report that objectively reflects the situation in serbia and its relations with the eu. serbia has been granted the status of candidate country deservedly. it now has the opportunity to realise its potential and become one of the 'front runners' of european integration. i want to encourage our serbian colleagues. after all, the status of candidate is only the beginning of a long and hard work. i am glad that the dialogue between serbia and kosovo is continuing. dialogue and agreements must contribute to improving relations and to the gradual elimination of anomalies between partners. the key is to implement agreements in good faith, respecting each other's partners in the dialogue and avoiding unnecessary tension. so serbia has a lot of work ahead of it. it will require strong pro-european-oriented politicians who can reform and move the country forward. serbia has the potential to successfully manage this process and has our full support in this.
in writing. the opening of accession negotiations with the european union was a historic moment for serbia. it was the first step in disengaging from the legacy of tito's communist regime. these negotiations, and above all the clear prospect of serbia's future eu membership, are key to achieving lasting stability in the war-torn balkans. the possibility of obtaining a european passport in the near future and free access to the single market for labour, goods and services also acts as a motivator for the serb minorities living in the surrounding republics. for serbs living outside serbia, too, this is a compelling argument in favour of constructively seeking a way of coexistence that is not based on conflict but rather on mutual accommodation and compromise. it would be naive to convince ourselves that the prospect of eu membership will eliminate all conflicts in the balkans once and for all. many of them have been going on for centuries, and they will take years, perhaps decades, to overcome. but i am convinced that the opening of accession negotiations has created the necessary space for this.
mr president, my thanks to the rapporteur for her work. kosovo is facing a year of challenges and opportunities. i appreciate and fully support the agenda prepared by the commission and the council for this year: moving on with the feasibility study, the visa liberalisation dialogue and the eu programmes constitutes concrete and ambitious steps which are urgently needed for kosovo now. the eu needs to invest in this agenda to be credible. we should also expect concrete and tangible results from the kosovo authorities, especially reforms in the judiciary and in public administration, but most importantly in strengthening the rule of law and in the fight against corruption and organised crime. i would also like to encourage kosovo to continue the dialogue with serbia in order to bring concrete results for kosovars and normalise relations between kosovo and serbia. i also believe that both the people’s representatives in the kosovo assembly and we in the european parliament should be regularly informed of this process and its results. finally, kosovo has lots of hard work ahead, but i am sure this will improve life in kosovo and bring it first closer to the eu and finally into the eu itself.
i respect the position of the european council, which in 2003 promised all the western balkan countries that they would be able to become members of the european union. but to fulfill this promise to the current administration of hashim thaci seems to me to be a mockery of the principles of humanity and justice on which we build the coexistence of peoples in the union. the report of the parliamentary assembly of the council of europe pointed to serious crimes committed by the drenica group, especially against the serb, but also the inconvenient albanian inhabitants of this province. the ongoing intimidation and murder of witnesses to these crimes demonstrates the inadequacy of the work of the european union rule of law mission in kosovo and its inability to document the crimes of the kosovo liberation army in a perfectly objective manner in a mafia-ridden environment. i am convinced that unless all the accusations made by the council of europe are thoroughly investigated, we have no right to legitimise by collective bargaining a regime led by people who are being investigated for serious crimes.
thanks and compliments to charles tannock for his leadership in the preparation of this report, but also for his unwavering support for the integration process in montenegro. credit goes to the shadow informants. montenegro has made tangible progress on the integration agenda. it is doing well in the process of social transformation and reform, and this also applies to the seven known priorities of the european commission. these processes need to be further supported. of course, many challenges remain, particularly in the areas of the rule of law, the fight against organised crime and corruption, cooperation between the state and civil society, and media freedom, but even here results are already being seen. these are long-term processes for which the european union has instruments during accession negotiations. montenegro is the champion of the western balkans on the way to the european union and is also a factor of regional stability. we should therefore continue to support it in this endeavour.
mr. president, i have to go. my dear officer. my fellow citizens! the experience of the crisis should leave no doubt about the need for a more transparent, stable, reliable, accountable and better governed union corporate sector. the experience of the series of failures of recent years has shown that good governance alone cannot prevent excessive risk-taking and that it is therefore necessary to establish flexible rules that respect independent control and different corporate cultures. corporate governance initiatives should be accompanied by corporate social responsibility initiatives. but the two are not to be confused, and we had a lot of debate about this during the report. despite the report's very complex management techniques and theoretical solutions, it is quite surprising that the anger is over quotas. and what is even more surprising to me is that the itre and imco committees have also focused on this in their opinions. i think that the question of diversity cannot be avoided when we talk about the boards of directors, but i think that it is not really a central question and that it should not be the fate of the report. i think that this is something that really needs to be looked at, but certainly the professional background, the professional training, needs to be considered, and it needs to be just as important as diversity.
in writing. half a year ago, we debated the 'free food' programme in parliament. the situation where the normal functioning of the programme was blocked by a group of states was unacceptable. the program is perhaps more important now than ever. food supplies are at an all-time low, the number of poor has increased because of the crisis, and i fear it will continue to rise, and food prices are also rising to dizzying heights. the programme should therefore be strengthened and its budget increased. after all, that is what the commission proposed. food is becoming more difficult to obtain from surplus stocks than it was at the beginning of the programme. now more and more of them have to be bought on the regular market, and that's understandably more expensive. i am glad that the debate on the viability of the programme has been resolved, also thanks to the european parliament. member states have been given assurances that the programme will be effective and that as much of the money will go to food purchases and as little to related expenditure such as distribution and administration. the example of slovakia also shows that the distribution of flour was not entirely problem-free, but this is not a reason to cancel the programme, only to make it more efficient. it is important that the programme continues to be legitimised and popularised, as its current form is valid for only two years. then it will be decided again. i would hate to see a repeat of last year's situation.
after the financial and economic crisis, there were high expectations that the european investment bank would be the one to support and ensure the continuity of many projects. however, in several areas these expectations have not been met and already last year, in the debate on the 2009 annual report, i pointed out that the crisis finance that was supposed to go to the smes in eastern europe in particular had improved the balance sheet of the private commercial banks in particular for quite a long time. we expected that in times of crisis, the priority for the european investment bank would be to help those areas that are most affected by the crisis. but if we look at the distribution of loans over the past year, we get a strange picture. while germany received 10% of the total, greece received only 1,6%. with the german savings and the trade surpluses and the greek problems, we expected the opposite. the same applies to central and eastern europe. the least affected countries get much more of the total pie, while the allocations for say bulgaria, lithuania, latvia, slovakia or romania are more in the tens of percent. i'd like to know the key to how you're allocating credit to each country.
the european investment bank may, by its choice of policy, technical and financial criteria for the selection of financial assistance, have a significant influence on the nature of the investment activities envisaged. its criteria for granting financial aid must therefore take account of certain visionary aspects of the expectation of change in a civilized society. support for technologies that do not meet better than average european environmental standards should therefore be significantly limited. i believe that the basis for qualified project appraisal in the future should be to place greater emphasis on the impact and participation of experts assessing the environmental and innovative parameters of the planned investments. this seems to me to be the only way, and the nature of the eib's assistance, to contribute to improving the innovation and greening of new investments both in europe and in the world.
in writing. the european investment bank is one of the european union's main instruments for pursuing its strategic objectives and plays a leading role in reviving the european economy and fostering growth. the total volume of loans granted, the european recovery recovery project, as well as the 30% increase in loans disbursed for the convergence objectives are key achievements not only for the bank itself, but above all for the recovery and recovery of the economy in europe. the bank's main activities support the europe 2020 strategy. the eib's efforts to provide greater support to smes, which are the driving force of the european economy, should be fully supported. the eib's activities are supported by funds raised on the capital markets. therefore, a aaa rating is essential for its functioning. the bank's capital needs were estimated at eur [0-5] billion in 2011 and eur [0-5] billion in 2012. therefore, measures are necessary to maintain the excellent credit rating. the eib should continue to support the europe 2020 strategy through the use of the structural funds and the further application of innovative financial instruments.
for the sake of brevity, i will address two shortcomings that i find fault with in the report. on the one hand, the report makes no mention of or addresses the issue of racism, despite the comments made by ngos. this is a fundamental mistake in my view, since racist speech is one of the major obstacles to the fulfilment of citizenship and civil rights in the european union and there is a marked increase in far-right extremism in the european union. another problematic area is the denial of the right to free movement of persons to ethnic minorities, which is a reality, mainly due to the existence of various barriers. there is no doubt that the free movement of ethnic or religious minorities is being impeded on a daily basis. this is particularly true of roma. the enforcement of the legal right of free movement must also take into account the right not to be discriminated against and must be applied in this sense, for example in the case of illegal deportations or other violations of this right. i believe that anti-discrimination must be at the heart of european union citizenship and we must ensure that it is adequately transposed into existing legislation.
the challenge to the exclusive competence of the member states in matters of family and marriage, under the pretext of discrimination, has already become the rule in this parliament. the report submitted is no different. in point 12, the rapporteur asks the commission to respond more specifically to petitions concerning the recognition of documents on marital status. he cites as an example a petition by the polish organization campaign against homophobia. but in this case, the commission's answer was very precise. i quote: 'the issue of certificates of civil status is the exclusive competence of the member states.' if we continue to question this authority, we will destroy the european project. we should take more initiative on the issues raised by ms jäätteenmäki in her contribution.
in writing. through the work of the committee on petitions, the ep is in direct contact with eu citizens who have approached the legislature about restrictions on their rights within the union. the latest eu citizenship report is important for legislative planning as it shows, through concrete examples, the areas where eu citizens still face difficulties in exercising their rights guaranteed by the treaties. in my meetings with citizens, i have often found that, although many economic, cultural and other opportunities are already open within the internal market, there are obstacles and unpleasant experiences that can deter citizens from exercising their right to freedom of movement. the petitions we receive are like a mirror for the institutions and contain accurate data that can help us take the next step in solving problems. it is not surprising to read that some member states still impede the exercise of social rights, the rights of those in higher education or the rights of the self-employed. citizens of the eu member states that joined in 2004 and later still face more difficulties in enjoying the rights guaranteed by the eu treaties as full eu citizens. the institutions are tasked with promoting the proper transposition of eu legislation in the member states and with speeding up the correction of recently discovered electoral, social, administrative, educational and other discriminatory measures.
i could not vote for the report submitted because it contains misleading information about one of the seats of parliament. since its creation, the european parliament has had a single seat, in strasbourg. and i fully support cutting costs during the austerity period. let's get rid of the expensive buildings in brussels and cancel the unnecessary mini-plenaries. and let's talk about whether the idea of a single mansion is compatible with the completion of the konrad adenauer complex in luxembourg. this has not been disputed by any of the representatives of one of the premises. the house of european history is also funded in parliament's budget for next year. if we do not want to trample on this history and rob it of its meaning, we must stop questioning strasbourg as the seat of the european parliament. the european union is not just about money.
in writing. − in october 2011, the european parliament was asked to give its consent to the council's proposal to adopt, on behalf of the european union, the amended statutes and the amended rules of procedure of the international rubber study group. the international rubber study group (irsg) is an intergovernmental organisation which has been based in singapore since 2008. the group is a platform for discussion among rubber producing and consuming countries on all aspects of the rubber supply chain. membership of the irsg is open to national governments. currently, the european union and nine countries are contributing members: the republic of cameroon, côte d'ivoire, india, japan, malaysia, nigeria, the russian federation, singapore and sri lanka. approximately 120 representatives of the industry are members through the panel of associate members. the group aims to collect and disseminate comprehensive statistical information on the global rubber industry. it is generally considered that this activity is of crucial importance in terms of increasing the transparency of rubber markets and market trends in this sector. i believe that it is appropriate to seek to take the necessary steps leading to the enlargement of the group's membership base, in particular through negotiations with the countries which are the largest producers and consumers of rubber. a strong membership base remains a fundamental prerequisite for the long-term viability and effectiveness of the irsg as an authoritative body.
in writing. − the aim of the report presented is to address the commission communication on the implementation of regulation (ec) no 261/2004 laying down common rules for a system of compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding in the event of cancellation or long delay of flights and the commission report on the implementation and results of regulation (ec) no 1107/2006 of 5 july 2006 on the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility when travelling by air. in ensuring access to passenger rights, it is important that passengers know their rights. information on passenger rights should therefore be communicated in a simple, appropriate and comprehensible manner during the main sections of the journey. effective, transparent and independent bodies to enforce compliance, deal with passenger complaints, help resolve disputes between passengers and air carriers and finally impose sanctions where necessary are essential. it is necessary to ensure consistency between the different legislation on air passenger rights in order to respond to the development of the travel market, which is moving towards an increasingly self-organised travel experience. as regards the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility in air transport, i believe that equal travel opportunities and non-discrimination guaranteeing equal access and barrier-free services should be ensured for these persons.
in writing. − the european union's engagement in the field of asylum is based on the need for solidarity between member states in addressing a challenge that, in an eu without internal borders, individual states cannot effectively address on their own. the creation of a joint eu resettlement programme will ensure that more eu member states participate in resettlement, while helping to demonstrate greater eu solidarity with third countries in receiving refugees. in view of the establishment of a common eu resettlement programme, which aims to increase the success of the eu's resettlement efforts to provide protection to refugees and to maximise the strategic impact of resettlement by better targeting those most in need of resettlement, common resettlement priorities should be formulated at eu level on a regular basis. it is therefore appropriate for the commission to decide on common annual eu priorities taking into account specific geographical regions, specific nationalities as well as specific categories of refugees to be resettled. in view of the resettlement needs, i consider it also necessary to provide persons (where resettlement is considered to be the most appropriate solution to their specific needs) with additional financial support in relation to specific geographical regions, specific nationalities, as well as specific categories of refugees to be resettled.
in writing. − if you have council regulation (ec) no 428/2009 of 5 may 2009 establishing a union regime for the control of exports, transfer, brokering and transit of dual-use items requires that dual-use items (including software and technology) are subject to effective control when exported from or transiting through the union or when supplied to a third country on the basis of brokering services provided by an intermediary resident or established in the union. in order to enable the member states and the european union to comply with their international obligations, annex i to regulation (ec) no 428/2009 establishes a common list of dual-use items and technologies referred to in article 3 of that regulation, which establishes internationally agreed controls on those items and technologies. technical progress in today's world brings with it the need to regularly update the list of controlled items. annex i to that regulation was last updated on 5 may 2009 on the occasion of the adoption of regulation (ec) no 428/2009. all international export control regimes have since taken decisions to amend and update their control lists. it is therefore necessary to make the necessary changes to ensure that the commitments undertaken by the eu member states under those schemes are fully applied throughout the union.
in writing. − if you have the ongoing financial crisis has brought otc derivatives to the forefront of regulatory attention. the looming collapse of bear sterns in march 2008, the collapse of lehman brothers on 15 september 2008 and the forced rescue of aig the following day highlighted the shortcomings in the functioning of the otc derivatives market. within that market, regulators paid particular attention to the role played by credit default swaps (cds) during the crisis. in its broader communication of 4 march 2009 stimulating economic recovery in europe , the commission committed itself to providing appropriate initiatives to increase transparency and address financial stability concerns, following the report on derivatives and other complex structured products. all subsequent steps are part of a wider international effort to increase the stability of the financial system in general and of the otc derivatives market in particular. given the global nature of the otc derivatives market, an internationally coordinated approach is crucial. it is therefore important that this proposal takes into account what is planned or has already been done in other jurisdictions in the regulation of otc derivatives in order to avoid the risk of regulatory arbitrage.
in writing. − following the entry into force of directive 2004/40/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 29 april 2004 on the minimum health and safety requirements regarding the exposure of workers to the risks arising from physical agents (electromagnetic fields), serious concerns were expressed by interested parties, in particular the medical community, regarding the impact of the implementation of that directive on the use of medical procedures based on medical imaging. they also expressed concern about the impact of the directive on certain industrial activities. the commission has examined the arguments put forward by interested parties and has decided to reconsider certain provisions of directive 2004/40/ec in the light of new scientific evidence. on 14 june 2011, the commission adopted a proposal for a new directive to replace the original directive. the new directive should ensure a high level of protection of the health and safety of workers and the continuity and development of medical and other industrial activities involving electromagnetic fields. given the very short time remaining until the transposition deadline of 30 april 2012, i believe that it is necessary to ensure that this directive is adopted by the european parliament and the council as a matter of urgency and that it enters into force without delay.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 2073/2004 of 16 november 2004 on administrative cooperation in the field of excise duties establishes a common system whereby member states assist each other and cooperate with the commission in order to ensure the correct application of excise legislation and, conversely, to combat evasion of excise duties and the resulting distortion in the internal market. the completion of the internal market continues to require a system of administrative cooperation in the field of excise duties. exchanges of information in excise matters are needed on a very large scale in order to establish a true picture of the excise matters of certain persons. for the purpose of proper coordination of information flows, it is necessary to maintain the provisions of regulation no 2073/2004 on a single point of contact in each member state. since more direct contacts between the authorities and officials may be necessary to ensure efficiency, the provisions on delegation and appointment of the relevant officials should also be maintained. for the purpose of effective monitoring of excise procedures in cross-border movements, it is also necessary to continue to provide for the possibility of simultaneous controls by member states and the presence of officials of one member state on the territory of another member state in the framework of administrative cooperation. furthermore, i believe that feedback is an appropriate means of ensuring continuous improvement in the quality of the information exchanged. a framework for providing feedback should therefore be established.
in writing. − the ceiling for heading 5 of the multiannual financial framework (mff) for the 2013 eu budget is eur 9 181 million in current prices. i believe that the aim of any budget negotiation should be to achieve maximum efficiency. in accordance with the agreement reached between the bureau and the committee on budgets at the conciliation meeting of 13 march 2012, the total amount of the draft estimates for 2013 is fixed at eur 1 759 391 671. at the same time, strict budgetary control, close cooperation with the committee on budgets and the identification of further possible savings during this budgetary procedure are needed. taking into account the increase in the activities of members on non-legislative work provided for in the rules of procedure, which commits significant resources of parliament and other eu institutions, it is necessary to analyse this fact and at the same time to present options to reduce this increased burden. i believe that further reorganisation of parliament's working methods should be considered, with significant savings being made by establishing a single seat. in accordance with the conditions laid down in the regulation on the financing of political parties, it is worrying that the principles on which the union is founded, namely the principles of freedom, democracy, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, are not fully respected. parliament should only provide funding to parties that strictly adhere to the eu's fundamental principles and the charter of fundamental rights.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation and to assist them with their reintegration into the labour market. the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 allows the mobilisation of the egf within the annual ceiling of eur 500 million. on 1 july 2011, spain submitted an application to mobilise the egf, in respect of redundancies in 513 enterprises classified in nace revision 2 division 41 ('building'), operating in the nuts ii region comunidad valenciana (es52), and supplemented it by additional information up to 25 november 2011. the application submitted complies with the requirements for establishing the financial contributions under article 10 of regulation (ec) no 1927/2006, and the commission has therefore proposed to make available eur 1 642 030. since the country fulfils the conditions laid down, i am also of the opinion that the egf should be mobilised in order to provide a financial contribution at the request of spain.
in writing. − if you have in his letter of 4 march 2011, the president of the european parliament asked the committee on constitutional affairs to examine a possible amendment to the rules of procedure following the meeting of the conference of presidents on 17 february 2011. at this meeting, the conference of presidents recalled that, following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, parliament had become the co-legislator of the european union and that, under the ordinary legislative and budgetary procedures, it had the same powers as the council. in view of this new institutional balance, the conference of presidents considers that there is no longer any need to maintain a question time for the council in its present form, i.e. at each plenary session, in the agenda for plenary sessions. on the contrary, according to the conference of presidents, it is necessary to maintain the possibility of holding a question time not only with the president of the commission but also with the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union and the president of the eurogroup. to take account of the development of institutional relations in recent years, the revision of parliament's rules of procedure will have to be much more extensive than originally planned. however, as regards question time for the council, the abolition of its present form reflects a change in the institutional balance. however, it appears useful to maintain the possibility of asking questions to the council during a specific question time on matters relating to its powers outside the exercise of its legislative and budgetary functions.
in writing. − the adoption of the treaty of lisbon was a major success for the european parliament, which ensured its participation in the legislative process with the council. these newly acquired powers and responsibilities should be fully reflected in parliament's decisions, including by removing unnecessary obstacles stemming from the previous institutional set-up. that is why i really welcome mr lamassoure's report, which makes it easier for parliament to put questions to the council. i am convinced that this will simplify and make the work of the european parliament more efficient.

in writing. - i strongly condemn all forms of terrorism and violence committed against innocent victims. but every human life is worthy of protection from conception to natural death. i therefore strongly oppose the execution of two young people in belarus, vladislav kavalev and dmitry konovalov. they were sentenced to death for allegedly committing a bloody terrorist act on 11 april 2011 in the minsk metro. the international community had serious doubts about the course of the investigation and the subsequent judgment from the outset. even many of the injured and relatives of the victims of this attack are still not convinced that these two young people were the real perpetrators. tens of thousands of belarusians have signed a petition calling for the death penalty not to be carried out. i am glad that this parliament is clear on the situation with regard to the belarusian dictator lukashenko. the resolution adopted is another signal to all democratically minded people in belarus of the strong support of the european union.
in writing. − the european parliament has decided to set up a special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering with the following powers: to analyse and assess the extent of organised crime, corruption and money laundering and their impact on the union and its member states and to propose appropriate measures to enable the union to prevent and address these threats at international, european and national level; or to analyse and assess the implementation of union legislation on organised crime, corruption and money laundering and relevant policies at present, with a view to ensuring that union law and policy are evidence-based. the european parliament also decided that the powers of the european parliament's standing committees responsible for matters relating to the adoption, monitoring and implementation of union legislation in this field will not be changed and that the special committee may, in close cooperation with the relevant standing committees, make recommendations on measures or initiatives to be taken.
in writing. − the idea of a european foundation for democracy has been incorporated into a more general eu debate on the review of eu policies and activities promoting democracy following the events in the southern mediterranean. the intention is to create a semi-independent institution that could support democracy activists and the development of democracy in the world in a non-bureaucratic way and that would not be directly linked to eu diplomacy or the european commission. for the polish presidency of the council, the european foundation for democracy was one of the priorities and worked with all stakeholders to make progress on this idea. parliament should now be the institution that contributes constructively to the debate and also takes part in the creation, management and control structures of this possible european fund. i believe it is important to take into account that the european union needs a more flexible and less bureaucratic instrument to support political actors seeking democratic change in their countries. at the same time, it also seems justified to envisage the establishment of a european foundation for democracy as a non-profit-making, grant-giving organisation set up to strengthen democratic institutions worldwide, as the pursuit of democracy worldwide is not only a moral imperative but also clearly set out as a fundamental principle of the union's external action.
in writing. − mr president, in his report, mr lambsdorf proposes, among other things, that the european foundation for democracy should support projects in 'gender sensitive areas'. as examples, she cites the fight against violence and activities promoting equal rights for women and girls in the areas of justice, education and the labour market. i fully support supporting projects that are aimed at this, but i believe that the use of the term 'gender sensitive areas' is misleading and confusing in this context. we are talking about women and men, about europe wanting to promote equal civil rights for women and men. the european foundation for democracy must avoid the temptation to export leftist ideological constructs of the 'gender' type to third countries, as this jeopardises its impartiality and credibility in the eyes of the partner states.
in writing. − in its opinion of 12 october 2011 on serbia's application for membership, the commission recommended that the european council grant serbia candidate country status. a constructive approach to regional cooperation and good neighbourly relations are key elements of the stabilisation and association process. i believe that if satisfactory action is taken to meet the key priorities outlined by the commission in its opinion and if the reform process continues, accession negotiations with serbia should be opened as soon as possible. serbia's significant progress towards meeting the copenhagen criteria is also welcome, with further progress in the european integration process dependent on continued progress in this area, and in particular on the guarantee of democracy, the functioning of democratic institutions, the rule of law, respect for human rights, the protection of minorities, the maintenance of good neighbourly relations and regional cooperation, including the peaceful resolution of bilateral issues, as well as the improvement of the functioning of the market economy. on the other hand, the situation in northern kosovo, especially in the second half of 2011, resulting in the violence resulting from the july incidents and subsequent attacks on the international forces of kfor, is of concern. such acts are reprehensible and the serbian government should make every effort to fulfil its commitment to do everything in its power to prevent them. only through continued political dialogue can a lasting de-escalation of tensions in the region be achieved.
in writing. − at the thessaloniki european council on 19 and 20 june 2003, all the western balkan states were given a pledge to become members of the european union, a pledge which was reiterated at the western balkans high-level meeting in sarajevo on 2 june 2010. regional cooperation and good neighbourly relations are of great importance in the process of european integration and also play an important role in ensuring security and stability in the region. kosovo's declaration of independence has been recognised by 85 countries, including 22 eu member states. it is important for the union to engage in dialogue with kosovo, and this commitment is also of great importance for maintaining stability and security in the eu's immediate neighbourhood. i believe that the eulex rule of law mission is of great importance, among other things, as tangible evidence of the commitment of the entire eu and its 27 member states to improving the rule of law in kosovo. the union should develop initiatives aimed at increasing the effectiveness and acceptance of this important mission throughout kosovo. in some areas, such as police and customs, significant progress has been made. however, there is a need to step up core activities in the areas of fighting corruption and organised crime as well as war crimes in order to bring more tangible results to the mission.
in writing. − accession negotiations with turkey started on 3 october 2005, after the council had approved the negotiating framework. turkey is committed to reform, good neighbourly relations and gradual rapprochement with the eu. this effort should be seen as an opportunity for it to modernise and strengthen and further improve its democratic institutions, the rule of law and respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. in its 2011 progress report, the commission concluded that turkey plays a key role in the security and prosperity of the union, that its contribution to the european union will only be effective in a number of important areas if a positive agenda and a credible approach to the negotiation process are ensured, and that it remains of paramount importance that turkey pursue reforms on policy criteria and make further substantial efforts to ensure fundamental rights. however, with a view to strengthening stability and promoting good neighbourly relations and a positive political and economic partnership, state actors must intensify their efforts to resolve outstanding bilateral issues with their direct neighbours, including unresolved legal obligations and disputes over land, sea and air borders, in accordance with the provisions of the un charter and international law.
in writing. − although turkey has been an associated country since 1963, accession negotiations did not begin until 2005. turkey is not only a candidate country for the european union, it is also a country that plays a very important regional role in relations with neighbouring countries. the close cooperation between turkey and the european union is a testament to the close relationship that has lasted for several decades. i therefore welcome the positive approach of the commission, which our group also shares. the accession negotiations are unfortunately not progressing as quickly as we would like. turkey still faces many problems and challenges, notably freedom of expression, the kurdish question and the cyprus issue. the eu has also been active in the fight against terrorism, and has been involved in the implementation of the un convention against torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. i firmly believe that together we can achieve this.
in writing. − i supported the enlargement report on turkey because i consider it balanced as a whole. on the one hand, it recognises the significant progress that turkey has made, but it also highlights my continued reservations about its full membership of the eu. turkey is our major economic partner and its position as an ally in the middle east is crucial from the west's perspective. however, a number of reservations remain on the issues of legislative harmonisation and application of the same values, as well as on the cyprus issue. however, i would also like to assure my turkish friends that, although equality before the law is a fundamental condition of the rule of law, the requirement to establish a 'equality council' and to take unspecified measures against homophobia are not such conditions. the broad interpretation of the terms discrimination and homophobia has led to real discrimination against many decent citizens in the eu. i would hate for turkey to make that mistake again.
in writing. − the european council has mandated the council to assess montenegro's progress on the basis of a commission report. the political consensus on eu-related issues remains broad in the country. the cornerstone of its foreign policy is progress towards eu and nato membership. i am convinced that reform efforts require strong political will and an overall commitment to addressing the upcoming challenges in the accession process. montenegro has made significant progress in the implementation of the seven key priorities set by the commission in 2010, namely improving the quality of the work of the parliament and the electoral framework, professionalism of the public administration, independence of the judiciary, fighting corruption, fighting organised crime, ensuring media freedom and strengthening cooperation with civil society. the country has experienced a moderate economic recovery, with low inflation and a significant inflow of foreign direct investment, as well as a small decline in the unemployment rate, and has also implemented the trade provisions of the eu stabilisation and association agreement. however, further reform efforts are needed to effectively implement the government action plan on key priorities, to accelerate recovery from the economic crisis, while also ensuring appropriate control of public expenditure and external debt. montenegro must also maintain fiscal stability and strengthen and build the administrative and institutional capacity necessary to assume the future obligations of eu membership.
