in writing. − the commission has recently reiterated its commitment to building a strong and successful single market that is people-centred and rebuilding trust. corporate governance and social responsibility are key elements in these efforts. corporate governance is traditionally defined as the system by which companies are managed and controlled and as the set of relationships between the company's management, its board of directors, shareholders and other stakeholders. according to the study available, the overall quality of the companies' statements concerning their corporate governance is unsatisfactory when deviating from the recommended corporate governance code. the study found that in more than 60% of cases where the company decided not to comply with the recommendation, it did not provide a sufficient explanation. the companies simply stated without any explanation that they deviated from the recommendation or provided only a general or limited explanation. however, in many member states, slow but gradual improvements can already be observed in this area. further progress could be made by introducing more detailed requirements on the information to be disclosed by companies deviating from the recommendations. the requirements should be clear and precise, as many of the current problems arise from a misunderstanding of the nature of the explanation required.
in writing. − the responsibility for the management of a company lies with those who own it the shareholders. it is our duty to create a legislative framework so that each shareholder can decide on his assets. we don't tell companies how many women to have on their boards. our job is to ensure that every citizen, woman or man, has equal civil, property and employment rights. if we start holding people accountable for their choices, we're taking away their freedom and their initiative. it'll be the end of business and a functioning economy. the eu cannot guarantee prosperity to people because it is born of risk. i lived in a country that, in an effort to eliminate market speculation and so-called undue profits, first abolished the stock exchange and then the business itself. this country is bankrupt.
in writing. − for more than 50 years, the european investment bank (eib) has been one of the eu's main instruments in promoting its strategic short- and long-term objectives. the bank's strong commitment to being a european bank and to playing a leading role in the recovery of the european economy and in supporting growth is encouraging. as regards the 2010 annual report, the bank has successfully completed its two-year anti-crisis activities and has started to return to pre-crisis lending levels. key achievements of the period include, for example, the completion of the eur 30 billion sme back-to-back loan scheme one year early, the completion of the eur 61 billion european recovery support package, a 30% increase in disbursed loans for the convergence objectives and a total lending of eur 72 billion. in 2010, the bank's board of directors adopted a new operational plan for the period 2011-2013 which identified three main aspects of the bank's activities, namely support for the europe 2020 strategy, combating climate change and supporting eu external policy objectives. i think it is also necessary to recognise that it is justified to measure results not only in terms of quantity but also in terms of quality. in this context, it is crucial to link inputs and outputs in order to assess the effectiveness of the system.
in writing. − the european investment bank contributes annually to promoting economic growth and development in the european union and beyond. supporting projects aimed at increasing employment, social inclusion and the development of disadvantaged regions brings funding where it is needed most. i therefore welcome the 2010 annual report of the european investment bank and encourage the eib to focus its operations on activities to overcome the consequences of the financial and economic crisis and to restore growth. the increased volume of loans for structural programmes is undoubtedly a step in the right direction. i believe that funding should not be limited to countries in serious financial difficulty, but should be made available more flexibly to convergence regions. in conclusion, i would like to express my belief that greater transparency as well as the disclosure of the final beneficiaries of loans will contribute to improving the allocation of available resources and raising awareness of eib projects.
in writing. − if you have the concept of citizenship of the european union, introduced by the maastricht treaty in 1992, added a new political dimension to the originally economic nature of european integration. anyone who has the nationality of an eu member state is now automatically a citizen of the european union. eu citizenship does not replace the nationality of a member state. instead, it grants all eu citizens additional rights, guaranteed by the eu treaties, that affect their daily lives. it serves to be a fundamental status of nationals of the member states enabling those who find themselves in the same situation to enjoy, within the scope of the treaty, equal legal treatment irrespective of their nationality. persons who use a european project to extend aspects of their lives beyond national borders through travel, study, work, marriage, retirement, purchase or inheritance of real estate, voting or online purchases in companies established in another member state must be able to enjoy the full benefits of the rights deriving from the treaties. however, a gap remains between the legislation in force and the reality of citizens' lives, especially in cross-border situations. the need for eu citizenship to be more effective in practice has been underlined on several occasions. i believe that it is right and important to work towards strengthening eu citizenship by revitalising the link between citizens and the union itself and giving effect to their rights.
in writing. − the european commission published in october 2010 a document entitled 'eu citizenship report 2010: removing obstacles to the exercise of eu citizens' rights'. the consultation of civil society has led to an overview of the main obstacles that eu citizens continue to encounter when exercising their rights abroad. i am pleased that the 2010 eu citizenship report is more thorough than previous reports and that it clearly identifies the most common obstacles that arise, together with some recommendations for overcoming them. on the other hand, i regret that as much as one quarter of the total number of petitions received from citizens concern problems related to free movement, which is one of the fundamental rights of eu citizens, and the concrete expression of european integration in everyday life. i therefore join the call for individual member states to step up their efforts in adopting concrete measures in the field of labour mobility, recognition of qualifications and at the same time improve access to social security entitlements and pension contributions.

one of the basic conditions for the smooth functioning of the free movement of labour within the union was the establishment of rules for the mutual coordination of the social security systems of the member states. the administrative commission for the coordination of social security systems proposes to update the currently valid coordination rules based on regulation no 833 of 2004 and regulation no 987 of 2009 in order to take account of changes in social reality and legal changes in the rules in some member states. of the proposed changes, perhaps the most significant benefit for our citizens is the clarification of the application of the substantive activity condition under article 13 (1) of regulation 833/2004 which will apply in cases where citizens work in two or more member states and will also apply to citizens working for different employers. similarly, the addition of a new provision to this regulation ensuring the protection of the self-employed in the event of loss of employment represents a higher degree of protection against labour market turbulence. however, there is a risk that this provision may be abused and this will need to be monitored closely.

the proposals concerning the coordination of social security systems aim in particular to improve and modernise the acquis, and are also affected by changes in social reality. it is precisely to respond to these changes that improvements are proposed in the area of determining the applicable legislation and unemployment benefits. i would like to clarify that in the case of work in two or more member states, the condition of substantial activity also applies to persons working for different undertakings or employers. the diversity and evolution of the conditions under which professional activities are carried out require that account be taken of the situation of highly mobile workers in particular. i also consider it important to ensure that self-employed persons receive benefits in accordance with the legislation of the member state concerned and that they are given the best possible prospects of reintegration into the labour market when they return to their member state of residence. i am of the opinion that the regulation should be amended accordingly in view of the above.

in writing. − the administrative commission for the coordination of social security systems has made relevant proposals on the coordination of social security systems, aimed at improving and modernising the acquis. the agreed proposals were incorporated into the text of the proposed regulation. the coordination of social security systems may be affected by changes in social reality. in order to respond to these changes, changes are proposed in the area of determining the applicable legislation and unemployment benefits. the diversity and evolution of the conditions under which professional activities are carried out require that the situation of highly mobile workers be taken into account. the new labour supply structures can be observed, among others, in the air transport sector. the establishment of a link between the legislation applicable to aircrew members and the member state in which the registered office or place of business of the undertaking or employer employing them is situated is effective only if there is a sufficiently close link with the registered office or place of business. i also believe that it is necessary to ensure that selfemployed persons receive benefits in accordance with the legislation of the member state concerned and that, on returning to their member state of residence, they are given the best prospects of reintegration into its labour market. regulation (ec) no 883/2004 and regulation (ec) no 987/2009 should therefore be amended accordingly.
in writing. − the free movement of persons is certainly one of the greatest achievements of a common europe. this is also linked to more frequent labour migration. today, it is no exception if a person works in two or more member states for different companies and employers. for this reason, the coordination of the social systems of the member states needs to be changed and updated. i am aware that there will continue to be cases of both workers and unemployed whose complexity of the conditions they have encountered will not be covered by the legislation of the state in question. i supported the motion for a resolution because it responds to the diversity and evolution of the conditions under which professional activities are carried out and takes into account the situations of highly mobile workers.
in writing. − the free movement of persons is one of the fundamental pillars on which the idea of european integration is based. the possibility of working in any member state of the european union allows union citizens to respond more flexibly to changes in labour markets. it also gives people the opportunity to seek the best use of their education and skills regardless of borders. on the other hand, it creates a healthy pressure on employers in smaller member states by exposing them to wider competition. the issue of social security is also closely linked to work. if the single labour market is to function in europe, the social security systems of the individual member states need to be coordinated at european level. however, this harmonisation of systems must respond flexibly to changes in pension and social rules. the proposed amendment to the regulation on the coordination of social security systems is based mainly on the comments of the member states and i therefore supported it in good conscience. i understand the concerns of some of my colleagues about the abuse of social systems in their countries, but i am convinced that rejecting european harmonisation does not solve this problem. generous social support schemes are not sustainable in the long term.
in writing. the treaty of friendship and cooperation in southeast asia was signed in february 1976 by indonesia, malaysia, the philippines, singapore and thailand. since the date of the signature, many countries have also become signatories, including the united states, turkey, and canada. the treaty aims to promote peace, stability and cooperation in the region. to this end, it calls for the peaceful settlement of disputes, the preservation of peace, the prevention of conflict and the strengthening of security in south-east asia. the rules and principles laid down in the treaty correspond to the objectives of the european union as regards the common foreign and security policy. i believe that, as with the common pursuit of international peace and stability in the region, the treaty should also promote active cooperation in the economic, social, technical, scientific and administrative fields, accelerating economic growth in the region, expanding trade and improving economic infrastructure, so that all this pursuit leads to mutual benefit of the countries concerned.

in writing. − a common consolidated corporate income tax base should offer a solution to some of the main tax obstacles to growth in the single market. in fact, without common corporate tax rules, there is often (due to the concurrent operation of national tax systems) excessive and double taxation, a high administrative burden for businesses and high compliance costs. this is a disincentive to investing, which is therefore contrary to the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. the proposed common approach would ensure the consistency of national tax systems but would not harmonise tax rates. the differences between the rates allow a certain degree of tax competition to be maintained in the internal market. i believe that fair competition ensures greater transparency and allows member states to take account of both their competitiveness on the market and their budgetary needs when setting their tax rates. moreover, as the proposed scheme is primarily designed for the needs of companies operating cross-border, it should be a voluntary scheme and should only complement existing national corporate tax systems.
in writing. − the directive on a common consolidated corporate tax base lays down common rules for the calculation of the tax base for companies operating in the european union. each member state shall apply its own tax rate to the share on the basis of the tax which has been allocated to it. harmonisation is limited to the calculation and allocation of the taxable amount. the fixing of tax rates remains a matter for the member states. the system is proposed as optional. companies, whether or not they operate on a cross-border basis, will be able to apply this scheme, but are not obliged to do so. i consider the common consolidated tax base to be a step forward in reducing the administrative burden of doing business in the eu and i support it.

by adopting the stockholm programme, the european council of december 2009 decided that the union should accede to the european convention for the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms. accession of the european union as a regional grouping organisation shall be subject to specific conditions which are different from those defined for the accession of states. it follows from the wording of the treaty of lisbon that legal acts of the union produce their effects on individuals only by means of implementing or implementing national measures. the union's accession to the convention would therefore need to transfer the specific character of the judicial system of the union to the framework of the principles governing the functioning of the control mechanisms established by the convention, in particular the principle of subsidiarity. given the complexity and scale of the changes resulting from accession to the convention, i therefore respect the position of those union states which are not subject to populist pressure to over-accelerate this difficult process.
the treaty of lisbon, which has been in force for almost two and a half years, has become a major milestone in the development of fundamental rights protection not only in the european union but also in europe. the lisbon treaty clearly stated that the european union would accede to the european convention on human rights. i am pleased that this accession will further strengthen and deepen the protection of fundamental human rights and freedoms in the union by giving the european court of human rights in strasbourg the power to review the conformity of union acts with the convention. i would therefore like to express the hope that the remaining legal uncertainties can be resolved without undue delay and that the member states can reach an acceptable agreement so that the european union can accede to the european convention for the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms as soon as possible.
concerns about the reliability and effectiveness of biometric passports in the european union have persisted and no satisfactory solution has been found, although passports have been used in various member states for more than five years. replacing conventional paper passports with biometric ones, which have a special chip with biometric data unique to each individual, was intended to help prevent passports from being falsified. the initial use of hundreds of thousands, some estimates say up to millions of biometric passports to be verified and the issuing of such passports on the basis of false or forged documents, however, indicates that minimum security standards for passports are not sufficient to ensure the authenticity of the document. as this is a matter of internal security and european union law and order, i support the introduction of stricter rules not only on passports themselves but also on the overall procedure for issuing them.

quality education for the growing population is an elementary condition for the dynamic development of society. in the european union, university education has a rich tradition and for young people, studying at a university is not only a matter of social prestige but also a prerequisite for obtaining a good job. however, current economic problems show us that the structure of higher education institutions is not responding to the needs of the changing labour market, resulting in a high percentage of university graduates who are unable to find a suitable job in their field. therefore, more efforts must be made to effectively align higher education institutions with the needs of the labour market so that the structure of the courses they offer is responsive to changing social and economic conditions. support for university and higher education by the states and the european union is necessary, but it should be directed only to those institutions whose graduates find a corresponding place in society after leaving school. we must therefore introduce new and better incentive criteria in the way they are financed.

for the efd group. first of all, it is regrettable to acknowledge the truth of the statement in the report that european policy on biodiversity protection has failed utterly. there are certainly a number of reasons for this failure. i think one of the reasons why the european union's biodiversity policy is failing is that there is a lack of awareness in society about the importance of preserving ecosystems for the future of life on earth. we must therefore be able to convince not only our citizens, but also regional politicians and business managers, that the protection of biodiversity is not incompatible with sustainable and economic growth. increased awareness of the need to protect and conserve ecosystems will generate greater pressure on public authorities as well as on business entities to not tolerate environmental damage through their actions. we also need to invest more in research to better understand the interactions between the different components of ecosystems and to avoid interfering with nature in ways that can cause serious damage to the system. research aimed at the conservation of biodiversity must be multidisciplinary in nature, taking into account not only ecological, climatological or genetic aspects but also social and economic aspects. commissioner, the continued degradation of ecosystems reminds us that we need to be much more agile in our actions to protect biodiversity.
for the efd group. civilization's interference with ecosystems causes irreversible environmental degradation, and therefore our efforts to eliminate the natural damage to the environment are fully legitimate and necessary. the sixth environment action plan, which has provided us with a framework for environmental policy, is coming to an end in july this year and therefore the continuity of european environmental policy needs to be addressed. in the subsequent seventh environment action programme, experience has shown that greater emphasis will need to be placed on substantially strengthening environmental legislation and gradually integrating environmental objectives into all sectoral policies. more emphasis will also need to be placed on the cross-border dimension of environmental protection. the broader thematic strategies should be translated into legislation with defined objectives and timetables in order to effectively monitor and evaluate their impact. in addition to a global environmental policy, we should also work on specific integrated strategies for individual geographical areas or urban agglomerations, taking into account the specific characteristics of their ecosystems. in any event, the seventh environment action programme should be better structured, more precise, more ambitious and more effective in order to make the best use of the experience of the european union's multiannual environmental policy.

in writing. − biodiversity is our life insurance, providing us with food, fresh water and clean air, shelter and medicines, mitigating natural disasters, damage caused by pests and diseases and contributing to climate regulation. it is also natural capital, providing the ecosystem services that underpin our economy. its loss, together with the climate change with which it is inextricably linked, represents the most critical global environmental threat. species are now dying off at an unprecedented rate. this rate is 100 to 1,000 times faster than it would be if they died naturally. and it is primarily human activities that are causing this situation. the continuing and increasing pressures on biodiversity in europe, such as land-use change, over-exploitation of biodiversity and its components, the spread of invasive alien species, pollution and climate change, are either remaining at a constant level or increasing, and at the same time indirect factors affecting biodiversity, such as population growth, limited awareness of biodiversity and the fact that the economic value of biodiversity is not reflected in the decision-making process, are not very conducive to the situation. i believe it is important to reverse the loss of biodiversity and accelerate the eu's transition to a so-called green, resource-efficient economy. and it is this effort that is also an integral part of the europe 2020 strategy.

the commission has repeatedly called on operators in the past to reduce excessively high roaming charges. but the challenges remained unanswered and the eu decided to intervene through price regulation in order to protect consumers. in july 2011, the commission proposed a third roaming regulation in a row. the reform aims to bring down the prices of international calls to the level of national tariffs. healthy competition has not yet developed and customers continue to pay prices that are unreasonably high. the report on the development of the roaming market states that current charges are not flexible enough to prevent users from paying excessively high prices. i think the proposed fee reduction is the right thing to do. if we want the vision of the single internal market to be truly realised, we must tackle the problems of roaming. such action is in line with the europe 2020 strategy, the single market act and also the digital agenda for europe. electronic communications must be universally accessible and available at reasonable prices. i therefore support all measures to eliminate unfair roaming charges. there is no technical justification for continuing roaming. roaming charges should be abolished altogether. we need to make sure that consumers are not being ripped off by the big mobile operators. their profits in this area are disproportionately high.
the high level of roaming charges is a major obstacle for citizens to study or work in another country. the current roaming regulation expires on 30 june 2012. the regulation has significantly reduced prices for both roaming calls and text messages. the effectiveness of regulatory intervention in the market for mobile roaming services should be extended beyond 30 june 2012. the aim is to ensure a substantial reduction in charges and by 2015 there should no longer be any differences between domestic and roaming charges. if, from 1 july 2014, customers can sign a contract for the provision of mobile roaming services, which will be separate from the contract for the provision of national mobile services, we will promote competition in the market for roaming services and this will be a further step forward in the evolution. the retail price regulation will continue until 1 june 2016, but its duration may be extended until the structural measures it introduces are fully effective. the new regulation should continue to regulate roaming charges for calls and text messages and introduce a new essential element: a euro data tariff for retail data roaming services. we need new structural measures to revive competition, with price ceilings maintained as a 'life-saving net' for customers to cover the period until competition itself pushes prices down.

in writing our society has reached a stage where we have to think about the underlying philosophy of intellectual property protection. we are witnessing a growing conflict between private and public interest. on the one hand, a patent as a time-limited monopoly makes it possible to cover the cost of costly research and development. without patent protection, investors' risk would be so greatly increased that many inventions and improvements would never have been made. their authors would not be able to obtain the necessary financial resources. on the other hand, we see that in areas such as agriculture and health, patent protection poses an ethical problem: we see that higher prices for patented crops or medicines prevent their distribution where they could save millions of lives from poverty, disease or death. this conflict is all the more complicated because the private interest and the pursuit of individual well-being through one's own work, including intellectual work, is an integral part of the public well-being. in other words, the well-being of society as a whole will only increase if the well-being of its members increases. it seems to me that we are not ready today to propose a fundamental reform of intellectual property protection, whether it be patents or copyright. so we have no choice but to take small steps. one of them is the distinction between traditional breeding and modern biotechnologies proposed by this parliament.

in writing − if you have in july last year, the dispute settlement body (dsb) of the world trade organisation (wto) adopted the appellate body report and the panel report, which were amended by the appellate body report in the case european communities definitive anti-dumping measures concerning certain iron or steel fasteners originating in china. whether the establishment of a single dumping margin and a single anti-dumping duty for several exporters is inconsistent with the articles of the wto anti-dumping agreement will depend on the existence of certain situations. these may include the existence of corporate and structural links between exporters, such as joint control, ownership and management. furthermore, the existence of corporate and structural links between the state and the exporters. on 19 january 2012, the european union and china agreed that the appropriate timeframe for implementing the recommendations and decisions of the dsb would be 14 months and two weeks from the date on which the dsb received the reports. that reasonable period of time will therefore expire on 12 october 2012. in order to allow the european union to respect a reasonable deadline for the implementation of the recommendations and judgments of the dsb agreed between the union and china, i consider it appropriate that the committee on international trade adopted the draft resolution under the simplified procedure.
in writing − the partnership and cooperation agreement establishing a partnership between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and russia, of the other part, entered into force on 1 december 1997. in october 2007, the european union concluded an agreement with the russian government on trade in certain steel products. the agreement introduced quotas for imports of steel from the russian federation into the eu. with russia's entry into the wto's rules-based multilateral trading system, the eu can expect to benefit from more liberal access to the russian market. any remaining obstacles to bilateral trade in steel products that might continue to exist should be minimal and should only be within the clearly defined scope of wto rules governing such matters as tariffs, applicable trade defence measures, technical standards, specific customs/dispatch procedures, etc. i consider it appropriate to examine and remove any trade and investment barriers that may persist bilaterally following russia's accession to the wto. i am also convinced that it would be in the interest of both parties concerned that trade relations between the eu and russia develop in full compliance with the jointly agreed provisions of the existing bilateral agreements.
in writing − if you have in 2010, russia was the largest exporter of steel to the eu with over 6,5 million tonnes, representing 24% of eu steel imports. however, as a result of russia's accession to the wto on 16 december 2011, the eu no longer has the right to apply import quotas for steel imports. following russia's entry into the wto, the eu is expected to benefit from more open access to the russian market. exports of iron and steel products to russia could increase by around eur 107 million per year. the increase in exports of these products from the eu to russia may also be helped by the reduction of the export duties on scrap iron from the current rate of 15% to a rate of 5% to be introduced within five years of russia's accession to the wto. therefore, i supported the repeal of council regulation no 134/2007 on quotas for imports of steel from russia.
in writing − the commission presented this proposal in april 2011 with the aim of improving legal certainty by broadening access to eu legislation and allowing everyone to rely on the electronic edition of the official journal of the european union (oj) as the official, authentic, up-to-date and complete version. the proposal therefore provides that the electronic edition will constitute the valid issue of the oj, whereas in exceptional and time-limited cases of unexpected interruption of the electronic edition, the printed edition would have legal value. electronic publication of oj was one of the priorities of the hungarian presidency from january to july 2011 in relation to the importance of public access to union legislation. however, in view of the council's reservations on national parliamentary scrutiny procedures, the council's formal request for the european parliament's consent was not sent until 13 march 2012. the council text welcomes the reform of the way in which oj are published, as it guarantees greater legal certainty and better access to union legal acts for citizens. today, almost every user consults the electronic version of eu legislation. it is unacceptable that the electronic version of legal acts is not legally binding. consultation of the printed versions of the official journal is a time-consuming and costly procedure carried out by only some users. the reform will therefore increase legal certainty and reduce the cost of access for citizens and businesses. i am of the opinion that all such reforms should be welcomed by the eu.
in writing. − the adoption of the regulation on the authenticity of the electronic version of the official journal of the european union is another step towards bringing the work of the eu institutions, including the legislative outcome, closer to eu citizens. the legislative process, whose parliamentary phase we have concluded today, was one of the priorities of the hungarian presidency in 2011. in today's fast-paced world, money, energy and time can be saved by having access to official texts in a reliable electronic format, including eu documentation. for the time being, the paper version of the official journal of the eu is the only form of publication that is official and can be consulted by anyone, making it more difficult for authorities and citizens to deal with the issue. the electronic version is for information only. the number of citizens who are interested in the outcome of legislation is increasing, which is why it is important that readers can rely fully on the texts published in the electronic version of the official journal. since 1998, when the official journal of the eu became available in electronic form, the number of paper subscriptions has decreased considerably each year. the credibility of the electronic official journal increases legal certainty, makes the work of the eu institutions more transparent and simplifies the lives of many citizens working under eu law, and improves the efficiency of public administration. i voted for the report as its shadow rapporteur.

in writing. − the commission has repeatedly called on mobile operators in the past to reduce excessively high mobile roaming charges. however, the challenges remained unanswered and the european union decided to intervene through price regulation in order to protect consumers. the proposed reform aims to reduce the prices of international calls from mobile networks to the level of national tariffs. healthy competition has not yet developed and customers continue to pay prices that are unreasonably high. the report on the development of the roaming market states that current charges (apart from specific tariffs) are not sufficiently flexible to prevent users from paying unreasonably high prices in the face of competing national tariffs. i believe that the proposed reduction of the maximum charges is a step in the right direction as part of the gradual abolition of any specific roaming charges. electronic communications are a service of general political interest. they must be universally accessible and available at reasonable prices. that is why i am in favour of all measures to eliminate unfair roaming charges.
in writing − high roaming prices are the result of a lack of competition in the roaming market caused by structural market problems. if no solution is found in effective structural measures, it is necessary to respond with temporary price regulation. however, the price caps should at the same time leave sufficient room for new entrants to enter the market and thus to strengthen competition. the new regulation introduces a new element: a euro data tariff for retail data roaming services. it also introduces the possibility for customers to sign a contract for the provision of mobile roaming services, which will be separate from national mobile services, as from 1 july 2014. the regulation will continue until at least june 1, 2016, and i supported the text of the regulation.
in writing. − millions of citizens in the european union use their mobile phones for everyday communication. the number of these users is increasing almost daily, making it easier to stay in touch. however, most europeans prefer to turn off their mobile phone services when abroad to avoid the high bills that carriers charge. this decline is mainly due to the continued weak competition in the roaming market. excessive roaming charges and the resulting low use of roaming services within the eu are not in the interests of european consumers or the european economy. the current state of affairs is also incompatible with the basic idea of a digital european internal market. the regulation which has just been adopted seeks to find a way out of this situation, which is why i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing - my colleagues. the internet is gradually becoming part of everyone's life. the interest, and unfortunately in many cases the need to be online wherever you are, is growing. i consider roaming charges in the european union, within its single market, to be an unnecessary financial burden on consumers. only the big companies that provide these mobile services benefit. although we have still not managed to completely abolish roaming charges, the s&d group has made significant progress in reducing roaming charges for calls, sms and data. data roaming in particular has caused significant problems for its users. we are constantly seeing cases where inadvertently activating such a service causes a user to incur large debts with the mobile companies. i therefore consider it of the utmost importance to address these problems by fairly regulating the prices of roaming services. by 2014, consumers should pay 65% less for roaming services, but i firmly believe that one day we will be able to abolish these charges completely.
in writing − i supported the roaming regulation, including its amendments, because it introduces structural measures that promote competition. in the financial and economic crisis, mobile operators have been the most prosperous. their massive daily advertising campaign entices people to buy their services many times over without disclosing the prices for individual items, but they offer services in packages where the consumer has no possibility to compare prices for individual services. mobile phones and data transmission have become an indispensable necessity of people's daily lives. therefore, the reduction in data charges and the price of roaming services will certainly be welcomed by all users. the adopted decision also created a choice for consumers between different mobile operators.
in writing. − the purpose of the rotterdam convention, which is being implemented in the european union, is to promote the exchange of information on chemicals traded between the parties to the convention and also to introduce a procedure for granting prior authorisation when a party to the convention exports chemicals to another party to the convention. it was important to change the rules on granting prior authorisation to make it easier for exporters of chemicals to export in cases where there is no response. according to the commission, if a country does not respond to export requests, it could be because the authorities in that country do not feel the need to respond to requirements relating to chemicals that are not covered by the rotterdam convention but only by eu legislation. however, it is also possible that the country has a weaker public administration and is therefore unable to respond in time. i think that in such cases it seems very problematic to allow the export of dangerous chemicals to these countries. if their administration is not able to respond to an export request, it is unlikely that it will be able to protect citizens or the environment from hazardous chemicals. the european union is a leader in environmental legislation and should remain so. i believe it is the union's responsibility to ensure that the chemicals we export do not cause unnecessary damage to human health or the environment.

in writing, the commission recommendation of december 2008 on common guidelines for national sides and the issuance of euro circulation coins sets out common principles for the designs used for national sides of euro circulation coins and for the mutual exchange of information and approval of these designs. as they circulate throughout the euro area, their national graphics processing elements are of general interest. they have a common european party and a different national party. the common european side of the coins contains the name of the single currency and the face value of the coin. the national side of euro coins should bear the name of the issuing member state in a prominent manner so that users of the coin can easily identify the issuing member state if they are interested. the designs on the national sides of the euro coins are decided by the individual participating member states. the issuing member states should inform each other of the new national sides well in advance of the intended date of issue. to this end, issuing member states should submit their designs of euro coins to the commission, which will verify their compliance with this regulation. i consider it important to amend this accordingly.

in writing − if you have the accelerated introduction of double or equivalent hull design requirements for single hull oil tankers is a very important issue. oil spills caused by tanker accidents are a major environmental disaster and a tragedy for marine life. in an effort to protect the environment and learn from past mistakes, the steps leading to the accelerated introduction of double hulls for oil tankers are also reducing the risk of hydrocarbon pollution causing accidents in european waters. in single-hull vessels, the oil in the transport tanks is separated from the seawater only by the plate forming the bottom and sides of the vessel. in the event of damage to this sheet due to a collision or a crash, the contents of the transport tanks may be spilled into the sea and cause widespread pollution. an effective means of eliminating this risk is to cover the transport tank with a second inner sheet at a sufficient distance from the outer sheet. this 'double hull' design protects the transport tanks against accident and reduces the risk of water pollution. i therefore consider it justified to put into practice in the foreseeable future the design requirements for double or equivalent hulls for single hull oil tankers mentioned above.

in writing, the european commission has proposed the creation of a financial transaction tax at eu level. the union is in the midst of an economic and financial crisis and effective instruments must be sought to combat it. the introduction of a financial transaction tax system is one of the effective tools to overcome the crisis. the tax is to be levied on all financial transactions between financial institutions, at least one of which is established in an eu member state. it is more than clear that the financial sector, which has been so far under-taxed by the exemption of most financial services from vat, simply has to contribute a much fairer share. the new financial transaction tax system will involve financial institutions in the costs associated with the crisis and prevent the collapse of the internal market for financial transactions. the introduction of the scheme would raise about eur 57 billion a year, the revenues would be shared between the eu and the member states, and part of the proceeds would become a source of the union's own revenue. this would reduce the national contributions of countries to the eu budget. moreover, the scheme will strengthen the functioning of the single market. it eliminates distortions of competition, discourages financial institutions from risky and speculative financial operations and complements regulatory measures aimed at preventing future crises. i believe that the financial sector must contribute equitably to overcoming the crisis in europe.

in writing − the power of inquiry is an important feature of the powers of scrutiny exercised by parliament. democratic parliaments around the world exercise this power in different ways. in most eu member states, the establishment of committees of inquiry is determined and regulated by the constitution, law or regulation. the treaty of lisbon has now shifted the institutional balance of the union and strengthened the political importance of parliament. article 14 teu clearly states that parliament exercises political control. the treaty also amends the procedure for determining the provisions on the exercise of powers of inquiry. although in the past this was a joint decision of the three main european institutions, the treaty of lisbon clearly gives parliament the right of initiative. however, it still needs to receive the formal approval of the council and the commission. however, as the european parliament is not a court, as such it does not have the power to impose penalties on individual citizens. however, by adopting the treaty of lisbon, all member states also agreed to give it the right to investigate breaches of rules and cases of maladministration in the implementation of union law. i am of the opinion that this should bind them to be able to force their public administration systems to provide assistance to any ep committee of inquiry. at the same time, i consider it right that the final power to take a decision should, however, be vested in parliament, irrespective of the powers conferred on the committee of inquiry for the performance of its duties.
in writing the right of the ep to set up temporary committees of inquiry to investigate suspected breaches of community law or maladministration was raised to primary law by the maastricht treaty. however, since the adoption of the interinstitutional agreement on this matter in 1995, the ep has set up only three committees of inquiry. the powers of these committees have been found to be limited and to require reform. the committees of inquiry must have sufficient resources, access to all the necessary documents and information, and the possibility of summoning any person needed. failure by persons and institutions to comply with obligations should lead to appropriate penalties. the outcome of the inquiry is to be a draft of the remedy as well as a report to the ep. i have endorsed and supported these principles.

rapporteur. − madam president, we can all agree that the gender pay gap should be closed. the question is how? back on 8 march 2010, 10 young female members of the european parliament requested a legislative initiative report on equal pay for equal work, pursuant to rule 42 of the rules of procedure. under this rule, parliament may request the commission to submit a proposal for a new act or to amend the old one. there is a new legal basis here: article 157 of the lisbon treaty and the secondary legislation in force. directive 2006/54 on the implementation of the principle of equal opportunities and equal treatment of men and women in matters of employment and occupation – the so-called recast directive – replaced directive 75/117 on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the application of the principle of equal pay for men and women. even though the deadline for transposition of the recast directive was in 2008, legal experts are of the opinion that only small or no profound changes have been made in member states’ legislation, and that no sanctions have been taken against employers under the directive’s provisions. there is only slow progress. the gender pay gap is currently 16.4% – varying from 4.5% up to 25.5% in individual member states – yet legislation has been in force for almost 40 years. it is obviously not efficient. the question is what to do with an inefficient piece of legislation? we are aware that legislation itself is not enough to tackle the issue, but experience shows that legislation can be improved and better enforced. the gender pay gap is a complex and multifaceted issue with multiple causes, including social and economic factors, such as occupational and sectoral segregation in the labour market, the undervaluing of women’s work, an imbalance between work and private life, and traditions and stereotypes such as the choice of educational paths and employment patterns, to mention only some of them. the explanations account for only half the difference: the remainder is considered as a difference caused by direct and indirect discrimination. what is more, statistics show that the gender pay gap is apparent after women’s return to the labour market following the birth of a first child, and that it grows with age, because of career breaks, but also with educational level. for these reasons, the answer has to be holistic and multi-level. it has to combine legislative and non-legislative measures, both of which are essential. our aim in this report was to identify those areas in legislation where improvement can be made. since the commission has an obligation under article 32 of the recast directive to review the directive and, if appropriate, to propose amendments in 2013, we call on the commission to address the unjust discrimination against women and to make the legislation on diminishing the gender pay gap more effective. improvements based on the best practices of various member states are also requested in selected areas. equal work or work of equal value has to be regarded equally whether it is done by men or women. no excuse can be acceptable.
thank you, mrs. bauer, for your tireless efforts to change the status of women in this issue. the problem of unequal pay has persisted for several decades because neither the commission nor the member states have understood it correctly. they are based on an incomplete answer to the fundamental question of why women actually earn less than men, even when they are in a comparable job. if the reason for this situation were simply the widespread prejudice that women are less productive workers than men, the solution would be to introduce financial penalties and stricter controls on employers. but it's not like that. it's more complicated than that. the real reason is that most women have two jobs: one at work and one at home. getting the man involved in housework is not an absolute solution. nor should pressure on a woman to relinquish her motherly responsibilities to the state be the solution to this natural situation. it is rather to consider whether the unpaid work of a woman mother today is not more valuable to society than if we make her a tractor driver or a manager who will behave like a man in her position if the situation requires it. she will put work before everything else, knowing that her children will be raised by complete strangers from infancy.
despite the fact that various steps are constantly being taken and resources are being spent to address the pay gap, we are making extremely slow progress. it is incredible that even today in some member states of the european union this gap is close to 28%, and in many countries it is still widening. women have to work on average, say, until march 2 this year to earn on average the same wage as men for the calendar year ending december 31. it's hard to believe it's been over two months. these differences stem from direct and indirect discrimination and many other factors. however, we need to improve and simplify the procedures and mechanisms to defend the principle of equal pay for equal work and to prohibit any form of gender discrimination. the commission should also review directive no 54 of 2006, in particular because it does not provide for any sanctions against employers. member states should also aim to increase the transparency of remuneration. commissioner, women are among the groups of society most affected by precarious employment and the effects of the economic and social crisis. i would therefore very much like the commission to take action as soon as possible to eliminate this discrimination.
it is sad that, despite the efforts of the european parliament over many years, discrimination against the vulnerable sections of our population in employment and legal relations still occurs in many countries of the european union. the fact that workers are entitled to equal pay for equal work regardless of age, race, or gender appears to be still unknown to many employers. it is therefore appropriate to continue to seek effective mechanisms to help eliminate unjustified gender pay gaps. however, we have all agreed for some time that the excessive administrative burden on smes in the union is already bordering on bullying. i would therefore suggest that we do not impose additional administrative burdens on smes through this report and that we transfer responsibility for implementing the measure proposed in point 2.3 of part ii of the analysis of the situation and transparency of the results for the public institutions, tax authorities or social insurance companies, which should already have all the necessary data on the wage policy of employers and the employment contracts of their employees.
the rapporteur. − i would like to thank the speakers for their valuable comments and the shadow rapporteurs for their active work. let me just make a few comments. i am very grateful to the commissioner for pointing out that the question of the wage gap is also linked to economic growth and that in 1957 - and i would like to emphasise this - the question of equal pay was not included in the treaty of rome for the sake of equal opportunities or human rights, but as a formulation of equal conditions of economic competition. but beyond that, it's not just an economic issue, it's not just a social issue, it's not just a human rights issue in the first place, but it does have a very far-reaching consequence, and that's what i tried to point out in the report, which is that the first big difference comes after the birth of the first child. it is true that today we are busy with the economic crisis from morning till night, but little is said about the fact that europe is in a deep demographic crisis. what message are we sending by saying that we have a law here that has targeted the wage gap for 50 years and it's not working? i understand the skepticism of my conservative colleagues, but the main issue is that we have a law here that is over 40 years old, we have a principle here that is over 50 years old, and it doesn't work. it's obviously not working. our job is that, even though each actor has a role to play in this area, our job is to look at what can be done in the area of legislation. and i think that's a question that we can't avoid here.
the decision of the swiss authorities in april this year to introduce quantitative quotas on the number of residence permits in switzerland for citizens of eight european union countries violates the agreements that switzerland has signed with the european union in order to enjoy the common benefits of the single market. according to our legal service, the swiss authorities have no legal basis for this measure and the european commission should therefore open negotiations with the swiss partners on the violation of international agreements, in particular the agreement on the free movement of persons of june 1999. i can't believe the swiss authorities are unaware of the possible consequences of their adventurous actions. if the swiss side were to question its contractual basis with the european union merely to avoid having to fulfil its legal obligations towards the union, it would also lose the benefits of cooperation with the european union. i therefore believe that the commission must remind its swiss partners more strongly of its commitments and, of course, ask for the amendment of this regulation.
on 18 april, the swiss government announced that it had unilaterally decided to re-introduce immigration quotas for citizens of eight european union countries, including my country, the slovak republic. moreover, the government indicated that it would review the programme before its expiry in april 2013 and consider extending it for another year. the swiss government is thus in breach of the bilateral agreement between the swiss confederation and the european union as amended by the 2004 protocol. this is discriminatory and the prohibition of discrimination between citizens of the european union is also laid down in article 21 (3) of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the commission notes that the new rules on the right of residence and the right to free movement of workers are not compatible with the internal market. another negative aspect of the decision is that the countries concerned were not informed in advance of this measure. switzerland cannot unilaterally benefit from cooperation with the union and prevent union citizens from benefiting from the swiss economy. i want to thank my colleagues from the non-affected countries for their solidarity and support.
written − eu macrofinancial assistance started in 1990 as macro-economic assistance to third countries experiencing short-term balance of payments difficulties. a total of 55 macro-financial assistance decisions have been approved so far, benefiting 23 countries, for a total of eur 7.2 billion in grants and loans or a combination of both. the eu has so far adopted macrofinancial assistance decisions on the basis of the so-called geneva criteria of october 2002, which have been subject to individual legislative decisions. the ep considered this situation unsatisfactory and in its 2003 resolution called for the development of a regulatory framework, the commission's proposal therefore comes as a direct response to this requirement. in its staff working document, the commission expressed concern about the current state of individual legislative decisions, in particular with regard to the mandatory eight-week consultation of national parliaments. although macro-financial assistance is a valuable contribution to macroeconomic stability in the eu's neighbouring countries, current practices rather reduce its effectiveness and transparency. i believe that certain changes will be required to establish clear rules and to simplify and make macro-financial assistance decision-making more efficient. however, i consider it unacceptable to remove parliamentary control over macro-financial assistance altogether and to introduce implementing acts for it.

the gsp is one of the most important instruments for implementing the european union's policy towards developing countries. the rules currently in force were laid down by a council regulation back in 2008 and, given the considerable dynamics of social and economic development, it is understandable that these rules need to be updated. in the light of the application of the new mechanisms of the legislative procedure under the treaty of lisbon, this regulation must also be subject to the ordinary procedure of the european parliament. although the commission's proposal for a regulation is based on a proven structure of three separate preferential regimes: 1) the standard gsp scheme, 2) the special incentive measures for sustainable development and good governance known as the gsp plus scheme, and 3) the everything but arms measure, the rules and criteria for granting preferences are changing, which is also reflected in the other structure of the beneficiary countries. the list of beneficiary countries is thus reduced to (a) countries with another agreement on preferential terms, such as free trade agreements, (b) overseas countries and territories of the european union, the united states of america and australia, and (c) countries classified by the world bank as high-income countries for three consecutive years, such as kuwait, qatar, saudi arabia, but also brazil or russia. however, the new classification proposed by the commission would also exclude most of the caribbean islands, most of the latin american countries, but also namibia, gabon and algeria from the gsp. at the same time, such rules would temporarily keep rich countries such as china, indonesia and thailand in the gsp. i therefore consider the proposal of the committee on international trade, which recommends the introduction of a transparent system combining several indicators objectively justifying the granting of the benefits of the gsp to selected countries, to be correct and meaningful.

in writing, eur 18 061 682 in commitment and payment appropriations in respect of the floods in italy in october 2011. on 25 october 2011, extreme weather conditions over north-west italy caused heavy rainfall over several hours. the provinces of la spezia in liguria and massa carrara in tuscany were the most affected. the heavy rains caused extensive damage to buildings, businesses and agriculture, and also disrupted major transport links and essential public infrastructure. the cinque terre, an integral part of the italian riviera and a unesco world heritage site, was also affected. following this disaster, italy subsequently submitted an application for financial assistance from the european union solidarity fund. as the total damage does not exceed the normal threshold for mobilising the solidarity fund, the application was assessed on the basis of the criterion of 'exceptional regional disaster'. on the basis of the above, assistance from the fund may exceptionally be granted to a region which has been affected by an exceptional disaster, in particular of a natural nature, affecting the majority of its population and having serious and lasting consequences for living conditions and economic stability in the region. i consider it justified to release financial assistance to disaster-affected areas through the eu solidarity fund.

in writing − sustainable energy supply is a prerequisite for economic development. the energy sector is therefore one of the strategic areas requiring tactical action focused on energy security and sustainability. however, the right energy mix, with renewables starting to make inroads, together with energy efficiency and other small-scale solutions, is not an integral part of the answer to the question of the energy dependence of many member states on energy supplies from outside the eu. in my view, the union should not only cultivate its relations with its traditional partners, such as russia, but should also gradually establish deeper strategic cooperation in energy with the countries bordering the black and caspian seas, the middle east, the mediterranean and central asia. of course, we must not forget the improvement of the functioning of the internal market, where unfortunately many barriers to competition persist, making the eu market less attractive to suppliers and investors outside europe. i agree that the eu and the member states must ensure an internal energy market that resists external pressures and attempts to use energy supplies and prices as a tool for external political pressure. i therefore believe that when the eu budget is being planned, resources should be increased for projects linking energy markets within the eu and for improving the european gas and electricity infrastructure network.
in writing, europe is the largest buyer of energy in global energy markets. this position is to some extent a very big handicap. the reason is the continuous creation of energy dependence on third countries. it is precisely because of the low self-sufficiency that relations with our partners - energy suppliers - are very important. member states are the biggest importers and if we use this fact at european union level in a common and coordinated way and take a firm bargaining position against third countries, we will almost always have a good bargaining position as a strong player on the demand side of the market. ensuring reliable and cost-effective access to global energy resources is therefore crucial to promoting europe's competitiveness and security in view of the eu's policy objectives set out in the 2020 package. it is also necessary to achieve our environmental objectives, such as meeting the commitment to decarbonise the economy by 2050.

written − the european union has granted trade preferences to developing countries through the generalised system of preferences (gsp) since 1971. the scheme is one of the key trade instruments providing assistance to developing countries in their efforts to ensure basic human and labour rights, reduce poverty and promote sustainable development and good governance in developing countries. the increased trade volume has integrated many developing countries and exporting sectors into the world market. in order to ensure better protection of the eu's financial and economic interests and to increase legal certainty, stability and predictability, the administrative procedures for the individual safeguard mechanisms are also improved. the new regulation is based on increased transparency and predictability, including applicable procedures and rights of defence. i am convinced that they will better protect the eu's financial and economic interests and increase legal certainty and stability. it is important to bear in mind that preferential access to the eu market is one of several factors that allow development to be sustained through trade. and it is this new gsp regulation that aims to achieve greater simplicity, predictability and better targeting of the eu gsp system so as to achieve its maximum effectiveness, all the procedures proposed being also in line with the un priorities for fighting world poverty.
written − since 1971, the eu has granted non-reciprocal trade preferences in the form of reduced tariffs on goods entering the european market from developing countries under the gsp. in 2009, the value of eu imports under this scheme was around eur 60 billion, representing 4% of total eu imports. the new rules, adopted under the lisbon treaty under the ordinary legislative procedure, are designed to reduce the number of beneficiary countries from 186 to 80. the so-called more developed countries, which are currently the most favoured and account for around 40% of the eu's preferential imports, will be excluded. the new regulation will also include a series of guarantee and control measures, and will also redefine the procedures leading to the application of safeguard clauses and decision-making procedures. i fully supported the motion.

in writing − the proposal for a regulation on strengthening economic and budgetary surveillance of member states in serious difficulties is set against the background of the financial and public debt crises currently facing the eu. the commission's proposals complement the package of six european economic governance rules adopted by the ep and the council in 2011. the main thrust of the commission's proposal is to make it compulsory for a member state whose currency is the euro to be subject to enhanced surveillance if it is experiencing or is threatened with serious financial difficulties. in the interest of rapid response, it should be the responsibility of the commission to take the necessary decisions, which include the procedure of enhanced surveillance of the member state. the council could reject this procedure by simple majority within 10 days. i supported the proposal in the ep's comments.
in writing − if you have the treaty on the functioning of the european union requires member states to regard their economic policies as a matter of common concern, to have their budgetary policies guided by the need for sound public finances and to ensure that their economic policies do not jeopardise the proper functioning of economic and monetary union. the treaty allows specific measures to be taken in the euro area, going beyond the provisions applicable to all member states, in order to ensure the proper functioning of economic and monetary union. the establishment of a common budgetary timetable for member states whose currency is the euro should better synchronise the key steps in the preparation of national budgets, thus contributing to the effectiveness of the european semester for the coordination of budgetary policies. however, biased and unrealistic macroeconomic and budgetary forecasts can significantly impede the effectiveness of budgetary planning and, consequently, weaken the commitment to budgetary discipline. on the contrary, the forecasts of independent bodies can provide unbiased and realistic macroeconomic forecasts. at the same time, a timely correction of any deviations indicating excessive deficits in member states should be ensured through more rigorous monitoring. i am also convinced that a gradually extended monitoring procedure will contribute to better budgetary outcomes for all member states whose currency is the euro.

written − the european union is establishing social legislation in road transport to increase road safety, improve working conditions for drivers and ensure fair competition between transport undertakings. this regulation lays down harmonised maximum daily and weekly driving times and minimum daily and weekly rest periods for drivers. at the same time, the union has developed a comprehensive policy of inspections and controls on compliance with social legislation in road transport. this policy has two basic pillars - one is the directive setting a minimum level of roadside checks and on-the-spot checks to be carried out by member states, and the other is the tachograph regulation. the commission has identified two problems in the current system that need to be addressed at union level: social rules are too often violated and the tachograph system is not effective enough. in july last year, the european commission proposed a revision of the tachograph regulation, with the aim of making fraud more difficult, better enforcing social rules and reducing the administrative burden through the full use of new technologies and the introduction of several new regulatory measures. i am convinced that none of the objectives of the proposal will be easily achieved unless the member states commit themselves to improving the enforcement of this regulation, which needs to be amended accordingly.
written − regulation (ec) no 561/2006 provides for harmonised maximum daily and weekly driving times and minimum daily and weekly rest periods for drivers. these rules apply to all drivers of goods vehicles over 3,5 tonnes and to drivers of passenger vehicles over 9 and more passengers. according to commission figures, on average 9% of vehicles inspected are found to be in breach of social rules. about a quarter of them are tachograph violations. an average of 45 000 vehicles are in breach of eu tachograph rules at any given time. companies that do not comply with the legislation gain a competitive advantage, as personnel costs represent 30 to 50% of operating costs. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of electronic data-processing systems, such as the electronic data-processing system, and to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of electronic data-processing systems.

in writing - water is essential for life. it is demonstrably the most important of all public goods. urbanization, population growth, overconsumption, biological and chemical pollution, hydromorphological changes and climate change are putting increasing pressure on the availability and quality of safe and secure water. future economic growth cannot be sustainable if it is associated with adverse environmental impacts on water. current water legislation provides a solid framework for sustainable and efficient water management. the water framework directive, adopted in 2000, in particular, can be seen as a milestone in european water management. however, the pace of implementation of this directive in european countries and regions is slow with very mixed results. i consider it important to promote the issue of water in all policy areas. the protection of water resources, with particular reference to drinking water, needs to be addressed in a global perspective, taking into account all ecosystem services supported by water. also, climate change mitigation and adaptation policies must always take into account the impact on water resources, and the eu should address this issue in a comprehensive way. i am of the opinion that decisive action at eu level will be needed to address the current and future water management challenges facing europe.
in writing − the need for a comprehensive approach to european water problems is of the utmost relevance. water is the basis of every ecosystem, and its efficient use and protection must also be a priority for european legislation. the annual floods, weather fluctuations, extreme droughts, landslides are all the result of poor water management and inefficient use in the energy and agriculture sectors, which are the largest water users. protecting the soil is a key element in maintaining water quality, but also water supply. in view of biodiversity, rapid afforestation of areas that have been subject to frequent flooding in recent years in individual member states is necessary. we know the causes of water mismanagement, but we do little to save it. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution text so that decisive eu action in this area can contribute to the protection of waters and biodiversity.
in writing − if you have more than 40,000 people die each year in traffic accidents. 150,000 people will suffer an accident resulting in permanent disability. meanwhile, according to estimates by the world bank and the world health organization, road traffic accidents are expected to increase in all parts of the world and will be the third leading cause of death by 2020. these predictions are alarming. the european union cannot stand by and watch such adverse developments. that is why i am in favour of the introduction of a pan-european ecall system. indeed, official statistics estimate that the full integration of ecall in vehicles in the eu member states will save 2 500 lives a year, while reducing the severity of injuries by 10 to 15%. this will be achieved by faster arrival of emergency services at the scene of an accident, ecall will reduce congestion times and contribute to the efficiency of road transport across the eu. in addition, the service will allow support for many other commercial services increasing safety and economic benefits. at the same time, it is equally important to ensure that the system is in full compliance with the relevant data protection and privacy regulations. also, if the service is to fulfil its purpose, namely to reduce the number of deaths and the severity of injuries in road accidents, it must in any case be free of charge, for the benefit of all drivers, regardless of the make of the motor vehicle.
in writing − in the event of a serious accident, a vehicle equipped with ecall will automatically initiate an emergency call and send an emergency message containing basic information on the time, location, direction of travel and vehicle description. this improves the efficiency of the rescue services. the introduction of the system requires car manufacturers to install an on-board system capable of triggering ecall, mobile network operators to enable the transmission of ecalls and member states to modernise their emergency call centres. in 2011, the commission adopted a recommendation calling for appropriate measures to be taken for the deployment of ecall by the end of 2014. the ep asks that the recommendation be followed up by a delegated act, with a deadline for adoption by the end of 2012, in the form of a directive that will bindingly define the necessary specifications. i agree with the ep's position.
in writing. − each year, 39 000 people die in traffic accidents in the eu and more than 1.2 million passengers are injured. these alarming statistics point to the fact that road safety concerns every eu citizen. our task is therefore to support proposals that would reduce road fatalities and take a step forward in road safety. ecall is one of the modern intelligent traffic safety systems whose task is to automatically call the emergency services in the event of an accident, without any effort being required by the driver who may be injured or unconscious. the quick and timely response of rescuers is often crucial. in the case of serious injuries, every minute counts. ecall is a major challenge for eu transport policies. given the time it has taken the eu to work out the details of the system, it is high time that it was finally harmonised in all member states by 2003. the only negative aspect may be the slightly increased cost of purchasing the motor vehicles, but it should be noted that in the case of series production this would be a marginal amount, which is negligible in comparison with the number of lives saved.
