in writing, the treaty of lisbon abolishes the old comitology system, which was based on the classic comitology procedures (consultation, management and regulatory procedure) and the regulatory procedure with scrutiny. this system is now being replaced by a two-tier structure consisting of delegated and implementing acts (the first of which also includes the right of veto of the parliament) which allow the commission to exercise powers of introduction and implementation. the existing body of legislation therefore needs to be brought into line with this new legal reality. one of the first proposals is to align the current draft regulation amending council regulation (ec) no 73/2009 establishing common rules for direct support schemes for farmers under the common agricultural policy and establishing certain support schemes for farmers. the proposal contains adjustments in terms of harmonisation but also simplifies the said regulation. the proposal also contains a number of provisions aimed at simplifying the current legislative environment and reducing the administrative burden for member states. in the interests of greater legal clarity and certainty, i support the proposed amendments.
in writing − if you have council regulation (ec) no 1698/2005 confers powers on the commission to implement certain provisions of that regulation. as a consequence of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the powers conferred on the commission in accordance with regulation (ec) no 1698/2005 need to be aligned with articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. pursuant to article 290 of the treaty (delegated acts), the legislator may, if appropriate, delegate to the commission the power to adopt non-legislative acts of general application to supplement or amend certain non-essential elements of a legislative act. as regards article 291 of the treaty (implementing acts), the legislator shall confer on the commission the power to adopt uniform conditions for the implementation of legally binding acts of the european union. in addition, some simplification elements are introduced in the current regulation, support is extended to the areas referred to in article 10 of the natural habitats and wildlife directive under natura 2000, and the number of annual progress reports and summary reports is reduced under the rural development programme, cross compliance checks are simplified and the rules for the use of advisory services are changed, and these elements should help to reduce the administrative burden on member states.

written − the eu-russia agreement on the maintenance of the commitments on trade in services contained in the eu-russia cooperation and partnership agreement is placed in the context of the new legal framework following russia's recent accession to the world trade organisation. the timetable for the liberalisation of trade in services contained in the multilateral package on russia's accession to the wto will provide significantly greater market access opportunities for foreign service providers. russia has agreed to reduce barriers to trade and investment and will ensure more favourable treatment of foreign service providers than in the past in 11 sectors, including professional services, information technology services, construction, postal services, telecommunications, media, transport, distribution, tourism and travel services and financial services. trade in services currently represents around 20% of european exports to russia. these commitments by russia will not only create more business opportunities for european businesses, but will also improve the situation for eu exporters and investors currently working with russia, including in the area of non-discrimination and free competition. increased competition should bring more services and a higher quality of services in russia in many areas, which could make it easier for all european companies established in russia to do business. i think it is appropriate for parliament to give its consent to the agreement.
in writing. − the government of the russian federation has been trying for several years to attract foreign manufacturers of automobiles and related components to its territory in order to offset the decline of its own automobile industry and to provide jobs for the workforce of this sector. under the terms of russia's accession to the wto agreed in november 2011 and approved by the european council, its automotive investment programme will be exempted from ensuring that all laws, regulations and other measures in force in the russian federation relating to trade and investment are, by 1 july 2018, in conformity with the provisions of the wto agreement, including the agreement on trade-related investment measures. the eu must accept this agreement as it is binding on its wto commitments. russia's accession to the wto will involve, inter alia, the implementation of the other commitments that membership brings, such as reforms in the associated areas of regulation and tariff reductions, from which eu producers would benefit immensely. finally, global external factors such as global demand for cars and global growth as well as domestic aspects in russia such as infrastructure development and business environment, all these factors can have a positive and negative impact on the growth of eu-russia trade in cars and motor vehicle components, which is difficult to estimate.
in writing, − the russian federation has undertaken to progressively reduce or eliminate its current export duties on specified raw materials in connection with its accession to the wto. these commitments concerning export duty rates are included in the list of concessions and commitments by russia concerning goods. the urgency and importance of a legally binding agreement on raw materials is clearly demonstrated by the recent ban on imports of livestock from any eu member state imposed by russia following the spread of the schmallenberg virus and bluetongue virus, even though such a ban is in clear breach of the rules of the world trade organisation. the introduction of this ban suggests that russia's approach has not changed much even after its accession to the wto. without a strong and legally binding bilateral agreement on raw materials, the eu will have no assurance that similar protectionist measures will not be taken in the future. the eu is russia's largest trading partner and largest investor in the country. it is therefore expected that a sufficiently serious commitment will be made to implement without delay the reforms required by wto accession, reciprocity and a commitment to negotiate a mutually beneficial new agreement, in particular in the areas of energy, trade and investment. i believe that parliament should give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement.
in writing negotiations on a trade agreement to combat counterfeiting started in june 2008 and ended in november 2010 after 11 rounds of negotiations. as with all international agreements, the european commission negotiated on behalf of the european union on the basis of a mandate given to it by the council. as the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement is a so-called mixed agreement, involving competences at both union and member state level, the member states were represented by rotating presidencies in the negotiations. the agreement was concluded by the european union, australia, canada, japan, korea, mexico, morocco, new zealand, singapore, switzerland and the united states of america. the agreement is, as defined by the negotiators, a trade agreement that addresses counterfeiting for commercial purposes and internet piracy by coordinating the global enforcement of existing copyright infringement legislation. the problems it is intended to address are real and are on the increase. counterfeiting and piracy have become widespread and continue to grow. the potential threats to civil liberties far outweigh the intended benefits of this international agreement. in view of the ambiguity of certain aspects and the uncertainty surrounding its interpretation, the european parliament cannot guarantee adequate protection of civil rights in the future after the entry into force of this agreement. for this reason too, it is not recommended that the european parliament should give its consent to its conclusion.

for the efd group. according to the practice hitherto followed in the fisheries sector, the country whose flag the vessel flies is responsible for the vessel's activities. in the case of a chartered vessel, the state in which the vessel is chartered shall be responsible for the operation of such vessel. however, in the context of the updating of the conventions on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora, a discussion has been opened on a fundamental change to that rule, so that the country in which the vessel is owned is responsible for the activities of the chartered vessel. i admit that i have some doubts that the states which have contractually leased a vessel to another state would be able to control effectively the activities carried out by that vessel. as an example, i could mention my country, which is located in the heart of europe, has no access to the sea but has its own navy. of course, it has no effective means of controlling these ships, since they are chartered and operated by other countries. it therefore seems to me that accepting the proposed change in liability for the activity of a chartered vessel in the convention would allow a legal situation to be established in which no one would actually bear any real liability for the activity of chartered vessels.

in writing. - the court has submitted a draft regulation to allow the appointment of substitute judges to the civil service tribunal of the european union. the civil service tribunal shall consist of seven judges. it follows that his activity may be seriously jeopardised if one of them falls ill or is unable to perform his duties for a long period. in order to ensure that the civil service tribunal does not find itself in a situation where it cannot perform its judicial functions, it has been proposed to allow the admission of substitute judges to the specialised courts. the substance of the proposal is that the council, on a proposal from the president of the court of justice, should draw up a list of three persons proposed as judges-rapporteurs. they shall be appointed for a period of four years, with the possibility of reappointment. they shall enjoy the privileges of a judge only in dealing with the case assigned to them. this means that the judges-rapporteurs could only perform judicial functions and could not take part in the administration of the civil service tribunal or in the election of the president of the court of justice or the presidents of chambers. in my view, the proposal before the court appears to be a reasonable solution to a practical problem which might otherwise seriously impede the functioning of the european union civil service tribunal.

tissue and cell donation mechanisms and systems are, like healthcare, the responsibility of the member states. therefore, mechanisms for tissue and cell donation vary from country to country. and they do not always correspond to article 3 (2) (c) of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which prohibits the exploitation of the human body and its parts for profit. the legal provisions in force in some member states which allow the payment of compensation to relatives for giving consent to the donation of tissues and cells of a deceased relative are manifestly contrary to that ethical principle. it is therefore important that only voluntary and unpaid donation based on the active expression of consent by a potential donor be considered legitimate in the union. only fair and transparent rules on voluntary free donation of tissues and cells under public control, the breach of which will be punishable by criminal law, will prevent the misuse of the human body and its parts for trafficking. it is therefore our duty to demand that all the countries of the european union do so.
half of the member states face a regular shortage of human tissues and cells, particularly bone marrow, or tissues such as cornea and skin. it is of particular ethical importance to ensure an adequate supply of tissues and cells needed for medical purposes. this is a sensitive issue. donations should be voluntary and anonymous. donor benefits should be carefully defined and limited to reimbursing the costs associated with the donation, such as healthcare costs. it should also be guided by protective legal and ethical principles that respect the inviolability of the person. however, many reports indicate that the principle of free donation is being repeatedly violated. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which is legally binding, prohibits the exploitation of the human body and its parts for profit. free donation is therefore not only an ethical principle but also necessary to protect the health of the donor and the recipient, given that large sums of money involved in the donation process can encourage the donor to take risks and can prevent the disclosure of risks in his medical history.

the european union has committed itself to finalising the establishment of a common european asylum system in 2012. the aim is a common area of protection and solidarity, based on common asylum procedures and a uniform legal status for persons granted international protection. ensuring the proper functioning of the seas is of particular importance in the present day. migration flows are most often mixed and include migrants, asylum seekers, refugees and vulnerable persons, such as unaccompanied minors. the flows of asylum seekers and migrants have their own characteristics which cannot be ignored or combined under any circumstances. member states are currently unable to deal adequately with asylum applications lodged on their territory. we therefore need to address asylum issues in a holistic way across the european union, through better division of competences, increased mutual trust, practical cooperation, technical assistance and financial solidarity.
the increased number of mediterranean migrants during the arab spring highlighted the gaps in european asylum policy. the logical response of the southern european countries, which were the most affected by the migration wave, was to demand that the material and organisational burden of the influx of migrants be redistributed to other countries of the union. as is often the case in life, a seemingly simple solution may not always produce good results. asylum seekers come to europe with the hope of continuing their lives in more dignified and civilized conditions. they know that the language of the former colonial power, which they learned at home and at school, will make it easy for them to communicate and integrate into the population of a certain part of europe. but if we tell a french-speaking family from algeria or an english-speaking family from india or egypt that their new asylum home is to be estonia or romania, we are putting them in front of a very difficult language barrier that is going to make them very impatient and complicate their ability to integrate in their new environment. in order to deal with the sensitive and humanitarian situation of asylum seekers, we should leave it to them to decide which part of the union they wish to settle in and help them integrate into society where they can do so most easily.

written − the commission's proposal for the granting of aid to winegrowers under the single payment scheme is part of the cap reform. the commission proposal aims to amend regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 on the common organisation of the market in wine, which allows member states to grant untied aid to wine-growers under the single payment scheme under their national programmes for wine-growers. under the existing provision, member states may adjust their support programmes once a year (for 5 years) in respect of the part of the appropriations allocated to the single payment scheme. the commission proposal requires member states to take a final decision on the transfer of funds from the budget allocated to the wine sector to the single payment scheme by the end of this year. payment claims under the single payment scheme shall be granted for an unlimited period and shall be known in advance in order to ensure predictability for farmers. the ep and the council agreed to change the five-year measure to a one-year measure valid for 2014 only and to provide for the possibility to make a one-off transfer of funds from 2015. the agreement is an acceptable solution in order to maintain the flexibility of decisions within the wine sector without being disrupted by the outcome of the 2013 cap reform.

in writing. − if you have since 2008, the internal market information system (imi) has been provided to the member states as a free service. it aims to improve the exchange of information within the internal market. the system has proven to be a fast and secure way of exchanging information and administrative cooperation across borders and currently has over 6 000 bodies registered from all eu member states and european economic community countries. the current proposal for a regulation aims to improve the conditions for the functioning of the internal market through an efficient and user-friendly tool enabling the practical implementation of administrative cooperation and information exchange. the regulation is based on two parts. one laying down rules for the use of imi for administrative cooperation, the other laying down basic rules for data protection. it is for the sake of better functioning that it is important to provide a coherent legal framework for imi.
in writing − the council directive on a common system of taxation applicable to interest and royalty payments made between associated companies of different member states has been amended several times in recent years. however, in the interests of clarity and accountability, it is still necessary to adjust the technical details. current estimates suggest that tax evasion and avoidance is costing european union governments a significant amount of money in the form of uncollected taxes. as a result of the loss of revenue, the deficit and debt of individual member states are growing. cooperation between the tax systems of the member states is increasingly desirable. the directive needs to be amended to further exclude the possibility of unintentional non-taxation, double taxation or tax avoidance in member states that distorts the proper functioning of the internal market.

in writing the european agricultural sector uses safe, clean and environmentally friendly methods to produce quality products that meet consumer requirements. the regional diversity of food and traditional production methods, some of which date back centuries, the emphasis on safety and good environmental conditions all contribute to the fact that the quality of european food is among the highest in the world. this quality-oriented approach can help to value the highest quality products in domestic as well as international markets. the eu has established a set of labels and quality systems within its food quality policy that recognise the high value characteristics of products as well as regional product specifications. the new quality legislative proposals put forward by the commission will improve union legislation on quality as well as on the operation of national and private certification schemes. they aim to make them simpler, more transparent, more understandable, to be adaptable to innovation and to be less burdensome for producers and managers. this will make the european quality system clearer and more comprehensive.

the european union has an exceptionally rich cultural heritage, but unfortunately most of it lies unused in the archives and libraries of the member states and is not accessible to european citizens. in order to preserve the diversity of european culture, it is therefore necessary to make those works accessible at cross-border level. orphan works are works for which the copyright holder cannot be identified or traced. so we don't get into a conflict with copyright ownership either. however, in accordance with the principles of copyright, making a work available to the public requires the authorisation of the rightholder. while the european legislation currently in force provides for certain exceptions that allow for scanning for conservation purposes, it does not permit and does not allow libraries to make such digitised works available online on the internet, even for non-commercial purposes. but we live in a digital age. the rational dissemination of information online has enormous benefits for the internal market. the digitisation of cultural material should also be supported at european level. the european parliament has already expressed its support for the idea of finding a legislative solution to the problem of these so-called orphan works. the new legislation will in future allow for europe-wide online access to these works. the commission's proposal is therefore more than welcome. copyright is the basis for innovation, creation, investment and production in the creative industries. however, we need to improve the current system and adapt it to today's digital world. the online availability of orphan works across the union will lead to the promotion of europe's cultural diversity and to the expansion of knowledge and learning resources.
the report is a good starting point for ensuring that europe's cultural heritage is not only accessible in a limited way. thanks to the legislative process launched recently at eu level in the field of copyright and the cultural and creative industries, europe is catching up and this has a positive impact on our competitiveness. we are also trying to meet the need for orphan works, which will make it easier for researchers, students and eu citizens to do their jobs. the digital world often knows no boundaries. an appropriate union legal framework, on the other hand, can provide protection for copyright holders and users. the parliament has added substantial elements to the proposal, such as the extension of its scope to cover photographic works of art. the directive aims to reduce the information and knowledge gap between the united states and europe. in future, it would be better to emphasise that the european legislator does not just look for reactions to policies outside the eu. the european legal culture has the potential to provide a well-functioning, modern legal framework for cross-border cases.
for the efd group a basic prerequisite for the proper functioning of the legal system is a simple and clear structure of rules that are understandable to the public and are easily enforceable. the repeated comments by national parliaments on the rules adopted by the european institutions point to the fact that we do not always succeed in achieving this quality of rules. the most common criticism is that the european institutions do not respect the principle of subsidiarity and proportionality when they legislate. the ambiguity of the legal language and the lack of transparency of the legal system, where regulations in some areas even overlap, are also often criticised. it is therefore necessary to continue efforts to improve legislation at european level, both through better cooperation with national parliaments and through more efficient use of electronic communication through the ipex and regpex websites. our efforts to simplify and make the legal system in the union more transparent must be seen as a continuous process and must be given constant attention.
for legislation to be effective at european union level, it must first be clear, simple, easy to understand and accessible to all. when european legislation is drawn up, the two fundamental principles of european union law, namely the principle of subsidiarity and the principle of proportionality, must be respected. i believe that we must also involve the national parliaments of the member states in the european legislative process in a much greater way, since the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality play an important role in the context of control. the european institutions must also simplify and consolidate their efforts to better draft and simplify european union legislation and to reduce administrative and regulatory burdens. our aim is to ensure that european legislation is as close to the citizen as possible and, in particular, that it is understood. nor must we forget that the principle of subsidiarity can lead to the extension of the union's action within its competence, if circumstances so require, or, conversely, to the limitation or reduction of the action concerned, if it is no longer justified. subsidiarity in this context concerns not only the relationship between the european union and its member states but also the regional and local levels.

in writing. − the atlantic region is characterised by several features: it is a dynamic maritime area thanks to renewable sources of marine energy, maritime transport, the maritime industry, tourism and fisheries; it is an area with a vulnerable marine environment that needs to be protected; it is an area that is the western gateway to the european union and is therefore strategic for europe; and it is an outermost region of the european union, which raises the question of its accessibility and connectivity with the rest of europe. these problems transcend national borders and require policy solutions that apply to the entire atlantic coast.
in writing. − the cotonou agreement sets out the conditions for the conclusion of economic partnership agreements between members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states and the eu and its member states. the detailed conditions were laid down in council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007, the so-called market access regulation. this regulation regulates the eu import regime applicable to the 36 african, caribbean and pacific states that initialled economic partnership agreements in 2007. it was a bridging solution for countries that could not yet apply these epas as they were awaiting ratification. several countries have not taken the necessary steps to ratify the epa or to conclude comprehensive regional negotiations. the european commission therefore proposes that those countries which have not yet signed or ratified the agreements be removed from the list of those affected by this provision. the european commission argues that the current situation is not compatible with wto rules and that it is also a question of fairness both towards countries that have fulfilled their commitments and ratified their agreements and towards developing countries that are not african, caribbean and pacific partners.
in writing. − the european union is heavily dependent on energy imports. more than 50% of the eu's total energy needs are imported, with gas and oil even more so. the eu's energy security is therefore sensitive to irregularity in energy supplies from outside the union. in addition, energy imports account for 6% of total eu imports and are associated with high economic costs and risks for the eu economy. it is in the interest of the eu and the member states that external energy relations be governed by intergovernmental agreements and that the negotiating power of the member states and their extensive internal market be strengthened through the exchange of information and best practices between the member states and the commission. intergovernmental agreements can therefore, especially when well coordinated between member states, increase the eu's competitiveness.
in writing. − stable and secure energy supplies are essential to fostering the development of a predictable economic environment for eu citizens and industry. the common energy supplies can best be secured through a functioning internal energy market. the introduction of the third energy package has contributed to the liberalisation of the energy market. many member states have decoupled energy production from its transport, thus enabling new players to enter the energy supply market and significantly increasing its liquidity. external vulnerabilities persist, however, as the eu imports 60% of its natural gas and 80% of its oil. the import rate is thus increasing. the challenges of secure energy supplies at competitive prices, including intergovernmental agreements between member states and third countries in the field of energy, must therefore be addressed. the commission's right to participate in such negotiations can make the outcome more effective.
in writing. − european agriculture produces high quality food and its production methods are environmentally and rural-friendly. the regional diversity of food and traditional production methods, the emphasis on safety and good environmental conditions all contribute to the fact that the quality of european food is among the highest in the world. a quality-oriented approach can help to value the highest quality products in domestic as well as international markets. the quality package presented by the commission aims to improve union legislation on quality, as well as on the operation of national and private certification schemes, to ensure that they are simpler, more transparent, more understandable, can be adapted to innovation and are less burdensome for manufacturers and administrators.
in writing. − the quality package presented by the commission aims to improve the union's quality legislation and also the transposition of internal and private certification systems, with the aim of ensuring that they are simpler, more transparent and more understandable, that they are capable of enabling innovation and that they are less burdensome for producers and managers. the package includes two draft regulations on quality schemes for agricultural products and on marketing standards and two guidance documents on certification schemes and on the labelling of foodstuffs with protected designations of origin and protected geographical indications. the commission's proposal can be seen as a good starting point for making the european quality system clearer and more comprehensive.
in writing. − the proposed regulation creates a legal framework within which various investment funds can be granted the designation 'european social entrepreneurship fund' and the corresponding 'authorisation'. the aim is to create a european sector for investing in legal entities carrying out non-profit-making activities aimed at fulfilling various objectives of a social nature. i support the commission's legislative initiative for a number of reasons. today, investors are increasingly seeking social goals, not just financial returns. a market for social investment is thus emerging in the european union, partly constituted by investment funds targeting social enterprises. such investment funds shall provide funding to social enterprises that act as drivers of social change by offering innovative solutions to social problems, helping to address the social consequences of the financial crisis and contributing in a valuable way to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives.
in writing − the proposal for a regulation establishes the legal framework under which different types of investment funds can obtain the status of 'european venture capital fund' and a venture capital licence. it aims to create a european venture capital investment sector for smes. the draft regulation lays down the criteria in relation to the available assets that such a fund must meet in order to obtain that status and authorisation. it also lays down requirements to be met by managers of venture capital funds and limits on the ability to invest the assets of the fund.
in writing. − the objective of the bilateral safeguard instrument is to provide a safety net if the industry needs time to adapt to new conditions as a result of the trade liberalisation provided for in the free trade agreement. the instrument will therefore only be applicable for a temporary period of 10 years from the entry into force of the agreement or slightly longer for products which have been liberalised for more than 10 years. the provisions proposed by the european commission for the bilateral safeguard clause of the trade agreements with peru and colombia are very similar to the model regulation implementing the bilateral safeguard clause of the eu-republic of korea free trade agreement, which was the first safeguard regulation for which the european parliament acted as co-legislator. this means that issues that were very important to the european parliament at the time, such as surveillance measures, factors to be taken into account in an investigation, and an online platform for more intensive information exchange, are all part of the proposal.
in writing. − on 22 march 2011, the european commission signed an association agreement with six countries in central america (costa rica, el salvador, guatemala, honduras, nicaragua and panama). the negotiations were conducted in parallel with the negotiations on the trade agreement with colombia and peru and were very similar in character. both agreements consolidate some of the concessions granted to these countries by the eu under the gsp plus system and, in addition, liberalise, in whole or in part, trade in certain agricultural products between the parties. the agreements contain a safeguard clause which needs to be transposed into european law in order to avoid serious distortions of the markets concerned.
in writing. − the european union has an exceptionally rich cultural heritage. however, most of this heritage lies unused in the archives and libraries of the member states and is not accessible to european citizens. in order to preserve the diversity of european culture, it is therefore necessary to make those works accessible at cross-border level. orphan works are works for which the copyright holder cannot be identified or traced. however, in accordance with the principles of copyright, the making available of a work to the public requires the authorisation of the rightholder. while the european legislation currently in force provides for certain exceptions that allow scanning for conservation purposes, it does not allow libraries to make digitised works available online on the internet, even for non-commercial purposes. but we live in a digital age. the rational dissemination of information online has enormous benefits for the internal market. the digitisation of cultural material should also be supported at european level. the european parliament has already expressed support in the past for the idea of finding a legislative solution to the problematic issue of orphan works. new legislation will in future allow europe-wide online access to such orphan works.
in writing. − the commission proposal, presented following the unprecedented floods that devastated large parts of pakistan last summer, seeks to extend autonomous trade preferences to the country and covers 75 product groups important to pakistan's exports (mostly textiles and clothing) by exempting them from duty, with the exception of one product (ethanol) which will be subject to a tariff quota. the proposed measures should be welcomed as an excellent example of the synergies made possible by the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. while the eu and its member states are already providing generous humanitarian assistance to pakistan, the extension of trade preferences to the country is part of a broader package of measures to help address the medium- and long-term economic consequences of the catastrophic floods. ensuring the reconstruction and future sustainable development of pakistan is of paramount importance not only for its citizens but also for security and stability in the region. the stability and prosperity of pakistan, which will not resort to extremism or fundamentalism, is clearly in the eu's interest.

in writing. − if you have when it was created in 1970, the vat-based own resource was designed as a potential genuine own resource, on the assumption that the ongoing process of harmonisation of national vat legislation would ultimately bring about full harmonisation of national vat bases. over time, however, it has been transformed into a complex and opaque statistical tool, which is in fact one of the forms of contribution based on gni and is shifted from national budgets. as early as june 2011, the commission presented its proposal for a multiannual financial framework for the years 2014-2020, together with a set of proposals for reforming the union's own resources system. the proposal is that the new eu vat-based own resource is based on the share of vat on supplies of goods and services, acquisitions and imports subject to the standard vat rate in each member state. it is therefore based on the actual harmonisation that already exists for these goods and services at a standard rate throughout the eu. also, under the new system, the european commission will carry out the bulk of the calculations currently carried out by the member states. i believe that this proposal represents an important improvement on the current system and has the potential to become a stable and reliable genuine own resource for the union budget.

in writing. − council decision 2008/971/ec of 16 december 2008 on the equivalence of forest reproductive material produced in third countries lays down the conditions under which forest reproductive material classified as 'identified source' and 'selective' produced in third countries may be imported into the european union. according to those rules, the systems for the approval and registration of basic material and the subsequent production of propagating material from that basic material should be in line with the organisation for economic cooperation and development (oecd) system for the certification of forest reproductive material in international trade. as regards 'qualified' material, those conditions should include the provision of information on whether or not the products have been genetically modified. i therefore consider that decision 2008/971/ec should be amended accordingly.

in writing. − air transport plays a major role in the economy and society of the european union. in this context, the air traffic management system is of key importance for air transport activities, addressing issues related to competitiveness, safety and sustainability. the air traffic management is still based on national sovereign airspace. in europe, it is highly fragmented and dominated by national monopoly service providers. as traffic volumes have increased significantly, not least due to the development of the single air transport market, this fragmentation now presents serious problems, in particular with regard to capacity and long delays for passengers. the single european sky does not yet exist. the single european sky initiative, which is based on five pillars: performance, safety, technology, airports and the human factor, is a possible solution. the idea presented has strong political support. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on air safety and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on air safety and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on air safety and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on air safety and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on air safety and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on air safety and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on air safety.
in writing. − since 2004, when the european union acquired air traffic control competence, decision-making methods have moved from the intergovernmental level to the european union framework. the eu's main objective is to reform air traffic management in europe to cope with the continuing growth of air traffic and to make air traffic operations as safe, efficient and environmentally friendly as possible. the commission communication on this issue details the results of the sesar (single european sky air traffic management research) joint undertaking study on the macroeconomic impact of the sesar project. if sesar is implemented as planned, the projections are very promising. the cumulative impact on gdp is expected to be eur 419 billion. furthermore, there will be room to create 328 000 jobs and to reduce co2 emissions by 50 million tonnes. the benefits of the full and timely implementation of the single european sky are therefore too great to be ignored.

in writing. − the eu and the us are each other's main trading partners, with the two economies together accounting for almost half of global economic output and almost a third of global trade flows. they thus represent the strongest economic partnership in the world. however, there is a general feeling that the potential of the transatlantic relationship is far from exhausted. the eu and the us share common values, similar legal systems and high standards of occupational and environmental protection, and it seems appropriate and justified to take advantage of this synergy and close cooperation to ensure the growth and jobs needed by both partners. the moderate increase in global trade over the last three years has contributed significantly to mitigating the negative effects of the economic crisis, in particular in the union and the united states, demonstrating that trade plays an important role in determining growth and employment. i consider it important to continue strengthening transatlantic economic relations. at the same time, i believe that close cooperation between the european parliament, the council, the commission, the us congress, the us government and stakeholders is in order to achieve full economic potential, to create new opportunities for businesses and workers on both sides of the atlantic and to strengthen the leadership of the eu and the us in the global economy.
in writing. − at last year's summit, the leaders of the european union and the united states set up a working group to increase job creation, economic growth and mutual competitiveness. the united states and the european union have among the most open economic relations in the world. our markets are firmly linked through significant trade and investment flows with a bilateral trade volume of eur 702.6 billion and bilateral investment stocks of eur 2 394 billion last year. despite these positive results, it is widely recognised that the potential of transatlantic relations is far from exhausted. moreover, the european union and the united states share common values, similar legal systems, and high standards of protection for workers and the environment. it is necessary to make the most of these synergies to ensure growth and jobs and set targets, which both partners desperately need in times of crisis.
for the efd group. according to the opinion of the european data protection supervisor, as well as judgments of the constitutional courts of germany, the czech republic and romania, directive 2006/24, which ordered telecommunications companies to retain identifying data on the sender, recipient, place and time of a telephone call or email for the purpose of possible investigation and prosecution of criminal offences for a period of 6 months to 2 years, does not meet the requirements set out in european privacy and data protection law. therefore, commissioner, a responsible decision must be taken, either to repeal the directive and leave it to the member states to deal with this agenda, or, if there is agreement that common union rules are needed in terms of police and judicial cooperation in such criminal matters, to prepare a new legal framework which should then correspond to the culture of today's european legislation. since april last year, i think, there has been enough time for you to make a responsible and serious decision on this matter.

rapporteur. − mr president, thank you for giving me this opportunity to make some short remarks, as we have had no preliminary discussion on this topic. the proposed directive is intended to replace the 1995 decision regarding consular protection for eu citizens by diplomatic and consular representations, in view of the legal framework established by the lisbon treaty. article 23 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, on which the proposal is based, provides that every citizen of the european union shall, in the territory of third countries where the member state of which he is a national is not represented, be entitled to protection by the diplomatic and consular authorities of any member state. the proposal covers not only everyday situations, such as loss of a passport or becoming a victim of crime, but also crisis situations where eu citizens might need help. while in relation to everyday situations citizens could seek help at any consulate or embassy of any member state, crisis situations are different. there was almost unanimous agreement in all the committees involved here that no single member state or lead-state should bear the burden of dealing with evacuation or other crisis-related tasks, including assistance to unrepresented eu citizens, so the role of coordination had to be shifted to eu delegations. this proposal is an excellent illustration of the fact that ‘more europe’ does not mean more bureaucracy or more brussels. ‘more europe’ could also mean more help for eu citizens in need, and more protection for citizens unrepresented in third countries who find themselves in precarious or crisis-related situations. finally i would like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs for their efforts and to ask all of you, colleagues, to support this proposal.

in writing. − the stabilisation and association agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of serbia, of the other part, was signed in luxembourg on 29 april 2008. the agreement shall enter into force on the first day of the second month following the date on which the parties notify each other of the completion of their respective ratification procedures. at the same time, the interim agreement between the european community and the republic of serbia, signed on the same day in order to allow for the earlier application of the provisions of the stabilisation and association agreement relating to trade and trade-related matters, entered into force on 1 february 2010. i consider it important and necessary to lay down the rules for the application of certain provisions of the interim agreement and the procedures for adopting the detailed rules for its application. since the provisions governing trade and trade-related matters in those agreements are largely identical, this regulation should also apply to the implementation of the stabilisation and association agreement after its entry into force.

in writing. − union fishing vessels have equal access to union waters and resources covered by the rules of the common fisheries policy. council regulation (ec) no 2371/2002 of 20 december 2002 on the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources under the common fisheries policy provides for a derogation from the equal access rule by allowing member states to restrict fishing in waters within 12 nautical miles of their baselines to certain vessels. the rules in place restricting access to resources within that zone have contributed to conservation by limiting fishing effort in the most sensitive part of union waters. however, the derogation shall expire on 31 december of that year. i think it is appropriate to extend it until a new regulation on the common fisheries policy is adopted.

in writing. − hunger and food insecurity are still a global problem. while significant progress has been made on many levels over the past decade, progress is relentlessly slow when it comes to hunger and malnutrition. in 2010, an estimated 925 million people (around 13.6% of the world's population) did not have enough to eat, despite a decline in income poverty in several regions. in developing countries, 98% of the world's undernourished live, 60% of them women. malnutrition is the underlying cause of more than a third of child deaths, an estimated 2.6 million children a year. as a result of long-term malnutrition, millions of children suffer stunted growth, threatening them with impaired cognitive and physical development. the number of people affected by disasters, including those caused by global climate change, is also increasing worldwide. in this context, the european parliament is expected to give its consent to the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the food aid convention (facc). the 2012 mff is fully in line with the eu's ongoing efforts to contribute to alleviating poverty and eradicating hunger in the world. i therefore consider it to be highly justified and appropriate for parliament to give its consent to the agreement.
in writing. − we must continue to treat hunger and food insecurity as a global problem. it is estimated that in 2010, more than 925 million people did not have enough to eat. although some significant progress has been made in recent years, progress is still slow. ninety-eight percent of the world's undernourished people live in developing countries. malnutrition is responsible for more than one third of child deaths. in addition, the number of people affected by disasters worldwide is increasing. the eu must therefore play a leading role in reducing poverty and eradicating hunger. it is clear that there is a continuing need for an international, legally binding framework to define and record commitments to food aid to developing countries. we need long-term solutions, with activities that make it easier to help. by strengthening local production and livelihood activities, we can avoid becoming dependent on aid in the long term. we therefore need to extend the range of products eligible for support to include products that help to protect the maintenance of life. that is why i voted in favour of this proposal. thank you, sir.
in writing. − i welcome the fact that the eu, as one of the main donors of humanitarian aid, has been working with the member states to negotiate the 1999 food aid convention and has been a major driving force towards a modern food aid convention at both eu and international level. the main objective of the food aid convention is to respond in an effective and efficient manner to the food and nutrition needs of the most vulnerable groups of the population. as a general principle, i support food aid only when it is the most effective and appropriate means of meeting the food or nutritional needs of the most vulnerable groups. i expect countries to make a commitment to ensure their food security, to create the conditions for poverty reduction and hunger eradication. we must work for a europe that is not only solidarity-based but also adequately social, and above all, one that ensures that citizens - if they are dependent on food aid - are not in a situation where they receive charity and it is unworthy of them.
in writing. − if you have pursuant to article 23 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), any citizen of the union in the territory of a third country in which the member state of which he is a national is not represented is entitled to protection by the diplomatic or consular authorities of any member state under the same conditions as a national of that state. this principle is also enshrined in article 46 of the charter of fundamental rights. a new legislative instrument is desirable and necessary in order to facilitate eu citizens' access to their rights, including the right to protection in third countries. at the same time, the number of areas affected by the crisis is increasing. for this reason too, i believe that a new, common approach is all the more important. we distinguish between local consular protection in everyday life and protection in crisis situations. building on the lisbon treaty, solidarity between member states must be maintained. therefore, in the day-to-day matters of consular protection, an unrepresented citizen has the right to seek assistance from any diplomatic or consular authority of any member state. for crisis situations, it is proposed that the union delegation be responsible for the coordination and provision of assistance in relation to crisis preparedness and in the event of a crisis.

in writing. − the energy star programme, created by the united states environmental protection agency (epa), aims to increase the energy efficiency of office equipment. in 2000, the eu and the us signed an agreement on the coordination of energy-efficiency labelling programmes for office equipment. the agreement in question, which was renewed in 2006 for a second five-year period, provides for the establishment of the energy star programme in the eu. under the agreement, the epa and the commission jointly manage the programme and it includes cooperation on the development of product specifications and mutual recognition of products registered in the eu and the us. before the current agreement expired in december 2011, the council authorised the commission to negotiate a new agreement to ensure the continuation of the energy star programme for a third five-year period. these negotiations were concluded in november 2011. it is justified for parliament to give its consent to the new agreement.

in writing. − on 22 may 2012, the european ombudsman presented the annual report for 2011 to the president of the european parliament, mr martin schulz. the ombudsman registered 2 510 complaints in 2011, compared with 2 667 complaints in 2010. of the total of 2 544 complaints, 698 (27%) were dealt with under its mandate. the number of complaints over the past nine years has been increasing. in 2011, the ombudsman adapted the procedures to make them more understandable to citizens. this explains why a higher number of investigations were opened in 2010 and why it took on average a little longer to close the investigations in 2011. this adjustment also meant that the ombudsman closed fewer cases marked 'solved by the institution' than in 2010, while closing a greater number of cases marked 'further investigation is not warranted'. as regards cooperation, the european ombudsman works closely with his partners in the member states. this cooperation takes place within the european network of ombudsmen, which consists of 90 offices in 32 european countries. it includes national and regional ombudsmen and similar bodies of the member states of the european union, eu candidate countries and other countries of the european economic area or the schengen area, as well as the european ombudsman and the committee on petitions of the european parliament.
in writing. − the markets in financial instruments directive (mifid), which has been in force since november 2007, is the main pillar of financial market integration in the eu. the fundamental objective is to deepen the integration, competitiveness and efficiency of eu financial markets. in particular, the possibility for member states to require that all trading in financial instruments take place on traditional exchanges has been removed, allowing for pan-european competition between these exchanges and alternative trading venues. banks and investment firms have been given stronger 'authorisation' to provide investment services within the eu, as long as they comply with organisational and reporting requirements as well as comprehensive rules designed to ensure investor protection. however, it is also true that the more competitive scene has led to new challenges. the benefits of stronger competition have not been equally shared by all market participants and have not always been passed on to the final retail or non-retail investors. in conclusion, although the comprehensive rules of mifid have largely proven themselves in the context of the financial crisis, there is a need for targeted but ambitious improvements. i believe that the revision of mifid is an integral part of the reforms aimed at creating a safer, more reliable, more transparent and more accountable financial system that works for the benefit of the economy and society as a whole in the period marked by the consequences of the financial crisis.
in writing. − the financial crisis has revealed shortcomings in the transparency of financial markets. enhancing transparency is therefore one of the common principles for strengthening the financial system, as endorsed in the g20 london declaration of 2 april 2009. in order to enhance transparency and improve the functioning of the internal market in financial instruments, a new framework setting out uniform requirements for the transparency of transactions in markets in financial instruments should be introduced. it should lay down comprehensive rules for the whole range of financial instruments. the group on eu financial supervision, chaired by jacques de larosière, called on the union to develop a more harmonised set of financial rules. the european council of june 2009 also underlined the need to create a single set of european rules applicable to all financial institutions in the single market within the framework of the future european supervisory architecture. the new legislation should therefore consist of two distinct legal instruments, a directive and this regulation. i believe that both instruments should together form a legal framework governing the requirements applicable to investment firms, regulated markets and reporting services providers. this directly applicable legal act aims to contribute decisively to the smooth functioning of the internal market. the commission therefore considers that the measure is imputable to the state and that it is imputable to the state.
in writing. − the economic, social and financial crisis and the sovereign debt crisis have not yet abated. the current economic situation has shown that greater coordination of member states' macroeconomic and budgetary policies is needed to achieve a more integrated and balanced economic union. the crisis and the growing competitiveness gap since the introduction of the euro have highlighted the need to strengthen the coordination of economic and employment policies and to improve budgetary procedures. the european council has made a strong commitment to mobilise all incentives, tools and policies at every level of government in the eu to revive smart, sustainable, inclusive growth that is resource-efficient and job-creating. all proposed measures in this area should contribute to achieving sound and sustainable public finances, minimising macroeconomic imbalances and reviving competitiveness, which can help and lead to higher growth and employment. i believe that there is a need to strengthen own coherence within and between recommendations for individual member states, to make better use of the macroeconomic scoreboard and also to take into account the negative effects of individual member states' economic policies.
in writing. − on 10 november 2011, the russian federation concluded multilateral negotiations on wto accession after 18 years of negotiations and was officially admitted as a member on 16 december 2011. the eu is a strategic trading partner of russia, considered to be the most important and growing source of imports, the main destination for exports and a key investment partner (in terms of foreign direct investment), accounting for 47,1% of russia's total trade. this relationship is still developing, with russia becoming the eu's second source of imports (eur 158.6 billion) and its fourth destination of exports (eur 86.1 billion) according to available data for 2010 . on the other hand, it is important to note that immediately before russia completed its accession to the wto, it did not act fully in the spirit of its future wto obligations. i consider it justified for the russian side to remove unjustified temporary bans, unilateral temporary tariff increases and protectionist measures and barriers to open and fair trade which have caused significant damage to eu exporters. provided that the commitments set out are mutually respected, russia's accession to the multilateral trading system and its rules will undoubtedly represent a further step in improving bilateral relations between the eu and russia.
in writing. − to date, none of the parliamentary or presidential elections held in belarus since 1995 have been recognised as free and fair by the osce. according to the osce/odihr international election observation mission and the osce parliamentary assembly, many osce commitments, including the rights of citizens to associate, to be elected and to express themselves, were not respected in the context of the 23 september parliamentary elections, despite some improvements to the electoral law. in addition, international election observers were not properly allowed to monitor the vote counting and the election process was negatively assessed in a large number of polling stations. independent international observers have reported that serious violations of standards have occurred during the elections and, due to the non-transparent counting of votes, the election results cannot be said to be a true expression of the will of the belarusian people. the undemocratic nature of the parliamentary election process in belarus is deplorable. moreover, in my view, this negative assessment of the parliamentary elections will again prevent the european parliament from establishing official relations with the belarusian parliament. at the same time, the euronest parliamentary assembly would have no reason in this situation to invite official representatives of the belarusian legislature to take their seats in the assembly, thus depriving the eastern partnership of one of the important means of bringing belarus closer to the democratic values of the eu.

the commission adopted an action plan to improve the safety of explosives as early as 2008. it also set up a so-called standing committee on precursors. it identified various explosives precursors that could be used to commit terrorist attacks and also recommended appropriate measures at european union level. some member states have therefore adopted laws, regulations and administrative provisions concerning the placing on the market, making available and possession of certain chemicals and mixtures which can also be used as explosives precursors. however, these differ from each other and may thus constitute certain obstacles to trade within the european union. that is why we must harmonize the rules. this will eliminate distortions of competition, facilitate the free movement of chemicals, while ensuring a high level of protection and safety for the general public. the commission proposal should prevent the general public from having access to specific substances which, although commonly used, can be misused as precursors to explosives. restricting public access to legitimate substances is also intended to reduce the frequency and impact of terrorist attacks. however, i think it is necessary to stress that it is essential that we also preserve the right of individuals to privacy in all cases. moreover, this regulation must be flexible enough to respond quickly to changing needs. in particular, a good system of exchange of information between manufacturers and dealers is essential in this regard. codes of conduct and voluntary agreements could also help. such means would greatly promote the good functioning of the regulation.

the commission's green paper on an integrated european market for card, internet and mobile payments highlights several obstacles that prevent the european payments market from functioning in the most efficient and open way possible. the european market for this type of payment is fragmented, both nationally and across borders. standardisation in this area should focus on the definition of security standards and should include the measures necessary to ensure a more open, transparent, innovative and competitive electronic payment market that benefits all consumers. moreover, the existence of a neutral and secure single european market for such payments, which would facilitate free competition and innovation, is essential for achieving a genuine digital single market. in addition, electronic payments play an important role in the fight against the grey economy and tax evasion. the european union's single legal framework in this area must therefore focus in particular on a high level of consumer protection.
shadow banking as such is carried out through an entity or financial contracts that create a combination of functions similar to those of banks, but outside the regulatory framework or under a regime that is either insufficiently consistent or addresses issues other than systemic risks. regulated entities in the standard banking system engage in activities defined as part of the shadow banking system and are linked to shadow banking entities in many ways. the global shadow banking system was estimated to be worth around eur 51 trillion in 2011. this represents up to 30% of the total financial system and half of the total bank assets. moreover, shadow banking has been identified as one of the possible main causes and circumstances that contributed to the financial crisis and a factor that threatens the stability of the entire financial system. that's why we need complete oversight of shadow banking.

in writing. − on 21 april 2009, the commission adopted a report on the application of council regulation (ec) no 44/2001 of 22 december 2000 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. the report concluded that the regulation is generally applied satisfactorily, but that it is nevertheless desirable to improve the application of some of its provisions, to further facilitate the free movement of judgments and to improve access to justice. since a number of amendments are to be made, this regulation should be recast in the interests of clarity. the union has set itself the objective of maintaining and developing an area of freedom, security and justice, inter alia, by facilitating access to justice, in particular through the principle of mutual recognition of judicial and extrajudicial decisions in civil matters. in order to gradually establish such an area, the union needs to adopt measures in the field of judicial cooperation in civil matters having cross-border implications, in particular where they are necessary for the proper functioning of the internal market. in order to achieve the objective of free movement of judgments in civil and commercial matters, it is necessary and appropriate that the rules governing jurisdiction, recognition and enforcement of judgments be governed by a legal act of the union which is binding and directly applicable. the regulation is one of the most successful pieces of eu legislation and its recast is of considerable importance.
in writing. − the action plan to enhance the safety of explosives adopted by the council in april 2008 called on the commission to set up a standing committee on precursors to assess measures and make recommendations on the regulation of explosives precursors available on the market in terms of cost and benefit. the committee subsequently identified various explosives precursors that could be used to commit terrorist attacks and recommended appropriate action at union level. some member states have already adopted corresponding laws, regulations and administrative provisions. however, they differ from one member state to another, which may constitute barriers to trade within the european union. for this reason, i consider it justified to harmonise them in order to guarantee the free movement of chemicals and mixtures in the internal market while ensuring a high level of protection of the health and safety of the general public. since the objectives of this regulation, namely to limit the access of the general public to chemicals which can be used for the domestic production of explosives, cannot be sufficiently achieved by the member states and can therefore, by reason of the scale of the action, be better achieved at union level, the european union may adopt measures, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. in accordance with the principle of proportionality, this regulation does not go beyond what is necessary in order to achieve those objectives.
