in writing. − greenland originally joined the european community (ec) in 1973 as part of denmark, but left the ec following a referendum in 1985. it is now one of the overseas countries and territories of the union within the meaning of article 355 (2) tfeu. greenland's economy is heavily dependent on fishing and exports of fishery products to the eu. the first fisheries partnership agreement with greenland was concluded after greenland's withdrawal from the ec in 1985, on the basis that the community could retain its original fishing rights after paying an annual financial contribution. the dpr between the eu and the former local government of greenland was adopted on 28 june 2007 with the current protocol setting out the annual fishing opportunities and financial contributions until 31 december 2012. the european commission, on the basis of a mandate from the council of 19 july 2011, has been negotiating with the government of greenland with a view to renewing the protocol due to the expiry of the current protocol on 31 december 2012. on the basis of those negotiations, a new protocol was initialled on 3 february 2012 for a period of three years from 1 january 2013. i am of the opinion that the fisheries partnership agreement with greenland is in line with the objectives of the common fisheries policy and the principles of sustainable fisheries and is of considerable benefit to both parties.
in writing. − the commission's report on the application of council directive 93/109/ec laying down detailed rules for the exercise of the right to vote and to stand as a candidate in elections to the european parliament for citizens of the union residing in a member state of which they are not nationals in 2004 has shown that certain provisions of that directive need to be amended. the directive provides that no person may vote and be elected in more than one member state more than once in the same election. difficulties which threaten the functioning and effectiveness of the exchange of information cannot be solved by harmonising the rules on registration in the national electoral registers alone. such a solution would not be proportionate to the objective pursued. for this reason too, i think it appropriate to abolish the exchange of information but to maintain the obligation to submit a declaration in which the voter or candidate undertakes to exercise his right to vote or to stand as a candidate only in the member state of residence. a routine check of all votes and nominations would be inadequate in view of the problems identified and would be difficult to implement. member states should therefore focus their checks only on situations where there is an increased likelihood of nationals voting and being elected more than once.
in writing. −the consumer credit directive has two objectives: a high level of consumer protection and the strengthening of the crossborder internal market in consumer credit. there is no doubt that the final harmonisation of some essential elements of the credit legislation has significantly increased the level of consumer protection in europe. however, some member states have not yet transposed all or some of the provisions of the directive within the deadline. the main reasons were the relatively short, two-year, timeframe and the large scope of the legislation. in a wide range of areas, including consumer protection, general credit rules and access to databases, many provisions have had to be changed or new provisions have had to be introduced. these procedures are very complex and concern both national legislatures and financial institutions. i think it would be appropriate to allocate more time in the future and set the transposition deadline at three years. i also believe that the commission should now review the transposition of the directive and urge the member states to apply it correctly. in due course, a thorough evaluation of the legal and substantive impact of the directive should be carried out and, subsequently, consideration should be given to the need to develop possible amendments.
in writing. − in my country, when the additional tax on banks was introduced, bank analysts and bank officials said that they had a planned profit, which if jeopardised would increase bank charges and again be overpaid by clients. therefore, in the context of free trade and services, i welcome the possibility of cross-border consumer credit. the consumer credit directive creates not only a common european legal framework but also competitiveness in total cost of credit. our banks, which were privatized debt-free, without any obligations with high-tribal packages, now offer consumer and mortgage loans 25% more expensive than, for example, banks in italy. therefore, in the context of competition in cross-border consumer credit, i see a great contribution of this directive to strengthening the internal market in cross-border consumer credit and i expect the establishment of such legal and technical arrangements to create such a standard form that would allow the consumer to reliably compare loans from different providers. i expect that a thorough evaluation of the directive from a legal and factual point of view will now follow and that there will be an urgent call for the member states to apply it correctly.
in writing. − the current economic and financial crisis will undoubtedly have a far-reaching impact on the european economy, employment rates, public savings and social investment in europe. most current and recent responses to the crisis are based on short-term objectives aimed in particular at restoring the sustainability of public finances, which are essential for the eu economy. the result of the economic and social crisis is that the unemployment rate in the countries. one of the consequences of the economic and social crisis is increased pressure on social assistance systems in many countries and substantial reductions in revenues for pension, employment or health care systems. most current crisis-response measures lack a social and employment policy dimension. the first attempt to create a coordinated eu response to the issue, the lisbon strategy together with the european employment strategy, has failed for lack of governance and, unfortunately, the success of the europe 2020 strategy seems uncertain and requires greater efforts by member states. i share the view that the recently established economic governance and macroeconomic surveillance should be linked to the monitoring of employment and social affairs policies. i also believe that it is justified for member states to sign the social investment pact, which will enable them to establish a better governance and control mechanism for the implementation of the europe 2020 objectives in the areas of employment, social affairs and education.
in writing. − the unemployment rate in eu countries rose to an average of over 10% in 2012 and in many regions is close to 20%. unemployment has mainly affected young people, low-skilled workers and the long-term unemployed. with unemployment, of course, comes an increase in poverty, which is at 22% of the european average among young people. for member states, this means an increased burden on social security systems and an increase in public spending, which can lead to weaker economic growth and even a deepening of the economic recession. we regret that most member states have not paid enough attention to the area of social affairs, employment and education, which i would see as a certain failure of the lisbon strategy. it is therefore necessary for member states to set up a mechanism to deliver effectively on the objectives of the new europe 2020 strategy. at eu level, we need to ensure that the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework contains the adequate budgetary resources necessary to stimulate and support social investment. i am therefore convinced that we must clearly maintain the budgetary volume for the structural funds, in particular the european social fund, in the next programming period, so that they can continue to support social investments and their priorities reflecting the specific needs of the member states.
in writing. − if you have one of the most significant societal impacts of the current economic and social crisis is the steadily rising unemployment rate in eu countries. it is the generation of young people that is most affected. students leaving university during this period encounter various obstacles that prevent them from fully engaging in the work process. whether it is the shortage of jobs, the high skill requirements of employers or the consequences of natural population ageing, the consequences of the crisis are unimaginable. a young man has to handle them himself. but there is a rule, and it is this: the longer a young person is unemployed, the more difficult and challenging it is for him to get any kind of employment. the economic and social consequences of youth unemployment are alarming. without work, it is absolutely impossible to plan for the future, to develop one's skills or to participate in social life. if we don't protect the interests of the younger generation, what future awaits us? for these reasons, i call on all relevant actors to focus on better allocating public finances and ensuring a sufficient share of financing in the 2014-2020 mff to support employment, job creation and support training programmes and skills that could counter the risks posed by the crisis. by ensuring investment in the social sphere, we will contribute to better youth employment and labour market balance.
in writing. − production in the european union is very diverse and of high quality, and the european union guarantees a high level of health safety and has all the resources at its disposal to take advantage of the projected development of global demand, provided that it highlights its strengths through a better targeted and more ambitious promotion policy. in addition, consumers in the internal market need to be better informed about the quality and variety of the offer available. the current legislative proposals on this issue for the period after 2013, which are currently being negotiated, aim to enable this policy to contribute fully to the europe 2020 strategy by promoting agriculture that provides guarantees for food security, sustainable use of natural resources and development of rural areas, while being a source of growth and jobs. an effective promotion policy is a necessary condition for achieving the objectives set. the reform of the common agricultural policy aims at improving the organisation of production, sustainability and quality of agricultural products. i believe it is essential to complement it with a promotion policy that will allow the food sector to develop to its full potential, thereby encouraging growth and employment in the european economy.

in writing. − the directive on the resale right was drawn up with a dual objective: on the one hand, to ensure that authors of graphic and fine art works share in the economic success of their original works of art and, on the other, to harmonise the application of the resale right in the eu. the commission considers that a clear link cannot be established between the loss of eu market share in the global market for modern and contemporary art and the harmonisation of the provisions on the application of resale rights in the eu as from 1 january 2006. nor can clear signs of a systematic shift of trade within the union from those member states which introduced the resale right for living artists in 2006 be demonstrated at present. however, the commission recognises that there is pressure on european art markets, across all price ranges, both for auctions and art dealers. the commission also notes that the quality of the administration of the resale right varies from one member state to another. therefore, the burden for lower level market players may be particularly high, as they are more burdened by the costs of managing the resale right. in this context, i believe that the commission should work closely with stakeholders to strengthen the position of the european art market and to remove some of the difficulties and obstacles.
in writing. − at its meeting on 19 october 2010, the conference of committee chairs held an extensive exchange of views on the negotiations relating to the ordinary legislative procedure. in his letter of 18 april, president buzek informed president casini of the outcome of this meeting and informed him of the decision of the conference to invite the committee on constitutional affairs to review rule 70 of the rules of procedure with a view to making the procedures more efficient, transparent and open by incorporating some key elements of the code of conduct for negotiations under the ordinary legislative procedure into a binding part of the rules of procedure. the question of interinstitutional negotiations and agreements in legislative procedures is also linked to the question of representative democracy at european level, on the basis of the principles of openness and democratic accountability. the public nature of debates and votes has been linked to democratic accountability since the beginning of parliamentary democracy: if voters were not able to know what their elected representatives are saying and how they are voting, they could not hold them accountable in the next elections. in this context, the introduction of binding provisions on negotiation in legislative procedures, which increase openness and thus accountability, would be a step towards strengthening representative democracy at european level.
in writing. − by letter of 13 january 2012, the president of parliament informed the committee on constitutional affairs of the decision taken by the bureau to restrict the translation of verbatim minutes of debates, to which parliament had committed itself when preparing the 2012 budget. in accordance with the current rule 181, the verbatim translations of the minutes of the proceedings are to be provided in all the official languages. at the same time, and in accordance with article 182, the audio-visual recording of the hearing shall be made available to the public on the internet, with interpretation into all the official languages, immediately after the conclusion of the hearing. in addition, the proceedings are broadcast in real time on the internet. members may also request that parts of the verbatim record be translated within a short time. after adopting a package of austerity measures for the 2012 budget, parliament has indeed fulfilled its budgetary commitments and started to translate the cre into english only as of july 2011. however, this situation is contrary to the current wording of articles 181 and 146 and could jeopardise the principle of multilingualism. i therefore consider it justified to draw up the cre only as a multilingual document, in which all speeches will be recorded only in their original language without any automatic translation being provided. the production of verbatim records in their original language will lead to greater budget and resource savings, while preserving the principle of multilingualism.
in writing. − on 4 october 2010, the commission adopted a proposal for a new regulation on the approval and market surveillance of two- or three-wheel vehicles and quadricycles. the l-category covers a wide range of vehicles: mopeds, two- or three-wheel motorcycles, quadricycles and mini-cars. the number of l-category vehicles currently in use in the eu is estimated at over 30 million. the european commission is seeking to simplify the current legal framework and to set new administrative and technical requirements, for example on environmental and safety aspects and market surveillance. the type-approval requirements for new l-category vehicles are currently laid down in framework directive 2002/24/ec and 14 other directives which refer to it. those directives will be repealed and replaced by a proposal setting out the basic provisions and the scope. the detailed technical requirements shall be specified in delegated acts at a later stage. the commission's proposal has an ambitious but somewhat complex set of dates and deadlines. in the interests of clarity, rationality and simplification, i think it is justified to consider drawing up a more transparent timetable with clear and decisive steps in terms of better market surveillance, stricter emission levels and binding safety requirements. this gives industry and national administrations time to adapt appropriately to the new requirements and obligations.
in writing. − the number of l-category vehicles, which includes mopeds, two- or three-wheel motorcycles, four-wheelers and minivans, is currently estimated at over 30 million. the legal and technical requirements for the approval of new l-category vehicles are currently laid down in framework directive 2002/24/ec and 14 other directives, which contributes to the lack of clarity and the complexity of interpretation. i therefore welcome the replacement of those directives by the proposal presented, setting out the essential requirements and scope, with the technical details to be subsequently determined in the delegated acts. when setting safety standards, we must focus on the protection of the life and health of drivers of l-category vehicles, as they are up to 18 times more likely to die in an accident than drivers of cars. i therefore support the mandatory introduction of anti-lock braking systems, so-called abs, on new motorcycles, as their use could, according to estimates, prevent 20 to 35% of all accidents or significantly reduce the severity of the consequences of accidents. as regards environmental aspects, i agree with the adoption of stricter emission limits for harmful substances within a reasonable timeframe to allow industry to adapt smoothly to the new requirements.
in writing. − the aim of the proposal is to establish harmonised rules for the production of agricultural and forestry vehicles (tractors, trailers and towed equipment) in order to ensure the functioning of the internal market while providing a high level of road safety, environmental protection and crew safety. the proposed regulation significantly simplifies existing type-approval legislation by replacing 24 basic directives (and some 35 related amending directives). the new regulation and its implementing and delegated acts are designed to maintain the requirements laid down in existing legislation without reducing the current level of protection. the commission proposal contributes to the competitiveness of the sector by simplifying existing type-approval legislation. in order to ensure a high level of road safety, crew safety and environmental protection and to complete the internal market for agricultural and forestry vehicles, i believe that it would be appropriate to consider and introduce a union approval procedure for all vehicle categories, while taking into account the cost-benefit ratio, with particular attention to be paid to small and medium-sized enterprises. the objective of the draft report presented is to address the key issues that require careful consideration in this draft, in order to facilitate the deliberations of the committee.
in writing. − the diversity of payment instruments at european and global level is increasing. although new uses of mobile and internet payments appear to be developing rapidly and are attractive to both consumers and businesses, the card payment market is far from reaching its full potential. in the eu, markets for card, internet and mobile payments are still fragmented. there are considerable differences between member states when it comes to the use of card payments. the process of creating a single euro payments area (sepa) is simplifying bank transfers in 32 european countries and by 2014 all participating countries should have common sepa standards in place. i believe that if sepa is to bridge the gap between domestic and cross-border payments, the aim should be, within the framework of the integration of the card payments market, to make cross-border payments as advantageous as domestic payments. at the same time, common technical and security standards should facilitate market entry for new entrants, promote the use of card payments and make them a simpler, safer and more efficient option for consumers. the guidance for the further development of common technical and safety standards should include the achievement of a level of common infrastructure that provides a level playing field, fosters innovation and competitiveness, but does not create additional obstacles to the development of the whole area.
in writing. − in today's digital world, almost every citizen is using one of the forms of payment. children have accounts, old-age pensioners have accounts, and they are using cashless payments, whether they want to or not. the commission's green paper initiative on an integrated european market for card, internet and mobile payments should therefore be welcomed. there are certainly many problems, but i will mention at least those that we, as customers of banking services, have to face most. it's high time we standardized card payments. while in some member states payments are not allowed, in other member states they harm consumers by overcharging them. cash withdrawal fees vary from bank to bank, and many times they charge a fee to check your account balance. real-time clearing and settlement should no longer be a problem for monetary institutions today, but it is still a problem. i'm sure many of you have experienced what i've experienced, where i've sent funds from one bank account to another and the withdrawal was recorded immediately, and the deposit was not made until the next day or two days later? an integrated european market for card, internet and mobile payments will certainly remove these problems too, albeit not in the short term.
in writing. − shadow banking as such is carried out through entities or financial contracts that create a combination of functions similar to those of banks, but outside the regulatory framework or under a regulatory regime that is either insufficiently rigorous or addresses issues other than systemic risks, and without access to central bank liquidity facilities or credit guarantees provided by the public sector. entities such as special purpose entities, off-balance sheet related entities, special purpose investment companies, money market funds, exchange traded funds and investment funds may be considered as shadow banking entities. as regards shadow banking activities, the european commission distinguishes between repurchase transactions, securities lending and securitisation. clearly, shadow banking does not exist in isolation. the commission notes that the bank has not provided any evidence that the bank has been able to compete with other banks in the union. as the commission underlined in its green paper, various measures have been taken to address the systemic risks posed by shadow banking. the market has also responded and since the start of the crisis, some of the shadow banking practices have disappeared. however, the innovative nature of the shadow banking system may lead to new developments that may be a source of systemic risk that needs to be addressed. in order to address this issue adequately, the necessary monitoring tools should be established in order to obtain a concrete overview of the entire credit intermediation system.

in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 1185/2003 on the removal of shark fins on board vessels and the current proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1185/2003 on the removal of shark fins on board vessels concern the prevention and combating of the practice commonly referred to as finning. this involves removing the fins of pelagic shark species and throwing the remaining body parts back into the sea. finning is unacceptable from an environmental point of view (it threatens the sustainability of some of the shark species that are subject to this practice), as well as from a social and economic point of view (it represents the waste of food with commercial value) and from a moral point of view (it represents an act of absolute disregard for the life of an animal). i consider it essential to condemn unequivocally the practice of removing shark fins and to take appropriate measures to prohibit this practice in european waters. in this context, and with the express aim of preventing this practice, the european council adopted regulation (ec) no 1185/2003 of 26 june 2003 prohibiting the removal of shark fins on board vessels, as well as the retention on board, transhipment or landing of shark fins. despite the absence of any evidence of finning in the european fleet, the commission's aim is to 'eliminate the dreadful practice of shark finning and ensure better protection' through the relevant regulations.

in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 2371/2002 established a community system for the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources under the common fisheries policy. the common fisheries policy should ensure that fishing and aquaculture activities contribute to sustainable environmental, economic and social conditions in the long term. it should also contribute to increased productivity, a decent standard of living within the fisheries sector, a stable market, and ensure that resources are available and that supply reaches consumers at reasonable prices. the objectives for fisheries were set in the decision of the conference of the parties to the convention on biological diversity on a strategic plan for biodiversity 2011-2020. the common fisheries policy should ensure consistency with the biodiversity objectives adopted by the european council and the objectives set by the commission, in particular with a view to achieving maximum sustainable yield by 2015. i believe it is important that the management of the cfp is based on the best available scientific advice, broad stakeholder participation and also a long-term perspective.

in april 1993, the world health organization (who) declared a global emergency for the first time in history. it was tuberculosis. german microbiologist robert koch said: "if the significance of a disease were measured by the number of victims it claims, even the most dreaded infectious diseases, such as plague and cholera, would all be far behind tuberculosis". today, tb kills more people each year than aids, malaria, and tropical diseases combined, at least 300,000 of whom are children. the dynamic development of resistance to current anti-tuberculosis drugs complicates and makes impossible the treatment of this infectious disease. experts estimate that more than 50 million people are now at risk from multidrug-resistant strains of tb bacteria. who forecasts for 2000 to 2020 warn that without improved health care, tb will infect an additional billion people, sicken 200 million, and kill 35 million during that period. i therefore consider it necessary to support the adoption of the resolution on the microbial challenge.

that would strengthen, unify and simplify the european patent system. we cannot afford to delay this decision any longer when this eu r & d industry is falling apart from the rest of the world year we have been trying for several years to adopt a single european patent system that would coexist with the national and european patent systems. the commission has put forward two legislative proposals which, if adopted, will allow any company or individual to protect their inventions through a single european patent. the high cost and complexity of the european patent granting system in several member states are the main reasons that discourage patent holders from seeking pan-european patent protection. for example, the total cost of validating a european patent, which is normally long, is estimated at between eur 22 000 and eur 26 000. the creation of a european patent will help to reduce these costs to eur 680 per patent and will also create more favourable conditions for investment in research and development. the single system for patent protection will bring significant simplification to the system and will enable users to reduce the administrative burden and to reduce the cost of patents in europe by up to 80%, thus improving the functioning and protection of the free movement of goods in the internal market and also providing scope for innovation and entrepreneurship. this will help us to achieve the target of investing in r&d of 3% of gdp as set out in the eu 2020 strategy. it will also bring much needed legal certainty in this area and i would also like to stress that it is very important that parliament, as co-legislator, is fully informed of all aspects of the commission's obligations towards the framers of this regulation.

in writing. − if you have according to the european commission communication of 9 november 2011 entitled 'small business, big world a new partnership to help small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) seize global opportunities', smes are hereinafter referred to as union enterprises which are independent from larger enterprises and multinational companies and which are characterised by having fewer than 250 employees, an annual turnover of less than eur 50 million and a balance sheet of eur 43 million or less. the european commission estimates that there are some 23 million smes operating in the eu's single market. several factors can be cited to justify the lack of internationalisation of smes. this can be summarised in two key aspects. on the one hand, eu smes face difficulties in obtaining information on foreign markets and trade and investment opportunities abroad, and on the other hand, many smes lack the capital to operate globally, including financing cross-border business activities. i think it is necessary and important to focus our attention on improving the quality of information available to smes and micro-enterprises on financing options and trade financing instruments that exist at national and european level. it is through such assistance that smes and microenterprises can gradually overcome the trade barriers that prevent eu companies from accessing third country markets.
in writing. − the 23 million smes in the eu form the backbone of the union's economy and provide jobs for two thirds of those employed in the private sector. at present, about a quarter of smes are involved in international export activities, but only 13% are active in markets outside europe, due to a lack of awareness of the opportunities and also to insufficient security for their business abroad. i therefore consider it necessary that the eu not only supports but also actively protects its industries, including smes, from breaching the established international trade rules, wto rules. at the same time, we should improve advice at eu and member state level on financing, project design, legal protection of legitimate interests, dispute resolution, and the fight against counterfeiting and misuse of intellectual property. the creation of single business advisory centres at local level to provide information on export and import opportunities is, in my view, a step in the right direction. as the specific proposals in the report on financing of trade and investment by smes are aimed at improving the quality of information available to smes and micro-enterprises, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − the internet and new technologies are playing an increasingly important role in the lives of the general public. technologies are changing societies on a global scale, the functioning of our democracies, economies and businesses, development strategies, security and defence concerns, and they also touch on human rights issues. several eu member states have recognised internet access as a fundamental right and the european commission has endorsed the inclusion of digital freedoms among the copenhagen criteria. in a globally interconnected world, i believe it would be appropriate for the eu's external action to include a strategy on how to deal with new technologies. i think it is important that the eu acts as a global player in several areas of this digital world, using its economic and political weight. while excessive regulation would do more harm than good to exploit the potential of the open internet, in some areas it is justified and necessary to update the rules in order to align the revolutionary impact of technological developments with adequate democratic oversight. i am convinced that the union can only fully exploit its strength and become a global player if it brings its trade, security and foreign policies into line and strives to align its values and interests.
in writing. − information and communication technologies are constantly evolving. the internet, which can be seen as the main representative of these technologies, presents two faces to the world. on the one hand, it's a positive tool. in many parts of the world, the internet is a space for the exercise of many fundamental rights, such as free access to information, freedom of expression, freedom of the press, freedom of assembly, a space for economic, social, political and cultural development and, last but not least, a factor in the development of international trade. unfortunately, the other side of information and communication technology is negative. there are countries where the internet serves as a tool to suppress, censor, control, monitor and search not only information but also specific people. the eu is the world's largest trading bloc, but it is also a community of values. they should also form the basis of the eu's external policy. the european union can harness this potential and lead by example in promoting and protecting digital freedoms worldwide, for example by including in its external policy development programmes aimed at protecting these freedoms or by prohibiting the trade in technologies that are designed to target human rights violations. pointing out both sides of ict is extremely important. taking them into account in the formulation of eu external policy is very important and this report was therefore well placed to support them.
in writing. − since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, foreign direct investment has been included in the list of matters falling within the scope of the common commercial policy. at the time of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the member states of the union had a considerable number of bilateral agreements with third countries concerning investments. the treaty does not contain any express transitional provisions concerning such agreements, which are now subject to the exclusive competence of the union. in the interest of eu investors and their investments in third countries, as well as of the member states hosting foreign investors and investments, bilateral agreements specifying and guaranteeing the conditions for investment should be maintained. i am convinced that the european parliament, the council and the commission should ensure that any information identified as confidential is treated in accordance with regulation (ec) no 1049/2001 of the european parliament and of the council of 30 may 2001 regarding public access to european parliament, council and commission documents. i consider it necessary to ensure that agreements maintained under this regulation continue to be applicable.
in writing. − relations between georgia and the european union are developing within the framework of the european neighbourhood policy. in 2006, the eu and georgia agreed on a european neighbourhood policy action plan, which identified medium-term priorities in eu-georgia relations. the eu and georgia began negotiations in 2010 on an association agreement, which is expected to replace the existing partnership and cooperation agreement. the framework for eu-georgia relations is further extended by the recently launched eastern partnership initiative. the georgian economy has been affected by the international financial crisis since the third quarter of 2008, which has been manifested by a decline in output, declining budget revenues and growing external financing needs. in view of the deteriorating economic situation and outlook, georgia has requested macro-financial assistance from the european union. it should not only complement programmes and resources from the imf and the world bank, but also provide added value to the union's involvement. in order to ensure effective protection of the european union's financial interests linked to this macro-financial assistance, it is necessary that georgia takes appropriate measures to prevent and combat fraud, corruption and any other irregularities linked to this assistance. i also consider it essential that the commission ensures appropriate controls and the european court of auditors adequate audits.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1406/2002 of the european parliament and of the council of 27 june 2002 established the european maritime safety agency to ensure a high, uniform and effective level of maritime safety and to prevent pollution from ships. the agency should act in the interest of the union. this should include the possibility for the agency to act outside the eu in its field of competence. the agency has established itself as a trusted provider of eu-level maritime transport data that is of interest and importance to other eu activities. by these activities, which concern in particular port state control, maritime traffic and shipping monitoring and assistance in tracing potential polluters, the commission should contribute to strengthening synergies at eu level with regard to certain coast guard operations. in addition, the monitoring and data collection by the agency should also gather basic information on potential threats to maritime transport and the marine environment arising from offshore oil and gas exploration and production. in order to achieve those objectives, i am convinced that the regulation in question should be amended accordingly.
in writing. − the unitary patent protection should support scientific and technical progress and the functioning of the internal market by making access to the patent system easier, less costly and providing legal certainty. it should improve the level of patent protection by providing for the possibility of obtaining the same patent protection in the territory of the participating member states and by removing costs and burdens for undertakings throughout the union. it should be available to patent applicants from participating member states and other countries, irrespective of their nationality, residence or place of establishment. the main feature of european patents with unitary effect should be their unitary character, i.e. they should provide uniform protection and have the same effect in all the participating member states. therefore, a european patent with unitary effect should be limited, licensed, transferred, revoked or extinguished only in respect of all the participating member states. since the objective of this regulation, in particular the creation of unitary patent protection, can be better achieved at union level, the union may adopt measures, where appropriate, by means of enhanced cooperation, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity as set out in article 5 of the treaty on european union. in accordance with the principle of proportionality, as set out in that article, this regulation does not go beyond what is necessary in order to achieve that objective.
in writing. − i support the creation of a single european patent for two reasons. it is in the interests of europe's future that the eu should be able to provide effective protection for new technologies. patents are a motivation for research, and without research, you cannot build a knowledge economy. patent protection in europe today is too complicated. but perhaps even worse, the administrative costs of patent protection are too high. i understand the concerns of some citizens and organisations about the introduction of a unitary patent. i think, however, that the rapporteurs have done everything possible to ensure that these concerns are not justified.
in writing. − in the european union today, patent protection can be obtained either through the national patent offices of the member states that grant national patents or through the european patent office (epo) under the european patent convention (epc). the european patent must be validated immediately after the grant of the epc in each member state where protection is sought. for the validation of a european patent in the territory of a member state, national legislation may, inter alia, require the proprietor of patent rights to submit a translation of the european patent into an official language of that member state. the current patent system in the eu is therefore very costly and complex, especially in terms of translation requirements. despite the general recognition that european enterprises suffer from a competitive disadvantage due to the absence of unitary patent protection, the union has not yet succeeded in establishing unitary patent protection. but it certainly has its justification and its importance, and i think that a unified system of jurisdiction should be established alongside the creation of unitary patent protection.
in writing. − knowledge and innovation play a key role in our future and it is therefore essential that the decision on a single eu patent valid in the 25 member states of the european union is based on interinstitutional cooperation and is based on uniformity and transparency for the users of the system. smes are at the heart of the european economy. therefore, in order to avoid persistent obstacles and subsequent consideration of the international expansion of smes, it is necessary to provide for a system that is legally unambiguous and affordable in terms of the costs associated with its validation and subsequent maintenance. after previous debates on the seat of the epo, we have solved the problem of the need to translate patents into all the languages of the member states. i believe that a single system of jurisdiction will facilitate the administration of justice in individual disputes. nevertheless, it is necessary to ensure its compatibility with european law and to ensure that the objections raised by the european court of justice to the legitimacy of this newly created judicial body are answered. that is why i am in favour of the additional and separate ratification of the agreement on the system of jurisdiction by each member state and i believe that this compromise will avoid any objections on their part and will speed up the entry into force of the unified patent regulations.
in writing. − an efficient patent system in europe can contribute to achieving growth through innovation in particular. european businesses, in particular smes, need such tools to combat the current economic crisis and to remain competitive on a global scale. the current patent system in europe allows the industrial property offices of the member states to grant national patents and the european patent office to grant european patents. once a patent has been granted, the european patent is divided into a series of national patents, which are governed by national law. the system is very costly and subject to a very expensive and risky multi-court dispute settlement system, which often leads to conflicting judgments. the proposals on unitary patent protection and the language regime, which are currently under legislative review by the parliament and the council, aim to abolish the current fragmented patent system. after many decades of failed attempts, a genuine single patent market is now within reach, capable of providing legal certainty and being internationally competitive. i therefore believe that parliament should support the proposed system of jurisdiction for patent disputes.
in writing. − in april 2007, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with certain central american countries. the negotiations resulted in an eu-central america association agreement. the agreement includes a bilateral safeguard clause allowing the reintroduction of a duty rate under the most-favoured-nation clause if, as a result of the liberalisation of trade resulting from this agreement, imports are made in such increased quantities and under such conditions as to cause or threaten to cause serious injury to union producers of like or competing products. the agreement also provides for a stabilisation mechanism for bananas under which the application of preferential duties may be suspended when a certain annual import volume is reached and which is applicable until 1 january 2020. both measures need to be transposed into eu law in order to become applicable. from a procedural point of view, safeguard clauses agreed with third countries and regions since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon are subject to the ordinary legislative procedure.
in writing. − the eu-central america association agreement sets an important precedent in that it is the first bi-regional association agreement signed by the eu after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. the key objectives of the eu-latin america bi-regional strategic partnership are regional, social, economic and cultural integration, which are underpinned by the sub-regional and bilateral association agreements concluded. in order to ensure that the development of the eu-latin america partnership benefits both parties and everyone, i believe it is necessary and important to take into account the respect for the principles of democracy, the rule of law and full respect for the human rights of all citizens as an essential element of political dialogue. i am of the opinion that the association agreement in question contributes effectively and efficiently to the efforts towards regional, social and political integration and to the achievement of the fundamental objective of a bi-regional strategic partnership between the eu and latin america.
in writing. − if you have on 19 january 2009, the council authorised the commission to open trade negotiations with the andean community member states, which eventually resulted in a trade agreement with colombia and peru. it provides, inter alia, for the reduction and ultimately the elimination of customs duties in bilateral trade between the partners. it also contains a safeguard clause which allows tariff preferences to be suspended or removed if such trade liberalisation leads to an unexpected increase in imports, which causes a deterioration in the position of european industry in competition with such imports and thereby threatens employment in the eu. the objective of the bilateral safeguard instrument is to provide a safety net where the industry needs time to adapt to new conditions as a result of the trade liberalisation provided for in the free trade agreement. the instrument will therefore only be applicable for a temporary period of 10 years from the entry into force of the agreement or slightly longer for products which have been liberalised for more than 10 years. in order to be effective, safeguard measures need to be incorporated into eu law.
in writing. − the trade agreement between the european union and its member states, on the one hand, and colombia and peru, on the other, is part of the long-term relationship between the eu and the andean community. the substance of the agreement is economic, but it also contains an enforceable human rights clause and a chapter on sustainable development, covering the ilo's main labour standards and international environmental protection agreements. it will give eu companies access to relatively small but growing markets. it can also be seen as a springboard for closer relations, especially trade, with central and latin america. the agreement represents an opportunity to provide a firm foundation for colombia and peru's reforms aimed at integrating into the global economy, increasing prosperity and consolidating their growth in order to improve the living conditions of their people. i think the european parliament should give its consent to its closure.
in writing. − the trade agreement between the european union and its member states, on the one hand, and colombia and peru, on the other, is part of the long-term relationship between the eu and the andean community (can). in 2007, negotiations were launched to conclude an interregional association agreement. disagreements between the andean countries on the approach to a number of key trade issues to be covered by the proposed agreement unfortunately led to the breakdown of the talks in june 2008. new negotiations, this time with colombia and peru only, were launched in january 2009 and successfully concluded in may 2010. on the issues of the new trade agreement, our political group has always supported and promoted its human and environmental dimension. we all know how important, for example, the rights of workers and the related rules on safety at work are. the november tragedy at a bangladeshi clothing factory is proof of that. the agreement will give eu companies access to relatively small but emerging markets. trade between the eu and colombia and peru increased by 10% between 2006 and 2010. the agreement represents an opportunity to improve trade relations with central america.
in writing. − although women live longer on average, they have a much higher incidence of various diseases, such as osteoporosis, rheumatoid arthritis, stroke, urinary incontinence and cancer, than men. cancer is currently the most common cause of death among older women in the eu. the incidence of disease increases rapidly with age. if we want to age well and actively, we must focus on prevention and information. it is the lack of them that causes the under-utilisation of existing opportunities. ageing is a very difficult time for women. we are experiencing dramatic changes, our social and work roles are changing, and physical changes are often very difficult to accept. older women are a specific and particularly vulnerable group in the eu population. they need to be given proper attention and care. clinical research should be more gender-sensitive. our policies must focus on promoting good habits and thus supporting a healthy and active ageing of the european population.
in writing. − older women are often discriminated against because of their age, gender and ethnicity, and women from low socioeconomic backgrounds face many difficulties. as women are paid less than men, gender income inequality results in women receiving lower pensions and living below the poverty line. because of their precarious economic situation, they cannot afford to pay for their health care, including prevention of illness or medical treatment. women are more exposed to chronic and disabling diseases that alter their quality of life. the main causes of death among older women are cardiovascular, respiratory and cancer. unfortunately, in many cases, access to health care is not as smooth as it should be. there's a long waiting list for the specialist and the diagnostic tests. either the patient gets there too late, or the long wait means he never gets there. in many cases, the quality of healthcare and information campaigns on prevention, treatment options and treatment of specific diseases are inadequate. i support initiatives aimed at more effective disease prevention and improving the health of the elderly. it is important that people become aware of what they can do to prevent disease in their own interests, including the importance of proper nutrition and exercise.
in writing. − prevention and early diagnosis extend life expectancy and contribute to reducing healthcare costs. preventive measures should therefore be a priority of health care. particular attention must be paid to people living in regions, and in particular in rural areas, where healthcare is less accessible than in urban areas, as well as to disadvantaged groups who often lack access to adequate healthcare. for example, women approaching menopause should have access to mammography screening, which could reduce the mortality rate of women with breast cancer by up to 30%. i believe that the eu and its member states must systematically increase the health literacy of their citizens so that they can make informed decisions and actively prevent disease themselves. awareness raising should address the most common diseases, for example through public campaigns in the media focusing on prevention, early diagnosis and treatment.
in writing. − despite the fact that women live longer than men, their health is much worse than that of men of the same age. whether it is musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, respiratory, diabetes, or cancer, women are the clear victims of age-related diseases. our task is therefore to propose a series of measures at national and european level to ensure that women live a full and dignified life in old age. the year 2012 was dedicated to the elderly. active ageing and intergenerational solidarity were the slogans that were supposed to draw the public's attention to the needs and shortcomings of the older generation. health is the most important premise, without which it is impossible to speak of the values that underlie significant active ageing. only a healthy person can actively participate in society, continue to educate himself or herself, or participate in intergenerational exchanges of knowledge or experiences acquired during life. i believe that the measures proposed will also help women to overcome the crisis of old age and reduce the number of elderly women suffering from depression or loss of self-esteem. it is also necessary to bear in mind that with the ever-increasing retirement age, older people are constantly exposed to the need to maintain a stable state of health. it is not without reason that the saying is true: "in a healthy body, a healthy spirit".
in writing. − the health of citizens is the greatest value and source of wealth of any society, which must be protected and developed. i welcome all the procedures and results that have been achieved so far within the union and the member states in line with the document entitled 'health for all in the 21st century' adopted by the world health organisation. i fully endorse the report on the prevention of age-related diseases in women, which is why i voted for it. this does not mean, however, that we can be satisfied with the current state of and access to preventive health care and medical care. it is well known that women use healthcare more often than men. however, women's health is determined by some specific factors that differentiate them from men. however, despite this fact, equality and solidarity of citizens must be the fundamental principles of the union in health protection and the provision of health and medical care. i expect that the resolutions adopted on the prevention of age-related diseases in women will be incorporated in the most concrete ways possible into the health development programmes and activities of each member state, region, because prevention is better than cure, because where there is no health, there is no everything.
in writing. − the eu population is ageing. people are living longer and longer. programmes initiated within the eu aim to promote healthy ageing, mainly through access to quality healthcare and preventive measures. the better these facilities are, the longer the elderly will be able to remain independent. this report focuses on women, taking into account the fact that women are more represented among the elderly. the second factor is that each sex is subject to specific diseases and health risks that need to be taken into account in studies and subsequent health policies. among the diseases that primarily affect older women are cardiovascular and respiratory diseases and cancer, which is the most common cause of death in older women. the report also mentions other diseases, such as dementia, alzheimer's disease, and depression. it is regrettable that 97% of the health budget is allocated to the treatment of noncommunicable diseases and only 3% is allocated to prevention. the rapporteur rightly points out that the cost of treating the consequences is substantially higher than that of prevention. it calls on member states to include more preventive measures in their health budgets in the future. prevention should include training in how to eat healthier, how to incorporate exercise into a sedentary lifestyle, and so on.
in writing. − the discovery of antimicrobials has led to a significant reduction in mortality rates for a number of serious and often fatal bacterial infections and has enabled innovative invasive surgical procedures that are now widely used. but this extraordinary medical progress is gradually being threatened by the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance. the list of multidrug-resistant infections is long and includes, among others, urinary tract infections, pneumonia and tuberculosis. not only are the costs of the drugs needed to treat cases of resistance often high, but the treatment itself is longer and more complex. in the coming years, we can expect a considerable increase in these figures. moreover, modern medical practices accelerate the development of drug-resistant organisms, mainly through improper use, including overdosing and irresponsible use and failure to complete the course of treatment as prescribed by the doctor. the consequences are alarming. antimicrobials, which require tens of millions of eur in science and research and take almost a decade to bring to market, tend to have an increasingly shorter lifespan during which they are effective. according to the who, there is a threat that we will enter a 'pre-antibiotic era' because of antimicrobial resistance. this is a global problem that needs to be addressed responsibly. i am therefore convinced that the union must act vigorously and decisively in this matter.
in writing. − antimicrobial resistance is the ability of microbial organisms to thrive and survive in the presence of antimicrobials, usually at a sufficient dose to suppress or kill microorganisms of the same species. since the discovery of penicillin in 1930, antimicrobials have revolutionized human and veterinary medicine, leading to a significant reduction in mortality rates for a number of serious and often fatal bacterial infections, and paving the way for innovative invasive surgeries used on a large scale. however, the extraordinary medical advances of the antibiotic era are gradually being threatened by the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance. according to the world health organisation (who), there are at least 440 000 individual cases of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis worldwide, resulting in more than 150 000 deaths per year. too much use has caused antimicrobials to lose their effectiveness and bacteria to become resistant to them, so that, for example, drugs for disease do not work. it is therefore necessary to start using them more carefully in both human and veterinary medicine, and we have also used natural remedies for diseases.
in writing. − last year, the european parliament addressed the issue of bacterial resistance in animals due to overuse of antibiotics. the resolution aimed to monitor the emergence of resistant bacteria and prevent the sale of affected products. i'm glad that in a year, we've moved from monitoring to the root of the problem. and the reason is that antibiotics are given to animals as a preventative measure to make more money. i support the classification of medicated feedingstuffs as 'medicines' and not as 'feedingstuffs'. the administration of such feedingstuffs would be subject to medical prescription. as a doctor, i'm aware of the dangers of giving antibiotics as a precaution. we're creating resistant bacteria that no treatment can cure. animal products then pass through to humans. i also support prevention and awareness-raising among the union's population and the prescription-only initiative. self-treatment of viral diseases with antibiotics, which is unnecessary and increases bacterial resistance, should be avoided. it is also important to explain to people that they should follow the dosage prescribed by their doctor and not stop treatment on their own. i expect the commission to monitor developments in this area and to report on the application of the adopted rules.
the daphne and erasmus programmes are very important. daphne helps to combat violence against women, adolescents and children in the union. this is especially important in times of economic crisis. the results of the daphne programme are undeniable, as is its impact on policy change in the member states. erasmus is the best investment in building a united europe, because it gives thousands of young people the opportunity to get to know other member states, their culture and language, while receiving a quality education. i am therefore very pleased that parliament insists on maintaining the funding of both programmes at the original level. i also want to say that i reject the budgetary populism of some member states which does not address the real problem of excessive public expenditure in the european union.
in writing. in the 2013 budget, the council is adamant that the level of payments is eur 5 billion below the needs estimates made by the commission. this level of appropriations will not be sufficient to cover the actual payment needs in the following year. the costs of non-agreement would have much more serious consequences and a much more negative impact on the implementation of union actions and programmes. that's why i'm voting for a compromise budget. the commission shall submit monthly reports to the parliament and the council on the development of member states' applications for each member state and fund. in the event of a shortage of resources, member states must provide the union with the necessary additional resources for the following year to enable it to pay its bills and maintain its credibility and solvency. all these problems show that the only way out of this impasse, which makes budgetary negotiations more difficult every year, is to resolve the question of union financing quickly and responsibly through a genuine system of own resources, which should come into effect from the new multiannual financial framework and which would eliminate forever the eu's division into net contributors and net beneficiaries.
the financial transaction tax was to be a significant own resource of the budget of the european union. it will not, because the enhanced cooperation method has been chosen in the face of opposition from some member states. the swedish experience tells us clearly what happens next. most trading on exchanges in the states that sign up to this cooperation will end. they're moving elsewhere, probably to london. we're replacing the political courage needed to refuse to finance the banks' losses with an absurd gesture. it's like we're telling the citizens: "the banks have behaved like irresponsible players, so now we're going to tax their business, and you're going to pay the tax in the end". and that, unfortunately, i cannot agree with.

- at a time of economic and social crisis, when the report on fundamental rights in the european union is intended to be proof that the european parliament, although it cannot ensure that the wages of states. article 2 of the treaty on european union establishes the union as a community of indivisible and universal values in human dignity, freedom, democracy, gender equality, non-discrimination, solidarity, the rule of law and respect for human rights and civil liberties for all persons residing in the territory of the european union, including persons belonging to minorities, stateless european union and for the full preservation of member states' rights. with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, on the basis of well as on the member states when they implement the law of the european union. the charter has transformed values and principles into tangible and enforceable rights. the effective protection and fulfil rights does not require new competences for the european union, but rather proactive institutional commitment in the field of human rights, a genuine culture of fundamental rights needs to be fundamental rights actors within the structure of the european union. ladies and gentlemen, citizens can only enjoy their rights fully if fundamental values and principles such as the rule of law, the independence of the judiciary, media freedom and non-discrimination are respected. however, the gap between fundamental rights and their implementation weakens the credibility of the european union and its member states. the effective protection and promotion of fundamental rights require that member states, in a spirit of solidarity and sincere cooperation with other member states, accept the control of the european union's respect for the values of the european union in legislative policies and practice. the commission shall adopt implementing acts. article 2 of the treaty on european union gives the institutions of the european union the power to assess whether there is a breach in the member states of common values such as respect for human rights, democracy and the rule of law. it also allows for political intervention in the countries concerned to prevent and remedy such breaches. it is therefore our duty to demand that these objectives be implemented. the current economic and social crisis, and in particular its effects, threaten the principle of solidarity, which is an important part of the history and identity of the european union, and the fundamental bond that binds the citizens of the european union together as members of one political community. i therefore ask you, even in this debate, despite the late hour, to support this very important report as a message to the citizens of the member states of the european union in the vote tomorrow.
the draft resolution on the situation of fundamental rights in the european union for 2010-11, submitted to the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, contains a wide range of proposals and recommendations for the commission, the council and the member states. in addition to general recommendations, ms monika flašíková-beňová's report also focused on recommendations aimed at eliminating discrimination from our society, protecting individuals belonging to minority groups, access to equal opportunities regardless of age, gender or disability, the problems of migrants and refugees, protecting the rights of children or victims of crime, with an emphasis on improving access to justice, as well as the general status of citizens in the union and the handling of their data by the institution. perhaps it is the breadth and detail of the proposed resolution which, in view of the different cultural and civilizational traditions of the european peoples, creates some room for polemic over certain formulations. although the report presented is based entirely on existing european legislation on fundamental rights, each of us will be able to decide for ourselves in the end to what extent it conforms to the proposed text of the resolution as a whole.
i have some important comments to make on mrs flaschek-bein's report. ms flašíková-beňová is calling into question the independence of the judiciary, seeking to interfere with the competences of nation states and introducing rights that cannot be considered fundamental even with the best of intentions. the application of human rights is the competence of the courts. the so-called interim evaluation of the judiciary would lead to the marking of judicial decisions by non-profit organisations and other institutions. i'm asking, on what grounds? only on the basis of their own interpretation of the law. the rapporteur is proud that her report addresses for the first time the topics of reproductive health, sexual education, planned parenthood and the application of legal abortion legislation. but these issues are the exclusive competence of the member states. the fundamental rights agenda of the european union does not include the requirement to introduce same-sex marriage. and the right to euthanasia is neither a fundamental, nor a european, nor a universal human right. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which is mentioned here repeatedly, does not contain these rights. on the contrary, my proposal to include a paragraph on poverty as an obstacle to the enjoyment of fundamental rights in the report was rejected by the rapporteur. let me conclude with one final remark. in the media, the reporter did not hesitate to label people as bigots and backward just because they are catholics and do not share her views. her report calls for the prosecution of hate speech. if she's serious, she should change her vocabulary or risk prosecution herself. in writing. − ground handling services consist of all ground aviation-related activities carried out for individual airlines at airports and are a key function in the air transport chain. the efficient provision of ground handling services is important for airports, airlines and passengers and is key to the efficient use of air transport infrastructure and the performance of the aviation system in general. the european union's single european sky initiative, which aims to reform the architecture of european air traffic management to meet future capacity and safety needs, recognises the importance of integrating key infrastructure such as airports into the whole system from take-off to landing (gate-to-gate). the general objective that we should strive to achieve, amongst others, is to increase the efficiency and overall quality of ground handling services for users and end-users at eu airports.
in writing. − if you have at aerodromes where the demand of airlines for operating intervals for take-off and landing exceeds the capacity of the aerodrome, the mechanisms for allocating operating intervals shall be used to define a set of rules to be followed for this purpose. depending on the characteristics of the airport, it may be necessary to allocate operating intervals to a certain time of the day or to certain periods of increased passenger demand. the objective is to ensure that access to congested airports is organised according to fair, non-discriminatory and transparent rules for the allocation of operating intervals for take-off and landing, thereby allowing for the optimal use of airport capacity and fair conditions of competition. the implementation of the schedule regulation has significantly improved the allocation of slots at congested european airports in terms of the neutrality and transparency of the allocation process. the commission therefore concludes that the aid granted to bsca does not constitute state aid within the meaning of article 107 (1) of the treaty. the schedule regulation was introduced at a time when the european air transport market was still dominated by a small number of traditional national airlines. today, however, competition is much more intense. i consider it justified to revise the interval regulation and to determine to what extent it can be improved in terms of capacity compliance with air transport demand in all segments.
in writing. − the proposal aims to update existing measures to enable local authorities to address noise reduction around union airports within the international framework of the international civil aviation organisation (icao) 's balanced approach to noise regulation. the balanced approach needs to be applied consistently. at icao level, the eu is actively supporting the development of new noise standards for aircraft and investing in new technologies through the framework programmes and the clean sky project. however, land use planning, together with related isolation and compensation programmes, is a national or local competence. operating procedures are the responsibility of the relevant aerodrome and air traffic services providers and are subject to single european sky legislation. the issue of noise standards is also addressed by another piece of european legislation the environmental noise directive, which commits member states to identify the main sources of environmental noise, to measure the impact of noise and to take appropriate measures. the proposal would complement directive 2002/49/ec in that it provides for a procedure for the development of a noise action plan consisting of cost-effective measures to reduce noise related to air traffic.
