in writing. − animal welfare in the 21st century is an expression of humanity and an issue that must be addressed by european civilization and culture, as any action to protect and ensure the welfare of animals must be based on scientific knowledge as well as on the principle that animals are sentient beings whose special needs must be taken into account, as laid down in article 13 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. eu animal welfare legislation must not lead to distortions of free trade in goods or disproportionate financial costs, while taking into account the specific disadvantaged geographical situation of peripheral and outermost regions. transport time constraints and overly restrictive conditions may jeopardise the regular supply of the market in certain countries and peripheral regions within the eu, with the result that some companies become economically unviable, with all the consequences associated with this loss of competitiveness. i believe that the conditions for the transport of animals should clearly be in the best interests of all. i also believe that the appropriate education and training of hauliers and transporters is essential for the proper treatment of animals, thus laying the foundations for the protection and welfare of animals.
in writing. − transporting animals over long distances in unhygienic and unfavourable conditions increases the risk of spreading infection and disease and directly affects the quality of meat products. i therefore agree that animals should be slaughtered as close as possible to their place of production, which would reduce the unnecessary stress and costs associated with their complex and painful transport. consumers could thus enjoy fresh meat from animals that have been reared in the region. food chains and meat producers that prefer to offer locally produced meat would thus also contribute to the development of their region. in this respect, however, we must ensure that eu hygiene legislation does not place an unnecessary administrative burden on small regional slaughter and processing establishments. at european union level, we need to adopt policies and legal instruments facilitating the creation of short supply chains to avoid the unreasonably long transport of live animals for the sole purpose of slaughter.
in writing. − since 1977, the european union has had rules governing animal welfare during transport, aimed at removing technical barriers to trade while ensuring an adequate level of animal protection. article 32 of the regulation requires the commission to submit to the european parliament, within four years of the date of entry into force of the regulation, a report on the impact of this regulation on the living conditions of transported animals and on trade flows in live animals within the enlarged community. the rapporteur welcomes the commission's report providing information on the implementation of the regulation, although he considers that the report does not contain a full assessment of the transport of animals in terms of all economic, social and environmental costs. one of the biggest problems in transporting live animals is the maximum time allowed for transport. parliament adopted a written declaration calling for a maximum transport time of 8 hours. the situation is such that one third of live animal transports take 8 hours or more. determining whether 8 hours is the right maximum transport time is also very difficult due to incomplete scientific evidence. however, to increase the protection of animals during transport, it is necessary to reduce this time and at the same time increase the penalties for violators. logical steps include supporting local slaughterhouses, which will help to minimise long-term transport.
in writing. - i am pleased that the report includes several articles on national minorities. the protection of national minorities is essential for the proper functioning of the union. the protection of minorities is an integral part of fundamental human rights. effective protection requires institutional commitment. although the protection of national minorities was included in mrs flašíková-beňová's report, i had to vote against the report because it contains several articles which i do not find acceptable. unfortunately, the report contains passages that go beyond the union's competence and impose on the union tasks that are unacceptable and unrealistic. the annual report on fundamental human rights must not become a battleground for political interests and ideologies. it should present an objective picture of the situation, drawing the attention of the member states and the union institutions to the shortcomings and formulating concrete proposals for solutions and realistic expectations to be addressed in the next annual report. this year's report does not do so and therefore, despite its positive wording, it cannot be supported.
in writing. − article 2 of the treaty on european union establishes the union as a community of indivisible and universal values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, gender equality, non-discrimination, solidarity, the rule of law and respect for human rights and civil liberties for all persons living in the territory of the eu, including persons belonging to minorities, stateless persons and persons temporarily or illegally present in the territory of the european union. all these values are common to the member states in a society that promotes pluralism, non-discrimination, tolerance, justice and equality between women and men. i consider it necessary and important to develop and strengthen a genuine culture of fundamental rights in the institutions of the union and in the member states. the union must promote a coherent eu human rights policy and a mechanism that brings together the various fundamental rights actors within the eu structure. it is clear that citizens can only enjoy their rights fully if fundamental values and principles such as the rule of law, the independence of the judiciary, media freedom and non-discrimination are respected. i believe that for the effective protection and promotion of fundamental rights it is important that member states, in a spirit of solidarity and sincere cooperation with other member states, adopt the eu's control of respect for eu values in legislative policies and in practice.
in writing. − the charter of fundamental rights of the european union clearly states that the right to marry and the right to found a family are guaranteed in accordance with national laws. member states therefore have the sovereign right to decide on the basis of their own cultural values and traditions. however, the report on fundamental rights in the european union does not respect such provisions of the charter and even deliberately exceeds the scope of the eu's competences. i cannot agree with many aspects of the report in particular, or with the whole of it, but i will concentrate on a few of the most important in my explanation of vote. the choice of two different instruments and a separate approach for so-called registered partnerships and marriages justified by the very nature of marriage, which is the union of a man and a woman. marriage, which is the foundation of the family and the space for the healthy upbringing of children, deserves special, privileged protection by society, especially in the field of law. for it is undeniable that the family in which children are born and raised is the foundation of any healthy and prosperous society. the attempt to establish an equal approach to two biologically, socially and psychologically different realities is therefore completely unjustified. as regards sexual and reproductive health services, in particular so-called safe and legal abortion, i must reiterate that the charter of human rights and other human rights instruments clearly establish the right to life and respect for the physical and mental integrity of the human being. for the reasons stated above, i shall vote against the report.
in writing. − since 1993, the european parliament has been actively involved in the observance of fundamental human rights in the individual member states. however, the european convention on human rights of 1977 already sets out the obligations of the european institutions to respect fundamental rights. the charter of fundamental rights, which became a primary law with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon and thus binding on the european institutions as well as the eu member states, has brought about a significant advance in the perception of human rights. the charter therefore has the same legal binding force as any eu treaty and is legally enforceable. the treaty of lisbon further strengthened the powers of the european parliament. the report on the respect of fundamental human rights in the eu thus gains in importance. it focuses on a number of areas not covered by previous reports. i welcome the focus on reproductive health and the call to member states to allow women to decide for themselves about their reproductive rights. i also support the rapporteur's proposal to the european commission to monitor compliance with legislation on this issue. among other areas, i particularly support the section on youth employment policy and believe that initiatives such as the youth guarantee will help us win the multiannual fight against unemployment in the coming years, in the midst of the ongoing economic crisis.

the situation in ukraine has been politically polarised for a long time. however, we cannot determine what the political composition of the representative bodies of ukraine will be. so we should communicate and cooperate with that representation that came out of free elections, even if we have a very difficult time dealing with it. we should also maintain close cooperation with all decent political forces in ukraine that respect freedom and democracy. the suspension of dialogue or postponement of cooperation under the association agreement may mean that ukraine will seek its future in closer cooperation with its eastern neighbours, which will certainly not improve the prospects of its people for a free and democratic future. so i think we have to be patient and a little generous. i am convinced that ukrainian citizens will also gradually be able to choose better and more trustworthy politicians. and if we allow them to travel openly in europe, their demands for the integrity of politicians will surely increase more quickly.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, this is a watershed moment in eu-ukraine relations. on the table is an unsigned association agreement, a document that has the potential to transform ukraine's economy and society. i understand the disappointment of my colleagues, as well as of several leaders of member states, at the imperfection of ukrainian democracy and the selective and politically motivated use of the judiciary. it is clear that the october parliamentary elections were not fully in line with eu standards either. however, freezing bilateral relations and postponing the signing of the association agreement indefinitely will not bring any positive results. he is a member of the 'people's council' of the so-called 'donetsk people's republic'. on the contrary, it will isolate ukraine, resulting in a second belarus on our borders. this would, among other things, mean the de facto end of the eastern partnership as a meaningful initiative. at this point, it is necessary to define clear and enforceable conditions for the ukrainian government in the areas of judiciary, electoral legislation and constitutional reforms so that the agreement can be signed at the next eastern partnership summit in vilnius. i am glad that this is the approach that the foreign ministers adopted at the last council meeting. many reproach the union for lacking a strategic dimension in its foreign policy for failing to clearly define and pursue its interests. the signing of an association agreement with ukraine is clearly in our strategic interest and has the added advantage of being of enormous benefit to ukraine itself.
on behalf of the ppe group. – madam president, we welcome this report and congratulate the rapporteur. we also congratulate the albanians on their achievements, and would like to encourage them to build on them. the commission gave a strong positive signal to albania in its last progress report by recommending candidate country status for albania, subject to the fulfilment of three remaining conditions. we believe that this should become a driving force for albania in its progress towards european integration, and i think that this is crucial to the process for the following reasons. first, the eu agenda must not divide politicians in albania and should not be treated as a bargaining chip in terms of internal politics. it needs to be a unifying factor. the report appreciates the efforts made so far, but it is also worth mentioning that political dialogue and political cooperation on the eu agenda cannot be selective, but needs to be solidly based within the system. there are still some concerns around this. second, the eu has been very clear and explicit as regards its expectations of albania. we agreed on key priorities which need to be fulfilled before the next steps in the process. the credibility of this process should be based on fair and rigorous conditionality. we should expect fulfilment of what was agreed on. finally, albania still has a good chance in the near future of progressing towards the eu. after a long time, we now have encouraging reports, but an important check in this respect is still to come. the elections offer a great opportunity to show how firmly politicians and mechanisms are rooted in democratic values.
the european union is founded on universal values such as human rights and freedoms and actively contributes to their preservation and development. in order to respect human rights, which have become a common and shared value for all eu member states, the fundamental rights agency was also established to deal with the human rights situation in the 27 eu countries. i would like to support the ideas expressed by the rapporteur, mr pirker, that on the one hand we have an agency, but it must work better. it must not spend two-thirds of its budget on administration alone and not use it for what it was set up to do. the eu agency for fundamental rights is to fulfil its tasks exclusively in the thematic areas identified in the multiannual financial framework and therefore the multiannual framework for the agency for the years 2013 to 2017 should be carefully formulated taking into account the new eu rights and obligations arising from the lisbon treaty. in my view, the rights of persons with disabilities, which i stress, derive from the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, which the eu ratified in january 2011, should be explicitly included in the work of the agency. this document ensures that people with disabilities can enjoy their rights on an equal basis with all other citizens. i am also in favour of the idea of including new thematic areas such as police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the multiannual framework, as they are already covered by the scope of the agency's remit. in conclusion, i would like to say that the functioning and focus of the agency must reflect the overall changes in eu legislation. the agency's activities in the new thematic areas will thus contribute to the thorough protection of fundamental rights in the european union.
i supported the alternative report by the european people's party, but voted against the report by mrs flašíková-bňová. the report does not benefit the european parliament, the european union or any of its citizens who suffer from the lack of respect for fundamental human rights. the report redefines basic human rights. it proposes new fundamental rights that upset the delicate balance between the common good and the interests of hard-to-defined minorities. the resolution proposes a new institutional architecture that undermines the fundamental principle of separation of powers. it may happen that the violation of fundamental rights is judged by ngo activists rather than by the judiciary. the european parliament has often strongly criticised the polarization of the judiciary in banana republics. however, this report brings polarization to the judiciary in the european union.
i did not vote for the multiannual programme of the fundamental rights agency. as the commissioner explained this morning in the plenary, the responsibilities of this agency are not clearly defined by the member states. until the skills are fixed, we should not be doing this alone. the lack of unanimity is due to the overly political nature of the fundamental rights agency. within the union itself, an agency wishes to intervene in regulatory responsibilities which belong to the competent authorities of the member states. it is the responsibility of national courts and, ultimately, of the judges of the european court of human rights and the european court of justice to find a violation of human rights. the politicization of fundamental rights is certainly not an appropriate strategy.
i have been a human rights campaigner for a long time and i regret that i could not support this report. i'm sorry that one of the rights being upheld is the right to abortion. let's call it what it is. the report deplores the fact that in some countries obstacles are being put in the way of abortion. i think that life is always a better choice than death, and therefore the issue of abortion should not be taken as a fundamental right. on the one hand, we defend the rights of the child and we talk about the vulnerability of the child, but on the other hand, we talk about the right to kill the unborn child before it is born. the report also highlights religious tolerance. it states that religion cannot be used to oppress or restrict other religions. however, the exact opposite was also seen in the european union's first reaction to the proposal for a commemorative two-euro coin with the portraits of saints cyril and methodius from slovakia.
the palestinian president has asked for the recognition of palestine as an observer state. of the old eu member states, only germany, the netherlands and the united kingdom abstained. the next day, the head of the hamas politburo repeated that he would never accept the existence of a jewish state. from the rostrum, he declared that the only way is jihad and violence. one would expect this parliament to respond with a resolution strongly calling on the palestinian leaders to return to the negotiating table, and in this context to condemn the irresponsible foreign policies of some eu member states and to express its disapproval of the plan to build new jewish settlements. but it didn't happen that way. excuse me, but we're going to criticize israel. i could not support such a resolution.
in writing. − on 15 february 2007, the council adopted regulation (ec) no 168/2007 establishing the european union agency for fundamental rights, which started its work on 1 march 2007. the multiannual financial framework is not a work programme. the agency's work programmes shall be approved each year by its management board within the thematic areas identified in the multiannual financial framework. at the request of the european parliament, the council or the commission, the agency may also carry out activities outside those thematic areas, provided that its financial and human resources so permit. the current multiannual framework (2007 2012) will expire at the end of 2012. it is therefore necessary to establish a multiannual framework for the agency for the years 2013 to 2017. for the period in question, the council proposed, among others, areas such as access to justice, victims of crime, including compensation for victims of crime, the information society, in particular respect for private life and the protection of personal data, roma integration, the rights of the child, etc. i believe that the scope of the agency's work should explicitly include social rights and a specific role in relation to the independent monitoring of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. it is appropriate that the commission reviews and proposes to review the agency's tasks, areas of competence and working methods in 2013 in order to guarantee the effective monitoring and implementation of the charter of fundamental rights.
in writing. − over the years, parliament has considerably extended its powers, thus securing important instruments that allow it to influence the decision-making process of the european union in most of the union's activities. institutions to which a written statement is addressed should ensure that it is followed up properly. such written statements serve as a useful tool for raising issues of particular concern to citizens of the union. they have minimal influence in setting the programme and in influencing decisions taken by the institutions, and therefore may give rise to misconceptions about their effectiveness. however, if used correctly, they can retain their relevance as a popular tool for promoting proposals. when it comes to proposals calling for the adoption of a legislative measure, rule 42 (2) should apply, which gives individual members a real opportunity to influence union legislation and to include the proposal in the work of parliament's committees. as the quality and significance of some written statements may appear unsatisfactory, i believe that parliament could, in the next parliamentary term, assess the impact of the new provisions of its rules of procedure relating to written statements and their effectiveness.
in writing. − the treaties commit the european union to base its external action on the principles of democracy, the rule of law, the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms, the preservation of human dignity, the principles of equality and solidarity, and respect for the principles of the united nations charter and international law. justice, the rule of law, accountability for all crimes, including the most serious crimes of concern to the international community, fair trials and an independent judiciary are indispensable aspects of the protection of human rights and pillars of a lasting peace. democracy and the rule of law are the best safeguards of human rights and fundamental freedoms, of non-discrimination in all its forms and of tolerance towards individuals and communities, and of equality for all. while the positive steps taken in the preparation of the annual report in recent years are welcome, i think it is also fair to say that, as a rule, there is always room for further improvement. the annual report should be an important tool for informing about eu action in this area and should help to improve the visibility of eu actions.
in writing. − the european union is founded on the principle of respect for human rights and has a legal obligation under its treaties to place human rights at the centre of all its policies and those of the member states without exception, and at the centre of all international agreements. dialogues between the eu, its member states and third countries must be followed by concrete measures designed to ensure that human rights remain at the heart of these policies. however, the current economic crisis has also shown, among other things, that grandiose pronouncements on human rights issues are insufficient if they are not accompanied by a policy of human rights principles, implemented through rapid and concrete measures and based on the obligation to respect the coherence and unity of the internal and external dimension of all eu policies. the promotion of human rights and democracy is a shared responsibility of the eu and its member states. i am convinced that progress in this area can only be achieved through coordinated and coherent action by both sides. the broad scope and main elements of the eu's new strategic framework on human rights and democracy require a high degree of unity and political will to achieve the concrete results that are desired.
in writing. − the eu's evolving common foreign and security policy, as well as its energy policy, should include russia as a strategic partner, in accordance with the principle of conditionality, provided that it also applies and promotes the fundamental values on which the union is founded, including democracy, the rule of law, the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity, the principles of equal treatment and solidarity, and compliance with the principles laid down in the un charter and international law. russia is a country with cultural roots in europe and, as a member of the un security council, the g8 and g20, the council of europe and the osce, an important global and regional player, and must therefore fulfil the obligations of membership in those organisations. however, under the leadership of president vladimir putin, russia has shown only a selective interest in the formulation of common policies and no real intention to create a genuine and comprehensive strategic partnership for the application of international law and conflict prevention. i consider it important that the union remains committed to further deepening and developing its relations with this country and to upholding the principles enshrined in the partnership for modernisation, which are based on common interests and a deep commitment to common values, democratic principles, respect for fundamental human rights and the rule of law.
in writing. − ukraine was identified during the eu-ukraine summit in 2011 in kiev as a european country with a european identity, sharing a common history and common values with the countries of the european union. the summit, which was to have resulted in the signing of an association agreement, did not meet its objectives, however, as the eu was concerned about the political situation in ukraine, in particular with regard to the arrest and prosecution of leading opposition figures yulia tymoshenko and yuri luzhenko. the european union further reaffirms its commitment to political association and economic integration with ukraine. i am convinced that to ensure strengthened relations between them, swift and decisive action by the government and all other relevant state bodies in ukraine is necessary to consolidate the democratic legitimacy of the country. effective cooperation between ukraine and the european union can only be implemented on the basis of a clear willingness of the ukrainian authorities to undertake the necessary reforms, in particular in the legal system and the judiciary, in order to start fully implementing the principles of democracy, protecting human rights, fundamental freedoms and minority rights, and respecting the rule of law.
in writing. − the future of albania and the other western balkan countries is linked to the european union. albania too belongs to europe geographically, historically and culturally. the country's accession to the eu should not be the goal of the government and the opposition, but should be in the common interest of all albanians. the candidate countries must demonstrate their capacity to strengthen the practical implementation of the values on which the eu is founded at all stages of the accession process. they must establish and support from the outset the proper functioning of the main institutions necessary for democratic governance and respect for the rule of law, from national parliaments, through the government and the judiciary, including courts and prosecutors, to law enforcement. i am of the opinion that albania, thanks to its reform efforts to date, and if the citizens of this country so wish, can progress in 2012 to the next stage of the accession process to obtain the status of candidate country for accession, if it achieves sufficient concrete results in the areas where key reforms are desirable and necessary.
in writing. − steel is crucial to the eu economy and to the development and competitiveness of several important downstream sectors, such as the automotive and engineering industries. in the recent period, it has faced considerable difficulties such as a significant drop in demand, strong competition from third countries, complicated access to raw materials and increased costs, which led to restructuring, mergers and job losses. i believe that one of our priorities should be to seek and adopt measures to prevent the threat of relocation of steel undertakings outside the european union. the commission's initiative to develop a european steel action plan by june 2013 is welcomed, but should be submitted as soon as possible. such an action plan should also take into account ways of addressing and mitigating the high energy and raw material costs that threaten the competitiveness of the steel industry. energy efficiency and resource efficiency can contribute to significant cost savings and in this context it is necessary that the commission and the steel industry itself continue to examine the options available for concrete steps to achieve cost savings. at the same time, successful restructuring cannot be achieved without a strong and responsible social dialogue.
in writing. − the petitioners have strongly expressed their concern about the extremely high level of dioxin emissions from the ilva steel plant in taranto, which has had and continues to have harmful and lasting effects on the health of the local population. up to 20,000 families have members who worked in or were involved with the steel industry, and pollution levels among the local population have led to unacceptable and intolerable levels of disease and chronic illness. the fragile and dangerous situation of ilva steel also causes serious environmental degradation and damage, as well as serious social and economic problems in the south of italy. unfortunately, neither the privatisation of this steel plant has led to any improvement in the overall situation nor in the environmental safety of the sector. overall, the steel industry, which employs some 360 000 people, is a key economic sector in the european union. i believe that parliament has a duty and a responsibility to show clearly its solidarity with the workers of ilva steel and their families who have been affected by this absolutely unacceptable situation. i believe that the necessary effort must be made to link economic objectives with social and environmental priorities in order to build a modern, competitive and sustainable european steel industry that is fully in line with european union environmental legislation.
for the efd group. i am convinced that the main cause of the ongoing conflicts in the east of the democratic republic of congo is the struggle for control over the exploitation of the natural resources in the area. if the congolese government does not have the authority and the necessary military force to maintain law and order in the country, adventurers of all kinds will always try to take advantage of this situation and by causing all kinds of unrest and conflict, create a path to the mineral wealth of the country. the local population is simply a victim of the commercial interests of various mining companies, which create conditions for the exploitation of mineral wealth from behind the scenes through armed gangs. therefore, i think that in addition to the standard measures we apply in similar cases, aimed at consolidating and stabilising the social and political environment of the country, we should also promote measures to protect against the illegal exploitation of natural resources and the trade in raw materials thus acquired. following the example of the dodd-frank act passed by the united states congress, we should be enforcing strict measures to better trace minerals that come from illegal mining, including more rigorous control of the international natural resources market. identifying and subsequently seizing illicitly extracted raw materials will discourage adventurous mineral conquerors from artificially inciting ethnic conflicts and funding armed gangs.
mr president, i am very much concerned about the humanitarian crisis and the many serious human rights violations which are going on in congo. we must condemn mass rape, torture, massacres of civilians and the enrolment of child soldiers. the non-prosecution of those responsible for human rights violations and war crimes promotes the climate of impunity and encourages the perpetration of fresh crimes. the eu has its role to play in this situation. we need to ensure our contribution to the restoration of justice and security in the country and secure the continuity of the military assistance mission and the police assistance mission. it is extremely important to find a solution which will secure respect for human rights and bring peace, security and stability to the region.
for the efd group. the battle against centuries of custom is complex and long- drawn out in every society. the caste system in india is apparently still very much in place. nevertheless, i think we must use the full authority of the european parliament to work with the indian administration to speed up the eradication of the inhuman manifestations of caste discrimination from indian society. in particular, women from the dalit and adivasi communities are often subjected to degrading treatment and unacceptable discrimination. often they are forced to do hard or disgusting work and are often the targets of impunity for sexual abuse by members of the ruling caste. evidence of these practices was also seen in the recent gang rape of a 16-year-old girl in the village of dabra. therefore, ladies and gentlemen, we must ask the indian state authorities to enforce the law on the lowest registered castes and registered tribes under the protection of the government more vigorously so that members of any caste or community in india are not subjected to violence, humiliation and discrimination. the responsibility for protecting the human rights of the people of india rests entirely with the indian state bodies and institutions. that's why we have to direct our criticism there.
